questions.knowledgeNote: Improper fraction: write the numerator as (x-3) + 6 so the division is exact up to a log term.
questions.question: Q3(vii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (x + 3)/(x - 3) dx. (T.U. 2049 H)
questions.solution: Divide out: (x + 3)/(x - 3) = (x - 3 + 6)/(x - 3) = 1 + 6/(x - 3). Integrate: x + 6 log(x - 3) + c. Check: d/dx = 1 + 6/(x-3) = (x-3+6)/(x-3) = (x+3)/(x-3). Boxed (printed key p571).

questions.question: Q3(viii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (3x - 1)/(x - 2) dx.
questions.solution: Divide out: 3x - 1 = 3(x - 2) + 5, so the integrand is 3 + 5/(x - 2). Integrate: 3x + 5 log(x - 2) + c. Check: d/dx = 3 + 5/(x-2) = (3x - 6 + 5)/(x - 2) = (3x - 1)/(x - 2). Boxed (printed key p571).

questions.knowledgeNote: Divide first: the quotient is x + 2 and the remainder 1 gives the log term.
questions.question: Q3(ix). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (x^2 + 3x + 3)/(x + 1) dx.
questions.solution: Polynomial division: (x^2 + 3x + 3) = (x + 1)(x + 2) + 1, so the integrand is x + 2 + 1/(x + 1). Integrate: (1/2)x^2 + 2x + log(x + 1) + c. Check by differentiating: x + 2 + 1/(x+1) = (x^2 + 3x + 3)/(x + 1). Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q3(ix); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Remainder theorem in practice: x^2 + 5 at x = -2 is 9, which is the numerator of the residual fraction.
questions.question: Q3(x). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (x^2 + 5)/(x + 2) dx. (T.U. 2056 S)
questions.solution: Divide: x^2 + 5 = (x + 2)(x - 2) + 9, so the integrand is x - 2 + 9/(x + 2). Integrate: (1/2)x^2 - 2x + 9 log(x + 2) + c. Check: x - 2 + 9/(x+2) = (x^2 - 4 + 9)/(x + 2) = (x^2 + 5)/(x + 2). Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q3(x); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Replace x by y - 1 so the whole integrand becomes a sum of powers of y.
questions.question: Q4(i). Find the indefinite integral: integral of x sqrt(x + 1) dx.
questions.solution: Put y = x + 1, so x = y - 1 and dx = dy. Then integral x sqrt(x+1) dx = integral (y - 1)y^(1/2) dy = integral (y^(3/2) - y^(1/2)) dy = (2/5)y^(5/2) - (2/3)y^(3/2) + c = (2/5)(x+1)^(5/2) - (2/3)(x+1)^(3/2) + c. Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q4(i); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Two factors of 1/a appear: one from dx and one from x = (y-b)/a, hence 1/a^2.
questions.question: Q4(ii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of x sqrt(ax + b) dx.
questions.solution: Put y = ax + b, so x = (y - b)/a, dx = dy/a. Then the integral is (1/a) integral ((y - b)/a) y^(1/2) dy = (1/a^2)[integral y^(3/2) dy - b integral y^(1/2) dy] = (1/a^2)[(2/5)y^(5/2) - (2/3)b y^(3/2)] + c, with y = ax + b. Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q4(ii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The factor 2x is exactly y - 3, which keeps the algebra clean; the 1/2 from dx halves the result.
questions.question: Q4(iii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of 2x sqrt(2x + 3) dx.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q4(iii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Same pattern as Q4(iii) with the inner derivative 5; the 1/5 from dx produces 2/25 and 4/15.
questions.question: Q4(iv). Find the indefinite integral: integral of 5x sqrt(5x + 2) dx. (HSEB 2051)
questions.solution: Put y = 5x + 2, so 5x = y - 2 and dx = dy/5. Then the integral is (1/5) integral (y - 2)y^(1/2) dy = (1/5)[(2/5)y^(5/2) - 2(2/3)y^(3/2)] = (2/25)y^(5/2) - (4/15)y^(3/2) + c, with y = 5x + 2. Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q4(iv); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The substitution turns x + 2 into (y + 4)/3, so both terms are powers of y; factor 2/9 at the end.
questions.question: Q4(v). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (x + 2) sqrt(3x + 2) dx.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q4(v); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: 2x + 3 becomes (2y + 7)/3 after y = 3x + 1; the 1/9 combines with the factors to give 2/9 outside.
questions.question: Q4(vi). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (2x + 3) sqrt(3x + 1) dx. (T.U. 2054)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q4(vi); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The 5 combines with 2/5 to give 2, which is why the outer factor simplifies from 1/16 to 1/8.
questions.question: Q4(vii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (5x + 3) sqrt(4x + 1) dx.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q4(vii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Splitting the numerator is enough: two single powers of y, no product rule needed.
questions.question: Q4(viii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (x + 2)/sqrt(x + 1) dx.
questions.solution: Put y = x + 1, so x + 2 = y + 1 and dx = dy. Then the integral is integral (y + 1)y^(-1/2) dy = integral (y^(1/2) + y^(-1/2)) dy = (2/3)y^(3/2) + 2y^(1/2) + c = (2/3)(x+1)^(3/2) + 2(x+1)^(1/2) + c. Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q4(viii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: 3 * (2/3) = 2 in the first term and 1 * 2 = 2 in the second - both coefficients come out as 2.
questions.question: Q4(ix). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (3x + 4)/sqrt(x + 1) dx.
questions.solution: Put y = x + 1, so 3x + 4 = 3y + 1 and dx = dy. Then the integral is integral (3y + 1)y^(-1/2) dy = 3(2/3)y^(3/2) + 2y^(1/2) = 2y^(3/2) + 2y^(1/2) + c = 2(x+1)^(3/2) + 2(x+1)^(1/2) + c. Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q4(ix); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: After the substitution both terms are single powers; the answer is printed with the factor 2/9 taken out.
questions.question: Q4(x). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (2x + 1)/sqrt(3x + 2) dx.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q4(x); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: For a negative power under a square root, the antiderivative raises the exponent: y^(-3/2) integrates to -2y^(-1/2), and y^(-1/2) to 2y^(1/2).
questions.question: Q4(xi). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (2x + 3)/(3x + 1)^(3/2) dx.
questions.solution: Put y = 3x + 1, so x = (y - 1)/3, 2x + 3 = (2y + 7)/3 and dx = dy/3. Then the integral is (1/9) integral (2y + 7)y^(-3/2) dy. Now integral y * y^(-3/2) dy = integral y^(-1/2) dy = 2y^(1/2) and integral y^(-3/2) dy = -2y^(-1/2). Hence (1/9)[2(2y^(1/2)) + 7(-2y^(-1/2))] = (2/9)[2y^(1/2) - 7y^(-1/2)] + c, with y = 3x + 1. Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q4(xi); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Both coefficients collapse to 2, so the bracket is simply y^(3/2) + y^(1/2) inside the factor 2/25.
questions.question: Q4(xii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (3x + 2)/sqrt(5x + 3) dx. (T.U. 2055 S)
questions.solution: Put y = 5x + 3, so x = (y - 3)/5, 3x + 2 = (3y + 1)/5 and dx = dy/5. Then the integral is (1/25) integral (3y + 1)y^(-1/2) dy = (1/25)[3(2/3)y^(3/2) + 2y^(1/2)] = (2/25)[y^(3/2) + y^(1/2)] + c, with y = 5x + 3. Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q4(xii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The conjugate factor turns the surd denominator into 1; the problem then collapses to two power integrals.
questions.question: Q5(i). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx/[sqrt(x + 1) - sqrt(x)].
questions.solution: Rationalise the denominator: multiply numerator and denominator by sqrt(x + 1) + sqrt(x). The denominator becomes (x + 1) - x = 1, so the integrand is exactly sqrt(x + 1) + sqrt(x). Integrate: (2/3)(x + 1)^(3/2) + (2/3)x^(3/2) + c = (2/3)[(x + 1)^(3/2) + x^(3/2)] + c. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q5(i); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The rationalising factor produces the constant 2a in the denominator, which combines with 2/3 to give 1/(3a).
questions.question: Q5(ii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx/[sqrt(x + a) - sqrt(x - a)].
questions.solution: Multiply by the conjugate sqrt(x + a) + sqrt(x - a); the denominator becomes (x + a) - (x - a) = 2a, a constant. Hence the integral is (1/(2a)) integral [sqrt(x + a) + sqrt(x - a)] dx = (1/(2a))[(2/3)(x + a)^(3/2) + (2/3)(x - a)^(3/2)] + c = (1/(3a))[(x + a)^(3/2) + (x - a)^(3/2)] + c. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q5(ii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Difference of the radicands is 4, so the conjugate leaves 1/4 in front; each surd then contributes 1/3.
questions.question: Q5(iii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx/[sqrt(2x + 1) - sqrt(2x - 3)]. (T.U. 2051 H)
questions.solution: Multiply by sqrt(2x + 1) + sqrt(2x - 3): the denominator becomes (2x + 1) - (2x - 3) = 4. So the integral is (1/4) integral [sqrt(2x + 1) + sqrt(2x - 3)] dx. Now integral sqrt(2x + 1) dx = (1/3)(2x + 1)^(3/2) and integral sqrt(2x - 3) dx = (1/3)(2x - 3)^(3/2) (each inner derivative is 2). Hence (1/4)(1/3)[(2x + 1)^(3/2) + (2x - 3)^(3/2)] + c = (1/12)[(2x + 1)^(3/2) + (2x - 3)^(3/2)] + c. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q5(iii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The general case: the constant left by rationalising is a + b, so the answer carries 2/(3(a+b)).
questions.question: Q5(iv). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx/[sqrt(x + a) - sqrt(x - b)].
questions.solution: Multiply by the conjugate sqrt(x + a) + sqrt(x - b); the denominator becomes (x + a) - (x - b) = a + b. Hence the integral is (1/(a + b)) integral [sqrt(x + a) + sqrt(x - b)] dx = (1/(a + b))[(2/3)(x + a)^(3/2) + (2/3)(x - b)^(3/2)] + c = (2/(3(a + b)))[(x + a)^(3/2) + (x - b)^(3/2)] + c. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q5(iv); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The inner derivative 5 divides the answer: -(1/5)cos 5x.
questions.question: Q6(i). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sin 5x dx.
questions.solution: Use integral sin(ax) dx = -(1/a)cos(ax) + c with a = 5: integral sin 5x dx = -(1/5)cos 5x + c. Check: d/dx[-(1/5)cos 5x] = (1/5)(5 sin 5x) = sin 5x. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q6(i); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Linear argument: divide by the coefficient a, the constant b does not affect the answer.
questions.question: Q6(ii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sin(ax + b) dx.
questions.solution: Put y = ax + b, dy = a dx: integral sin(ax + b) dx = (1/a) integral sin y dy = -(1/a)cos y + c = -(1/a)cos(ax + b) + c. Check by differentiating: -(1/a)(-a sin(ax + b)) = sin(ax + b). Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q6(ii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The coefficient of x here is a^2, so the dividing factor is a^2 (not a).
questions.question: Q6(iii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of cos(a^2 x + b) dx.
questions.solution: Put y = a^2 x + b, dy = a^2 dx: integral cos y dy/a^2 = (1/a^2) sin(a^2 x + b) + c. Check: d/dx[(1/a^2)sin(a^2 x + b)] = (1/a^2)a^2 cos(a^2 x + b) = cos(a^2 x + b). Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q6(iii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The antiderivative of sec^2 is tan; the inner coefficient 2 divides.
questions.question: Q6(iv). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sec^2(2x + 3) dx.
questions.solution: Since d/dx[tan u] = sec^2 u * u', integral sec^2(2x + 3) dx = (1/2)tan(2x + 3) + c. Check: d/dx[(1/2)tan(2x+3)] = (1/2)sec^2(2x+3)*2 = sec^2(2x+3). Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q6(iv); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Never integrate a square directly: linearise with the half-angle identity first.
questions.question: Q6(v). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sin^2(ax) dx.
questions.solution: Use the double-angle identity sin^2 t = (1 - cos 2t)/2 with t = ax: integral sin^2(ax) dx = (1/2) integral [1 - cos(2ax)] dx = (1/2)[x - sin(2ax)/(2a)] + c. Check by differentiating: (1/2)[1 - cos(2ax)] = sin^2(ax). Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q6(v); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The companion half-angle identity gives the plus sign: (1/2)[x + sin(2bx)/(2b)].
questions.question: Q6(vi). Find the indefinite integral: integral of cos^2(bx) dx.
questions.solution: cos^2 t = (1 + cos 2t)/2 with t = bx: integral cos^2(bx) dx = (1/2) integral [1 + cos(2bx)] dx = (1/2)[x + sin(2bx)/(2b)] + c. Check: (1/2)[1 + cos 2bx] = cos^2(bx). Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q6(vi); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: tan^2 has no antiderivative of its own form; writing it as sec^2 - 1 makes both terms standard.
questions.question: Q6(vii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of tan^2(ax) dx.
questions.solution: Use tan^2 t = sec^2 t - 1 with t = ax: integral tan^2(ax) dx = integral [sec^2(ax) - 1] dx = (1/a)tan(ax) - x + c. Check: d/dx[(1/a)tan ax - x] = sec^2(ax) - 1 = tan^2(ax). Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q6(vii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Reduce sin^4 to a sum of cosines of multiple angles; the standard result is (1/32)(12x - 8 sin 2x + sin 4x).
questions.question: Q6(viii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sin^4 x dx.
questions.solution: Use sin^2 x = (1 - cos 2x)/2 twice: sin^4 x = [(1 - cos 2x)/2]^2 = (1/4)[1 - 2cos 2x + cos^2 2x] = (1/4)[1 - 2cos 2x + (1 + cos 4x)/2] = (3/8) - (1/2)cos 2x + (1/8)cos 4x. Integrate: (3/8)x - (1/4)sin 2x + (1/32)sin 4x + c = (1/32)[12x - 8 sin 2x + sin 4x] + c. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q6(viii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Each multiple-angle term is divided by its own inner coefficient (2n and 4n), giving the 1/(32n) factor.
questions.question: Q6(ix). Find the indefinite integral: integral of cos^4(nx) dx.
questions.solution: The same reduction with t = nx: cos^4 t = (3/8) + (1/2)cos 2t + (1/8)cos 4t. Hence integral cos^4(nx) dx = (3/8)x + (1/2)sin(2nx)/(2n) + (1/8)sin(4nx)/(4n) + c = (3/8)x + sin(2nx)/(4n) + sin(4nx)/(32n) + c = (1/(32n))[12nx + 8 sin 2nx + sin 4nx] + c. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q6(ix); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Split into sec^2 + csc^2 and integrate each to tan x and -cot x.
questions.question: Q6(x). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx/(cos^2 x sin^2 x).
questions.solution: Write the integrand as sec^2 x csc^2 x. Since sec^2 x csc^2 x = sec^2 x (1 + cot^2 x) = sec^2 x + sec^2 x cot^2 x, and sec^2 x cot^2 x = cos^2 x/(cos^2 x sin^2 x) = csc^2 x, the integrand is sec^2 x + csc^2 x. Integrate: tan x - cot x + c. Check: d/dx[tan x - cot x] = sec^2 x + csc^2 x. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q6(x); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Rewrite everything in sin and cos, expand, and use the half-angle identity once for sin^2 x.
questions.question: Q6(xi). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx/(sec^2 x tan^2 x).
questions.solution: 1/(sec^2 x tan^2 x) = cos^2 x * cos^2 x/sin^2 x = cos^4 x/sin^2 x = (1 - sin^2 x)^2/sin^2 x = 1/sin^2 x - 2 + sin^2 x. Integrate: integral csc^2 x dx = -cot x, integral 2 dx = 2x, integral sin^2 x dx = x/2 - sin 2x/4. So the result is -cot x - 2x + x/2 - sin 2x/4 + c = -cot x - (3/2)x - (1/4)sin 2x + c. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q6(xi); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Half-angle identity under the root; dividing by the inner coefficient n/2 doubles the constant.
questions.question: Q7(i). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sqrt(1 + cos nx) dx.
questions.solution: 1 + cos nx = 2cos^2(nx/2), so sqrt(1 + cos nx) = sqrt(2) cos(nx/2). Then integral sqrt(2)cos(nx/2) dx = sqrt(2) * sin(nx/2)/(n/2) + c = (2 sqrt 2/n) sin(nx/2) + c. Check: d/dx[(2 sqrt2/n) sin(nx/2)] = (2 sqrt2/n)(n/2)cos(nx/2) = sqrt2 cos(nx/2). Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q7(i); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The minus version of the half-angle identity gives a sine under the root and hence a cosine in the answer.
questions.question: Q7(ii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sqrt(1 - cos px) dx.
questions.solution: 1 - cos px = 2sin^2(px/2), so sqrt(1 - cos px) = sqrt(2) sin(px/2). Then integral sqrt(2) sin(px/2) dx = sqrt(2) * (-cos(px/2)/(p/2)) + c = -(2 sqrt 2/p) cos(px/2) + c. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q7(ii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Perfect square behind the root: sin^2 + cos^2 + 2 sincos = (sin + cos)^2.
questions.question: Q7(iii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sqrt(1 + sin 2ax) dx.
questions.solution: 1 + sin 2ax = sin^2(ax) + cos^2(ax) + 2 sin(ax)cos(ax) = (sin ax + cos ax)^2, so on the positive branch sqrt(1 + sin 2ax) = sin ax + cos ax. Integrate: -(1/a)cos ax + (1/a)sin ax + c = (1/a)(sin ax - cos ax) + c. Check by differentiating: (1/a)(a cos ax + a sin ax) = sin ax + cos ax. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q7(iii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Convert the denominator into a single cosine, which turns the integral into sec^2(mx/2)/2.
questions.question: Q7(iv). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx/(1 + cos mx).
questions.solution: 1 + cos mx = 2cos^2(mx/2), so the integrand is (1/2)sec^2(mx/2). Integrate: (1/2) * tan(mx/2)/(m/2) + c = (1/m)tan(mx/2) + c. Check: d/dx[(1/m)tan(mx/2)] = (1/m)sec^2(mx/2)(m/2) = (1/2)sec^2(mx/2) = 1/(1 + cos mx). Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q7(iv); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The companion case: 1 - cos gives a csc^2 and hence a minus cotangent.
questions.question: Q7(v). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx/(1 - cos nx).
questions.solution: 1 - cos nx = 2sin^2(nx/2), so the integrand is (1/2)csc^2(nx/2). Integrate: (1/2) * (-cot(nx/2))/(n/2) + c = -(1/n)cot(nx/2) + c. Check: d/dx[-(1/n)cot(nx/2)] = -(1/n)(-csc^2(nx/2))(n/2) = (1/2)csc^2(nx/2). Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q7(v); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Rationalising with the conjugate turns the denominator into cos^2 ax, giving two standard integrals.
questions.question: Q7(vi). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx/(1 - sin ax).
questions.solution: Multiply numerator and denominator by (1 + sin ax): the denominator becomes 1 - sin^2 ax = cos^2 ax, so the integrand is (1 + sin ax)/cos^2 ax = sec^2 ax + tan ax sec ax. Integrate: (1/a)tan ax + (1/a)sec ax + c = (1/a)(tan ax + sec ax) + c. Check by differentiating: sec^2 ax + sec ax tan ax, which is the rewritten integrand. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q7(vi); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Convert the product into a sum of sines before integrating; no product rule for integrals exists.
questions.question: Q8(i). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sin 6x cos 2x dx.
questions.solution: Use 2 sin A cos B = sin(A + B) + sin(A - B) with A = 6x, B = 2x: sin 6x cos 2x = (1/2)[sin 8x + sin 4x]. Integrate: (1/2)[-cos 8x/8 - cos 4x/4] + c = -cos 8x/16 - cos 4x/8 + c. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q8(i); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Product-to-sum for sine times sine carries the 1/2 and a minus on the higher-frequency term.
questions.question: Q8(ii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sin 7x sin 5x dx.
questions.solution: Use 2 sin A sin B = cos(A - B) - cos(A + B): sin 7x sin 5x = (1/2)[cos 2x - cos 12x]. Integrate: (1/2)[sin 2x/2 - sin 12x/12] + c = sin 2x/4 - sin 12x/24 + c. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q8(ii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: sin(A - B) with A < B is negative, which is why the second term gains a plus after integration.
questions.question: Q8(iii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sin 6x cos 8x dx.
questions.solution: 2 sin 6x cos 8x = sin 14x + sin(-2x) = sin 14x - sin 2x, so the integrand is (1/2)[sin 14x - sin 2x]. Integrate: (1/2)[-cos 14x/14 + cos 2x/2] + c = -cos 14x/28 + cos 2x/4 + c. Boxed (printed key p572, printed as cos 2x/4 - cos 14x/28 + c).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q8(iii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The general product-to-sum form; each multiple-angle sine is divided by its own coefficient.
questions.question: Q8(iv). Find the indefinite integral: integral of cos px cos qx dx.
questions.solution: Use 2 cos A cos B = cos(A + B) + cos(A - B): cos px cos qx = (1/2)[cos(p + q)x + cos(p - q)x]. Integrate: (1/2)[sin(p + q)x/(p + q) + sin(p - q)x/(p - q)] + c. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q8(iv); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: integral e^(kx) dx = e^(kx)/k: the negative exponent gives the minus sign in front.
questions.question: Q9(i). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (e^(px) + e^(-qx)) dx.
questions.solution: Integrate each exponential separately: integral e^(px) dx = e^(px)/p and integral e^(-qx) dx = e^(-qx)/(-q) = -e^(-qx)/q. Sum: e^(px)/p - e^(-qx)/q + c. Check by differentiating: e^(px) + e^(-qx). Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q9(i); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The cross term is 2e^(px)e^(-px) = 2, a constant, which integrates to 2x.
questions.question: Q9(ii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (e^(px) + e^(-px))^2 dx.
questions.solution: Expand the square: e^(2px) + 2 + e^(-2px). Integrate: e^(2px)/(2p) + 2x + e^(-2px)/(-2p) + c = e^(2px)/(2p) + 2x - e^(-2px)/(2p) + c. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q9(ii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Splitting the fraction reduces the problem to three standard exponentials.
questions.question: Q9(iii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (e^(2x) + e^x + 1)/e^x dx.
questions.solution: Divide term by term: e^(2x)/e^x = e^x, e^x/e^x = 1, 1/e^x = e^(-x), so the integrand is e^x + 1 + e^(-x). Integrate: e^x + x - e^(-x) + c. Check by differentiating: e^x + 1 + e^(-x). Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q9(iii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Multiplying powers adds exponents: x + 2x = 3x.
questions.question: Q9(iv). Find the indefinite integral: integral of e^x(e^(2x) + 1) dx.
questions.solution: Expand: e^x e^(2x) + e^x = e^(3x) + e^x. Integrate: e^(3x)/3 + e^x + c. Check: d/dx = e^(3x) + e^x. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q9(iv); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Substitution rule: if the derivative of the inner function appears as a factor, set u = inner function and the integral collapses to integral of u^n du.
questions.question: Q1(i). Find the indefinite integral: integral of 3x^2 (x^3 + 1)^3 dx. (T.U. 052 H)
questions.solution: Let u = x^3 + 1, du = 3x^2 dx - exactly the factor present. Then integral 3x^2(x^3+1)^3 dx = integral u^3 du = u^4/4 + c = (1/4)(x^3+1)^4 + c. Check: d/dx[(1/4)(x^3+1)^4] = (1/4)*4(x^3+1)^3*3x^2 = 3x^2(x^3+1)^3. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q1(i); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Constant-factor adjustment: du carries a constant multiple of x dx, so divide by that constant - never by x itself.
questions.question: Q1(ii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of x (a^2 + x^2)^(3/2) dx.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q1(ii); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: When the numerator is a constant multiple of the inner derivative the result is a logarithm: integral du/u = log|u|.
questions.question: Q1(iii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of x dx / (3x^2 - 4).
questions.solution: Let u = 3x^2 - 4, du = 6x dx, so x dx = du/6. Then integral x dx/(3x^2-4) = (1/6) integral du/u = (1/6) log|3x^2 - 4| + c. Check: d/dx = (1/6)*6x/(3x^2-4) = x/(3x^2-4). Boxed (printed key prints log(3x^2-4) without the modulus; the modulus is the correct domain-safe form).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q1(iii); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: The exponent n-1 is deliberately one less than n so that d(a^n + x^n) = n x^(n-1) dx: a textbook substitution.
questions.question: Q1(iv). Find the indefinite integral: integral of x^(n-1) dx / sqrt(a^n + x^n).
questions.solution: Let u = a^n + x^n, du = n x^(n-1) dx, so x^(n-1) dx = du/n. Then integral x^(n-1) dx/sqrt(a^n+x^n) = (1/n) integral u^(-1/2) du = (1/n)*2 sqrt(u) = (2/n) sqrt(a^n + x^n) + c. Check: d/dx[(2/n)(a^n+x^n)^(1/2)] = (2/n)*(1/2)(a^n+x^n)^(-1/2)*n x^(n-1) = x^(n-1)/sqrt(a^n+x^n). Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q1(iv); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Match the numerator to the inner derivative up to a constant: (3x^2+9x+5)' = 6x+9 = 3(2x+3).
questions.question: Q1(v). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (2x + 3) dx / (3x^2 + 9x + 5)^3.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q1(v); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Same pattern with a different constant: (3x^2+4x+1)' = 6x+4 = 2(3x+2).
questions.question: Q1(vi). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (3x + 2) dx / (3x^2 + 4x + 1)^3.
questions.solution: Let u = 3x^2 + 4x + 1, du = (6x+4) dx = 2(3x+2) dx, so (3x+2) dx = du/2. Then integral (3x+2)u^(-3) dx = (1/2) integral u^(-3) du = (1/2)*u^(-2)/(-2) = -1/(4u^2) + c = -1/[4(3x^2+4x+1)^2] + c. Check by differentiating back. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q1(vi); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Recognise 3x(x+2) = 3x^2 + 6x = (x^3 + 3x^2 + 1)' - the whole prefactor is the inner derivative.
questions.question: Q1(vii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of 3x(x + 2)(x^3 + 3x^2 + 1)^2 dx.
questions.solution: Let u = x^3 + 3x^2 + 1, du = (3x^2 + 6x) dx = 3x(x+2) dx. Then integral 3x(x+2)u^2 dx = integral u^2 du = u^3/3 + c = (1/3)(x^3+3x^2+1)^3 + c. Check: d/dx = (1/3)*3u^2*(3x^2+6x) = 3x(x+2)u^2. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q1(vii); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: The inner derivative 2x+4 = 2(x+2) is twice the numerator, so the answer is the square root itself.
questions.question: Q1(viii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (x + 2) dx / sqrt(x^2 + 4x + 3).
questions.solution: Let u = x^2 + 4x + 3, du = (2x+4) dx = 2(x+2) dx, so (x+2) dx = du/2. Then integral (x+2)u^(-1/2) dx = (1/2) integral u^(-1/2) du = (1/2)*2 sqrt(u) = sqrt(x^2+4x+3) + c. Check: d/dx sqrt(x^2+4x+3) = (2x+4)/(2 sqrt(x^2+4x+3)) = (x+2)/sqrt(...). Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q1(viii); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Here (x^3+3x+4)' = 3(x^2+1): the numerator is exactly one third of the inner derivative.
questions.question: Q1(ix). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (x^2 + 1) dx / sqrt(x^3 + 3x + 4).
questions.solution: Let u = x^3 + 3x + 4, du = 3(x^2+1) dx, so (x^2+1) dx = du/3. Then integral (x^2+1)u^(-1/2) dx = (1/3) integral u^(-1/2) du = (1/3)*2 sqrt(u) = (2/3) sqrt(x^3+3x+4) + c. Check by differentiating. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q1(ix); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Composite sine with a quadratic argument: u = ax^2 + b turns the integral into -(1/(2a)) cos u.
questions.question: Q2(i). Find the indefinite integral: integral of x sin(ax^2 + b) dx.
questions.solution: Let u = ax^2 + b, du = 2ax dx, so x dx = du/(2a). Then integral x sin(ax^2+b) dx = (1/(2a)) integral sin u du = -(1/(2a)) cos(ax^2+b) + c. Check: d/dx = (1/(2a)) sin u * (2ax) = x sin(ax^2+b). Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(i); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: d(x^3+1) = 3x^2 dx, so the cube-and-square pattern again gives a single sine term.
questions.question: Q2(ii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of x^2 cos(x^3 + 1) dx.
questions.solution: Let u = x^3 + 1, du = 3x^2 dx, so x^2 dx = du/3. Then integral x^2 cos(x^3+1) dx = (1/3) integral cos u du = (1/3) sin(x^3+1) + c. Check: d/dx = (1/3) cos u * 3x^2. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(ii); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: d(log x) = dx/x: the logarithmic substitution removes the 1/x factor entirely.
questions.question: Q2(iii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (1/x) sin(log x) dx.
questions.solution: Let u = log x, du = dx/x. Then integral (1/x) sin(log x) dx = integral sin u du = -cos u + c = -cos(log x) + c. Check: d/dx[-cos(log x)] = sin(log x)/x. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(iii); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Odd power of sine with its derivative present: u = sin x.
questions.question: Q2(iv). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sin^3 x cos x dx.
questions.solution: Let u = sin x, du = cos x dx. Then integral sin^3 x cos x dx = integral u^3 du = u^4/4 + c = (1/4) sin^4 x + c. Check: d/dx = sin^3 x cos x. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(iv); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: With an odd power of cosine, split off one cos x, convert the remaining even power by cos^2 = 1 - sin^2, then substitute u = sin x.
questions.question: Q2(v). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sin^2 x cos^3 x dx. (T.U. 2049 H)
questions.solution: Write cos^3 x = cos^2 x * cos x = (1 - sin^2 x) cos x. Let u = sin x, du = cos x dx: integral sin^2 x (1 - sin^2 x) cos x dx = integral (u^2 - u^4) du = u^3/3 - u^5/5 + c = (1/3) sin^3 x - (1/5) sin^5 x + c. Check: d/dx = sin^2 x cos x - sin^4 x cos x = sin^2 x cos x (1 - sin^2 x) = sin^2 x cos^3 x. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(v); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Now the odd power is sine's: keep one sin x as du, write sin^2 = 1 - cos^2, and substitute u = cos x (the minus sign flips the result).
questions.question: Q2(vi). Find the indefinite integral: integral of cos^5 x sin^3 x dx.
questions.solution: Write sin^3 x = sin^2 x * sin x = (1 - cos^2 x) sin x. Let u = cos x, du = -sin x dx, so sin x dx = -du: integral cos^5 x (1 - cos^2 x) sin x dx = -integral u^5 (1 - u^2) du = -u^6/6 + u^8/8 + c = (1/8) cos^8 x - (1/6) cos^6 x + c. Check: d/dx = -cos^7 x sin x + cos^5 x sin x = cos^5 x sin x (1 - cos^2 x) = cos^5 x sin^3 x. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(vi); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Linear inner function with cos x as its own derivative (over a).
questions.question: Q2(vii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (a sin x - b)^3 cos x dx.
questions.solution: Let u = a sin x - b, du = a cos x dx, so cos x dx = du/a. Then integral u^3 du/a = (1/a) u^4/4 + c = (1/(4a))(a sin x - b)^4 + c. Check: d/dx = (1/(4a))*4(a sin x - b)^3*a cos x. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(vii); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: d(1 - cos x) = sin x dx, so a power of a cosine-shifted denominator integrates by the power rule (m = 1 is the separate logarithmic case).
questions.question: Q2(viii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sin x dx / (1 - cos x)^m. (HSEB 2054)
questions.solution: Let u = 1 - cos x, du = sin x dx. Then integral u^(-m) du = u^(1-m)/(1-m) + c for m /= 1, i.e. (1/(1-m))(1 - cos x)^(1-m) + c. Check: d/dx = (1/(1-m))*(1-m)(1-cos x)^(-m)*sin x = sin x/(1-cos x)^m. For m = 1 the answer would be log|1 - cos x| + c instead. Boxed (printed key p578, m /= 1).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(viii); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: cot x dx = d(log sin x): the whole integrand is u^3 du with u = log sin x.
questions.question: Q2(ix). Find the indefinite integral: integral of cot x (log sin x)^3 dx. (T.U. 2052)
questions.solution: Let u = log sin x, then du = (cos x/sin x) dx = cot x dx. So integral u^3 du = u^4/4 + c = (1/4)(log sin x)^4 + c. Check: d/dx = (log sin x)^3 cot x. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(ix); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Even power of secant with a tan^2 in front: keep sec^2 theta dtheta for du and convert the remaining sec^2 with sec^2 = 1 + tan^2.
questions.question: Q2(x). Find the indefinite integral: integral of tan^2 theta sec^4 theta dtheta. (T.U. 2050 H)
questions.solution: Let u = tan theta, du = sec^2 theta dtheta; sec^4 theta = (1 + u^2) sec^2 theta. Then integral tan^2 theta sec^4 theta dtheta = integral u^2 (1 + u^2) du = u^3/3 + u^5/5 + c = (1/3) tan^3 theta + (1/5) tan^5 theta + c. Check: d/dtheta = tan^2 theta sec^2 theta + tan^4 theta sec^2 theta = tan^2 theta sec^2 theta (1 + tan^2 theta) = tan^2 theta sec^4 theta. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(x); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: sec^2 x is the derivative of tan x; the leftover sec^2 becomes (1 + tan^2).
questions.question: Q2(xi). Find the indefinite integral: integral of tan^3 x sec^4 x dx.
questions.solution: Let u = tan x, du = sec^2 x dx; sec^4 x = (1 + u^2)^2. Then integral tan^3 x sec^4 x dx = integral u^3 (1 + u^2) du = integral (u^3 + u^5) du = u^4/4 + u^6/6 + c = (1/4) tan^4 x + (1/6) tan^6 x + c. Check: d/dx = tan^3 x sec^2 x + tan^5 x sec^2 x = tan^3 x sec^2 x (1 + tan^2 x) = tan^3 x sec^4 x. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(xi); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Here the odd power is tan's: keep sec x tan x for du and rewrite tan^2 = sec^2 - 1 in terms of u = sec x.
questions.question: Q2(xii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of tan^3 x sec^(3/2) x dx.
questions.solution: Let u = sec x, du = sec x tan x dx. Write tan^3 x sec^(3/2) x = tan^2 x * sec^(1/2) x * (sec x tan x) = (u^2 - 1) u^(1/2) du. So integral = integral (u^(5/2) - u^(1/2)) du = (2/7) u^(7/2) - (2/3) u^(3/2) + c = (2/7) sec^(7/2) x - (2/3) sec^(3/2) x + c. Check: d/dx = sec^(5/2) x sec x tan x - sec^(1/2) x sec x tan x = tan x sec^(3/2) x (sec^2 x - 1) = tan^3 x sec^(3/2) x. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(xii); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Mirror of Q2(xi) for the co-functions: d(cot x) = -cosec^2 x dx, and cosec^2 = 1 + cot^2.
questions.question: Q2(xiii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of cot^(3/2) x cosec^4 x dx.
questions.solution: Let u = cot x, du = -cosec^2 x dx; cosec^4 x = (1 + u^2) cosec^2 x. Then integral cot^(3/2) x cosec^4 x dx = -integral u^(3/2)(1 + u^2) du = -[u^(5/2)/(5/2) + u^(9/2)/(9/2)] = -(2/5) cot^(5/2) x - (2/9) cot^(9/2) x + c. Check: d/dx[-(2/5)cot^(5/2)x] = -(2/5)(5/2)cot^(3/2)x*(-cosec^2 x) = cot^(3/2)x cosec^2 x, and -(2/9)(9/2)cot^(7/2)x*(-cosec^2 x) = cot^(7/2)x cosec^2 x; the sum is cot^(3/2)x cosec^2 x (1 + cot^2 x) = cot^(3/2)x cosec^4 x. Boxed (printed key p578 reads -(2/5)cot^(5/2)x -(2/9)cot^(9/2)x + c - 320-dpi zoom confirms the 5).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(xiii); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Numerator is (1/a) times the derivative of the denominator - the logarithmic form again.
questions.question: Q2(xiv). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (sin ax + cos ax)/(sin ax - cos ax) dx.
questions.solution: d/dx (sin ax - cos ax) = a(cos ax + sin ax) = a(sin ax + cos ax). Hence integral (sin ax + cos ax)/(sin ax - cos ax) dx = (1/a) integral du/u with u = sin ax - cos ax, giving (1/a) log|sin ax - cos ax| + c. Check: d/dx = (1/a)*a(cos ax + sin ax)/(sin ax - cos ax). Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(xiv); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Standard form: cot x = cos x/sin x, and cos x is the derivative of sin x.
questions.question: Q2(xv). Find the indefinite integral: integral of cot x dx.
questions.solution: integral cot x dx = integral cos x dx/sin x. With u = sin x, du = cos x dx: integral du/u = log|sin x| + c. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(xv); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Companion standard form: tan x = sin x/cos x and sin x dx = -d(cos x).
questions.question: Q2(xvi). Find the indefinite integral: integral of tan x dx.
questions.solution: integral tan x dx = integral sin x dx/cos x = -integral du/u with u = cos x = -log|cos x| + c = log|sec x| + c. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(xvi); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Multiply and divide by (sec x + tan x) so the top becomes the derivative of the bottom.
questions.question: Q2(xvii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sec x dx.
questions.solution: sec x = sec x (sec x + tan x)/(sec x + tan x). The numerator sec^2 x + sec x tan x = d(sec x + tan x)/dx, so the integral is log|sec x + tan x| + c. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(xvii); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Multiply and divide by (cosec x - cot x): its derivative is -cosec x (cosec x - cot x).
questions.question: Q2(xviii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of cosec x dx.
questions.solution: Write cosec x = cosec x (cosec x - cot x)/(cosec x - cot x). Since d(cosec x - cot x)/dx = -cosec x cot x + cosec^2 x = cosec x (cosec x - cot x), the integral is log|cosec x - cot x| + c. Equivalently log|tan(x/2)| + c. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(xviii); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Peel off tan x sec^2 x (which integrates to tan^2/2) and convert the remaining tan^2 with the identity tan^2 = sec^2 - 1.
questions.question: Q2(xix). Find the indefinite integral: integral of tan^3 x dx.
questions.solution: tan^3 x = tan x (sec^2 x - 1) = tan x sec^2 x - tan x. Hence integral tan^3 x dx = (1/2) tan^2 x - integral tan x dx = (1/2) tan^2 x - log|sec x| + c = (1/2) tan^2 x + log|cos x| + c. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(xix); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Mirror image: cot^3 = cot x cosec^2 x - cot x.
questions.question: Q2(xx). Find the indefinite integral: integral of cot^3 x dx.
questions.solution: cot^3 x = cot x (cosec^2 x - 1) = cot x cosec^2 x - cot x. The first term integrates to -(1/2) cot^2 x and integral cot x dx = log|sin x|, so integral cot^3 x dx = -(1/2) cot^2 x - log|sin x| + c. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(xx); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Even power of secant: keep sec^2 x for du, express the rest with sec^2 = 1 + tan^2.
questions.question: Q2(xxi). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sec^4 x dx.
questions.solution: sec^4 x = (1 + tan^2 x) sec^2 x. With u = tan x, du = sec^2 x dx: integral (1 + u^2) du = u + u^3/3 + c = tan x + (1/3) tan^3 x + c. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(xxi); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Even power of tangent: split tan^2 * tan^2 and replace one factor by sec^2 - 1 to expose a perfect derivative.
questions.question: Q2(xxii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of tan^4 x dx. (T.U. 2053)
questions.solution: tan^4 x = tan^2 x (sec^2 x - 1) = tan^2 x sec^2 x - tan^2 x. The first term gives tan^3 x/3; for the second write tan^2 x = sec^2 x - 1, so integral tan^2 x dx = tan x - x. Hence integral tan^4 x dx = (1/3) tan^3 x - tan x + x + c. Check: d/dx = tan^2 x sec^2 x - sec^2 x + 1 = tan^2 x sec^2 x - tan^2 x = tan^4 x. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(xxii); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Odd power: peel tan x sec^2 x, then the remaining tan^2 integrates as tan x - x.
questions.question: Q2(xxiii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of tan^5 x dx.
questions.solution: tan^5 x = tan^3 x (sec^2 x - 1). So integral tan^5 x dx = integral tan^3 x sec^2 x dx - integral tan^3 x dx = tan^4 x/4 - [tan^2 x/2 - log|sec x|] = (1/4) tan^4 x - (1/2) tan^2 x + log|sec x| + c, using Q2(xix). Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(xxiii); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Factor the identity: tan^2 + tan^4 = tan^2 (1 + tan^2) = tan^2 x sec^2 x - a perfect derivative.
questions.question: Q2(xxiv). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (tan^2 x + tan^4 x) dx.
questions.solution: tan^2 x + tan^4 x = tan^2 x (1 + tan^2 x) = tan^2 x sec^2 x. With u = tan x, du = sec^2 x dx: integral u^2 du = u^3/3 + c = (1/3) tan^3 x + c. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(xxiv); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: sin x cos x = (1/2) sin 2x, and its derivative is cos 2x: the exponent's derivative is exactly the multiplier.
questions.question: Q2(xxv). Find the indefinite integral: integral of e^(sin x cos x) cos 2x dx.
questions.solution: Let u = sin x cos x = (1/2) sin 2x. Then du = (1/2)*2 cos 2x dx = cos 2x dx, so integral e^u du = e^u + c = e^(sin x cos x) + c. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(xxv); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: d(sin^2 x) = 2 sin x cos x = sin 2x, so the multiplier is precisely the derivative of the exponent.
questions.question: Q2(xxvi). Find the indefinite integral: integral of e^(sin^2 x) sin 2x dx. (T.U. 2048 H)
questions.solution: Let u = sin^2 x, du = 2 sin x cos x dx = sin 2x dx. Then integral e^u du = e^u + c = e^(sin^2 x) + c. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(xxvi); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: d(x + 1/x) = 1 - 1/x^2 - the classic exponent-is-its-own-derivative trick.
questions.question: Q2(xxvii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (1 - 1/x^2) e^(x + 1/x) dx. (T.U. 2048, 2055 S, 2058 S)
questions.solution: Let u = x + 1/x, du = (1 - 1/x^2) dx. Then integral e^u du = e^u + c = e^(x + 1/x) + c. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(xxvii); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: d(sqrt x) = dx/(2 sqrt x): the 1/sqrt x factor is the derivative up to the constant 2.
questions.question: Q2(xxviii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sin(sqrt(x))/sqrt(x) dx. (T.U. 2050)
questions.solution: Let u = sqrt x, du = dx/(2 sqrt x), so dx/sqrt x = 2 du. Then integral sin u * 2 du = -2 cos u + c = -2 cos(sqrt x) + c. Check: d/dx = -2(-sin sqrt x)*(1/(2 sqrt x)) = sin sqrt x / sqrt x. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(xxviii); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Substituting u = 1 + e^x turns e^x into u - 1, so the integrand becomes a simple proper fraction.
questions.question: Q2(xxix). Find the indefinite integral: integral of e^(2x) dx/(1 + e^x). (T.U. 2052 H)
questions.solution: Let u = 1 + e^x, du = e^x dx. Since e^(2x) = e^x * e^x = (u - 1) du, integral e^(2x)/(1 + e^x) dx = integral (u - 1)/u du = integral (1 - 1/u) du = u - log|u| + c = e^x - log(1 + e^x) + c (since u > 0). Check: d/dx = e^x - e^x/(1 + e^x) = e^x(1 + e^x - 1)/(1 + e^x) = e^(2x)/(1 + e^x). Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(xxix); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Divide top and bottom by e^(x/2) to reveal tanh(x/2), whose integral is 2 log cosh(x/2).
questions.question: Q2(xxx). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (e^x - 1)/(e^x + 1) dx.
questions.solution: Multiply numerator and denominator by e^(-x/2): (e^(x/2) - e^(-x/2))/(e^(x/2) + e^(-x/2)) = tanh(x/2). Then integral tanh(x/2) dx = 2 log|cosh(x/2)| + c = 2 log(e^(x/2) + e^(-x/2)) + c (the log 2 and log cosh constants absorb into c). Check: d/dx[2 log(e^(x/2)+e^(-x/2))] = 2 * ((1/2)e^(x/2) - (1/2)e^(-x/2))/(e^(x/2)+e^(-x/2)) = (e^x - 1)/(e^x + 1). Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(xxx); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: d(x e^x - e^x) = x e^x dx, so the reciprocal-cosine-squared is a sec^2 of the inner function.
questions.question: Q2(xxxi). Find the indefinite integral: integral of x e^x dx / cos^2 (x e^x - e^x).
questions.solution: Let u = x e^x - e^x. Then du = (e^x + x e^x - e^x) dx = x e^x dx - exactly the numerator. So integral sec^2 u du = tan u + c = tan(x e^x - e^x) + c. Boxed (printed key p578).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.2 Q2(xxxi); book p576-577 = PDF p603-604; key book p578 = PDF p605

questions.knowledgeNote: Standard inverse-sine form: the derivative of sin^-1 x is exactly 1/sqrt(1-x^2).
questions.question: Q1(i). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx / sqrt(1 - x^2).
questions.solution: Recognise d/dx (sin^-1 x) = 1/sqrt(1-x^2), so integral dx/sqrt(1-x^2) = sin^-1 x + c. Derivation by substitution: put x = sin theta, dx = cos theta d theta, sqrt(1-x^2) = cos theta, giving integral d theta = theta + c = sin^-1 x + c. Boxed (printed key p583).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.3 Q1(i); book p582-583 = PDF p609-610; key book p583 = PDF p610

questions.knowledgeNote: For sqrt(a^2 - x^2) put x = a sin theta; here a = 3. The surviving cosec^2 theta integrates to -cot theta.
questions.question: Q1(ii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx / [x^2 sqrt(9 - x^2)].
questions.solution: Let x = 3 sin theta, dx = 3 cos theta d theta, sqrt(9-x^2) = 3 cos theta. Then x^2 sqrt(9-x^2) = 9 sin^2 theta * 3 cos theta = 27 sin^2 theta cos theta, so the integral is integral 3 cos theta d theta/(27 sin^2 theta cos theta) = (1/9) integral cosec^2 theta d theta = -(1/9) cot theta + c = -(1/9) sqrt(9-x^2)/x + c = -sqrt(9-x^2)/(9x) + c. Check: d/dx[-sqrt(9-x^2)/(9x)] = -1/9 [(-x/sqrt(9-x^2))*x - sqrt(9-x^2)]/x^2 = -1/9[(-x^2 - (9-x^2))/sqrt(9-x^2)]/x^2 = 1/(x^2 sqrt(9-x^2)). Boxed (printed key p583).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.3 Q1(ii); book p582-583 = PDF p609-610; key book p583 = PDF p610

questions.knowledgeNote: x = a sin theta collapses the 3/2 power to a cos^3 theta, leaving integral sec^2 theta d theta = tan theta.
questions.question: Q1(iii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx / (a^2 - x^2)^(3/2).
questions.solution: Let x = a sin theta, dx = a cos theta d theta, (a^2 - x^2)^(3/2) = (a^2 cos^2 theta)^(3/2) = a^3 cos^3 theta. Then the integral = integral a cos theta d theta/(a^3 cos^3 theta) = (1/a^2) integral sec^2 theta d theta = (1/a^2) tan theta + c = (1/a^2) * x/sqrt(a^2-x^2) + c = x/(a^2 sqrt(a^2-x^2)) + c. Check: d/dx[x/(a^2 sqrt(a^2-x^2))] = (1/a^2)[sqrt(a^2-x^2) + x^2/sqrt(a^2-x^2)]/(a^2-x^2) = (1/a^2)(a^2)/(a^2-x^2)^(3/2) = 1/(a^2-x^2)^(3/2). Boxed (printed key p583).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.3 Q1(iii); book p582-583 = PDF p609-610; key book p583 = PDF p610

questions.knowledgeNote: Same substitution, then the half-angle identity sin^2 theta = (1 - cos 2 theta)/2 turns it into two elementary integrals.
questions.question: Q1(iv). Find the indefinite integral: integral of x^2 dx / sqrt(a^2 - x^2).
questions.solution: Let x = a sin theta, dx = a cos theta d theta, sqrt(a^2-x^2) = a cos theta. Then integral x^2 dx/sqrt(a^2-x^2) = integral a^2 sin^2 theta * a cos theta d theta/(a cos theta) = a^2 integral sin^2 theta d theta = a^2 integral (1 - cos 2 theta)/2 d theta = (a^2/2)[theta - (sin 2 theta)/2] + c = (a^2/2)(theta - sin theta cos theta) + c = (a^2/2) sin^-1(x/a) - (1/2) x sqrt(a^2-x^2) + c (since a^2 sin theta cos theta = x sqrt(a^2-x^2)). Boxed (printed key p583).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.3 Q1(iv); book p582-583 = PDF p609-610; key book p583 = PDF p610

questions.knowledgeNote: x = 3 sec theta turns sqrt(x^2-9) into 3 tan theta; the leftover sec theta tan^2 theta splits into sec theta sec^2 theta - sec theta.
questions.question: Q2(i). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sqrt(x^2 - 9) dx / x.
questions.solution: Let x = 3 sec theta, dx = 3 sec theta tan theta d theta, sqrt(x^2-9) = 3 tan theta. Then integral sqrt(x^2-9) dx/x = integral 3 tan theta * 3 sec theta tan theta d theta/(3 sec theta) = 3 integral tan^2 theta d theta = 3 integral (sec^2 theta - 1) d theta = 3(tan theta - theta) + c = sqrt(x^2-9) - 3 sec^-1(x/3) + c. Check: d/dx[sqrt(x^2-9)] = x/sqrt(x^2-9) and d/dx[-3 sec^-1(x/3)] = -3 * (1/3)/((x/3)sqrt(x^2/9-1)) = -3/x * ... = -(3*3)/(x sqrt(x^2-9)) = -9/(x sqrt(x^2-9)); the sum is (x^2-9)/(x sqrt(x^2-9)) = sqrt(x^2-9)/x. Boxed (printed key p583).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.3 Q2(i); book p582-583 = PDF p609-610; key book p583 = PDF p610

questions.knowledgeNote: x = a sec theta: the sec/tan factors cancel completely and leave a plain cosine.
questions.question: Q2(ii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx / [x^2 sqrt(x^2 - a^2)].
questions.solution: Let x = a sec theta, dx = a sec theta tan theta d theta, sqrt(x^2-a^2) = a tan theta. Then x^2 sqrt(x^2-a^2) = a^3 sec^2 theta tan theta, so the integral = integral a sec theta tan theta d theta/(a^3 sec^2 theta tan theta) = (1/a^2) integral cos theta d theta = (1/a^2) sin theta + c = (1/a^2) sqrt(x^2-a^2)/x + c = sqrt(x^2-a^2)/(a^2 x) + c. Boxed (printed key p583).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.3 Q2(ii); book p582-583 = PDF p609-610; key book p583 = PDF p610

questions.knowledgeNote: After x = a sec theta the integrand becomes sec theta/tan^2 theta = cosec theta cot theta, whose integral is -cosec theta.
questions.question: Q2(iii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx / (x^2 - a^2)^(3/2).
questions.solution: Let x = a sec theta, dx = a sec theta tan theta d theta, (x^2-a^2)^(3/2) = a^3 tan^3 theta. Then the integral = integral a sec theta tan theta d theta/(a^3 tan^3 theta) = (1/a^2) integral sec theta/tan^2 theta d theta = (1/a^2) integral cosec theta cot theta d theta = -(1/a^2) cosec theta + c = -(1/a^2) * x/sqrt(x^2-a^2) + c = -x/(a^2 sqrt(x^2-a^2)) + c. Boxed (printed key p583).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.3 Q2(iii); book p582-583 = PDF p609-610; key book p583 = PDF p610

questions.knowledgeNote: Standard logarithmic form integral dx/sqrt(x^2 - a^2) = log|x + sqrt(x^2-a^2)|, here a = 2.
questions.question: Q2(iv). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx / sqrt(x^2 - 4).
questions.solution: Use the standard result (obtained by x = 2 sec theta, or by rationalising with u = x + sqrt(x^2-4)): integral dx/sqrt(x^2-4) = log|x + sqrt(x^2-4)| + c. Check: d/dx log|x + sqrt(x^2-4)| = [1 + x/sqrt(x^2-4)]/[x + sqrt(x^2-4)] = [sqrt(x^2-4) + x]/[sqrt(x^2-4)(x + sqrt(x^2-4))] = 1/sqrt(x^2-4). Boxed (printed key p583).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.3 Q2(iv); book p582-583 = PDF p609-610; key book p583 = PDF p610

questions.knowledgeNote: The substitution x = a sec theta turns the whole thing into 4a integral cosec^2(2 theta) d theta; then cot 2 theta is converted back to x.
questions.question: Q2(v). Find the indefinite integral: integral of x^3 dx / (x^2 - a^2)^(3/2).
questions.solution: Let x = a sec theta, dx = a sec theta tan theta d theta, x^3 = a^3 sec^3 theta, (x^2-a^2)^(3/2) = a^3 tan^3 theta. Then the integral = integral a^3 sec^3 theta * a sec theta tan theta d theta/(a^3 tan^3 theta) = a integral sec^4 theta/tan^2 theta d theta = a integral d theta/(sin^2 theta cos^2 theta) = 4a integral cosec^2(2 theta) d theta = -2a cot 2 theta + c. Now cot theta = a/sqrt(x^2-a^2), so cot 2 theta = (cot^2 theta - 1)/(2 cot theta) = (2a^2 - x^2)/(2a sqrt(x^2-a^2)). Hence -2a cot 2 theta = (x^2 - 2a^2)/sqrt(x^2-a^2) + c. Boxed (printed key p583).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.3 Q2(v); book p582-583 = PDF p609-610; key book p583 = PDF p610

questions.knowledgeNote: Standard inverse-tangent form; the a in the denominator comes out of the substitution x = a tan theta.
questions.question: Q3(i). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx / (x^2 + a^2).
questions.solution: Let x = a tan theta, dx = a sec^2 theta d theta, x^2 + a^2 = a^2 sec^2 theta. Then the integral = integral a sec^2 theta d theta/(a^2 sec^2 theta) = (1/a) integral d theta = (1/a) theta + c = (1/a) tan^-1(x/a) + c. Boxed (printed key p583).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.3 Q3(i); book p582-583 = PDF p609-610; key book p583 = PDF p610

questions.knowledgeNote: x = tan theta gives integral sec theta/tan^2 theta d theta = -cosec theta, and cosec theta = sqrt(x^2+1)/x.
questions.question: Q3(ii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx / [x^2 sqrt(x^2 + 1)].
questions.solution: Let x = tan theta, dx = sec^2 theta d theta, sqrt(x^2+1) = sec theta. Then x^2 sqrt(x^2+1) = tan^2 theta sec theta, so the integral = integral sec^2 theta d theta/(tan^2 theta sec theta) = integral sec theta/tan^2 theta d theta = integral (1/cos theta)(cos^2 theta/sin^2 theta) d theta = integral cos theta/sin^2 theta d theta = -1/sin theta + c = -cosec theta + c = -sqrt(x^2+1)/x + c. Boxed (printed key p583).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.3 Q3(ii); book p582-583 = PDF p609-610; key book p583 = PDF p610

questions.knowledgeNote: x = tan theta makes the integrand sin^2 theta; the half-angle identity then gives two terms.
questions.question: Q3(iii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of x^2 dx / (1 + x^2)^2.
questions.solution: Let x = tan theta, dx = sec^2 theta d theta, (1+x^2)^2 = sec^4 theta. Then integral x^2 dx/(1+x^2)^2 = integral tan^2 theta sec^2 theta d theta/sec^4 theta = integral sin^2 theta d theta = (1/2) integral (1 - cos 2 theta) d theta = (1/2)(theta - (sin 2 theta)/2) + c = (1/2)(theta - sin theta cos theta) + c = (1/2) tan^-1 x - (1/2) * x/(1+x^2) + c. Boxed (printed key p583 prints (1/2)tan^-1 x - (1/2) x/(x^2+1) + c).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.3 Q3(iii); book p582-583 = PDF p609-610; key book p583 = PDF p610

questions.knowledgeNote: Standard logarithmic form integral dx/sqrt(a^2+x^2) = log|x + sqrt(a^2+x^2)|.
questions.question: Q3(iv). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx / sqrt(a^2 + x^2).
questions.solution: Substitute x = a tan theta: dx = a sec^2 theta d theta, sqrt(a^2+x^2) = a sec theta, so the integral = integral sec theta d theta = log|sec theta + tan theta| + c = log|sqrt(a^2+x^2)/a + x/a| + c = log|x + sqrt(a^2+x^2)| + c (the -log a is absorbed into c). Boxed (printed key p583).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.3 Q3(iv); book p582-583 = PDF p609-610; key book p583 = PDF p610

questions.knowledgeNote: x = tan theta turns it into integral cosec theta d theta = log|tan(theta/2)|, then tan(theta/2) = (sec theta - 1)/tan theta is converted back.
questions.question: Q3(v). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx / [x sqrt(x^2 + 1)].
questions.solution: Let x = tan theta, dx = sec^2 theta d theta, sqrt(x^2+1) = sec theta. Then the integral = integral sec^2 theta d theta/(tan theta sec theta) = integral sec theta/tan theta d theta = integral cosec theta d theta = log|tan(theta/2)| + c. Using tan(theta/2) = (sec theta - 1)/tan theta = (sqrt(x^2+1) - 1)/x, the answer is log|(sqrt(x^2+1) - 1)/x| + c. Boxed (printed key p583). Equivalently -log|(sqrt(x^2+1)+1)/x| + c = -log|cosec theta + cot theta| + c, the same family.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.3 Q3(v); book p582-583 = PDF p609-610; key book p583 = PDF p610

questions.knowledgeNote: The denominator is the derivative of tan^-1 x, so the whole integrand is u du with u = tan^-1 x.
questions.question: Q3(vi). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (tan^-1 x)/(1 + x^2) dx.
questions.solution: Let u = tan^-1 x, du = dx/(1+x^2). Then integral u du = u^2/2 + c = (1/2)(tan^-1 x)^2 + c. Check: d/dx = tan^-1 x * 1/(1+x^2). Boxed (printed key p583).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.3 Q3(vi); book p582-583 = PDF p609-610; key book p583 = PDF p610

questions.knowledgeNote: Rationalise the numerator first: sqrt((a+x)/(a-x)) = (a+x)/sqrt(a^2-x^2), which splits into two standard forms.
questions.question: Q4(i). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sqrt((a + x)/(a - x)) dx.
questions.solution: Multiply numerator and denominator of the radicand's fraction by (a+x): sqrt((a+x)/(a-x)) = sqrt((a+x)^2/(a^2-x^2)) = (a+x)/sqrt(a^2-x^2) for a+x > 0. So the integral = integral a dx/sqrt(a^2-x^2) + integral x dx/sqrt(a^2-x^2) = a sin^-1(x/a) - sqrt(a^2-x^2) + c. Check: d/dx = a/sqrt(a^2-x^2) + x/sqrt(a^2-x^2) = (a+x)/sqrt(a^2-x^2) = sqrt((a+x)/(a-x)). Boxed (printed key p583).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.3 Q4(i); book p582-583 = PDF p609-610; key book p583 = PDF p610

questions.knowledgeNote: Substitute x = a sin^2 phi so that the radical becomes tan of a half-angle, leaving 2a integral sin^2 phi d phi.
questions.question: Q4(ii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sqrt(x/(a - x)) dx.
questions.solution: Let x = a sin^2 phi, so dx = 2a sin phi cos phi d phi and sqrt(x/(a-x)) = sin phi/cos phi. Then the integral = integral (sin phi/cos phi)(2a sin phi cos phi) d phi = 2a integral sin^2 phi d phi = a integral (1 - cos 2 phi) d phi = a(phi - sin phi cos phi) + c. Since phi = sin^-1 sqrt(x/a) and sin phi cos phi = sqrt(x/a) * sqrt((a-x)/a) = sqrt(x(a-x))/a, the answer is a sin^-1 sqrt(x/a) - sqrt(x(a-x)) + c. Boxed (printed key p583).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.3 Q4(ii); book p582-583 = PDF p609-610; key book p583 = PDF p610
