questions.knowledgeNote: LIATE rule: the logarithm is the u, the algebraic part is dv, so differentiating removes the log entirely.
questions.question: Q1(a). Calculate the integral: integral of x log x dx.
questions.solution: By parts with u = log x, dv = x dx, so du = dx/x, v = x^2/2: integral u dv = uv - integral v du gives integral x log x dx = (x^2/2) log x - integral (x^2/2)(dx/x) = (x^2/2) log x - (1/2) integral x dx = (x^2/2) log x - x^2/4 + c = (1/4)x^2 (2 log x - 1) + c. Boxed (printed key p588).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(a); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: Same LIATE split with a linear factor: u = log x, dv = (5x - 2) dx, v = 5x^2/2 - 2x.
questions.question: Q1(b). Calculate the integral: integral of (5x - 2) log x dx.
questions.solution: By parts with u = log x, dv = (5x-2)dx, du = dx/x, v = 5x^2/2 - 2x: integral = (5x^2/2 - 2x) log x - integral (5x^2/2 - 2x)(dx/x) = (5x^2/2 - 2x) log x - integral (5x/2 - 2) dx = (5x^2/2 - 2x) log x - 5x^2/4 + 2x + c = (1/2)x(5x - 4) log x - 5x^2/4 + 2x + c. Boxed (printed key p588).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(b); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: The general log-times-power case: v = x^(n+1)/(n+1) and the leftover integral is again a pure power.
questions.question: Q1(c). Calculate the integral: integral of x^n log x dx. (T.U. 2051 H).
questions.solution: By parts with u = log x, dv = x^n dx, du = dx/x, v = x^(n+1)/(n+1): integral = x^(n+1)/(n+1) log x - (1/(n+1)) integral x^n dx = x^(n+1)/(n+1) log x - x^(n+1)/(n+1)^2 + c = x^(n+1)/(n+1)^2 [(n+1) log x - 1] + c. Boxed (printed key p588). Note n = -1 is excluded because log x itself would then be the integrand's square.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(c); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: Take u = (log x)^2 with dv = dx; one round of by parts leaves integral log x dx, which is a known standard form.
questions.question: Q1(d). Calculate the integral: integral of (log x)^2 dx.
questions.solution: By parts with u = (log x)^2, dv = dx, du = 2 log x dx/x, v = x: integral (log x)^2 dx = x(log x)^2 - 2 integral log x dx = x(log x)^2 - 2(x log x - x) + c = x(log x)^2 - 2x log x + 2x + c. (The inner integral is itself by parts: integral log x dx = x log x - x.) Boxed (printed key p588).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(d); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: u = log(x - 1), dv = x dx; the leftover integral is an improper fraction, so divide x^2 by (x - 1) first.
questions.question: Q1(e). Calculate the integral: integral of x log(x - 1) dx. (T.U. 049 H).
questions.solution: By parts with u = log(x-1), dv = x dx, du = dx/(x-1), v = x^2/2: integral = (x^2/2) log(x-1) - (1/2) integral x^2 dx/(x-1). Polynomial division: x^2/(x-1) = x + 1 + 1/(x-1), so the leftover is (1/2)[x^2/2 + x + log(x-1)]. Hence integral = (x^2/2) log(x-1) - x^2/4 - x/2 - (1/2) log(x-1) + c = (1/2)(x^2 - 1) log(x-1) - x^2/4 - x/2 + c. Boxed (printed key p588).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(e); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: Exponential beats polynomial in LIATE, so u = x^2 and by parts runs twice, the power dropping 2 -> 1 -> 0.
questions.question: Q1(f). Calculate the integral: integral of x^2 e^(ax) dx. (HSEB 2058).
questions.solution: By parts with u = x^2, dv = e^(ax) dx, du = 2x dx, v = e^(ax)/a: integral x^2 e^(ax) dx = x^2 e^(ax)/a - (2/a) integral x e^(ax) dx. Apply by parts again to integral x e^(ax) dx = x e^(ax)/a - e^(ax)/a^2. Therefore the integral = x^2 e^(ax)/a - (2/a)[x e^(ax)/a - e^(ax)/a^2] + c = x^2 e^(ax)/a - 2x e^(ax)/a^2 + 2 e^(ax)/a^3 + c. Boxed (printed key p588).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(f); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: Single round of by parts with a = 5, then simplify: (5x - 1)e^(5x)/25.
questions.question: Q1(g). Calculate the integral: integral of x e^(5x) dx.
questions.solution: By parts with u = x, dv = e^(5x) dx, du = dx, v = e^(5x)/5: integral x e^(5x) dx = x e^(5x)/5 - (1/5) integral e^(5x) dx = x e^(5x)/5 - e^(5x)/25 + c = (5x - 1) e^(5x)/25 + c. Boxed (printed key p588).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(g); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: With a linear factor one round of by parts is enough, and the answer collapses to (x - 1)e^(2x).
questions.question: Q1(h). Calculate the integral: integral of (2x - 1) e^(2x) dx. (T.U. 048).
questions.solution: By parts with u = 2x - 1, dv = e^(2x) dx, du = 2 dx, v = e^(2x)/2: integral = (2x-1) e^(2x)/2 - integral e^(2x) dx = (2x-1) e^(2x)/2 - e^(2x)/2 + c = (2x - 2) e^(2x)/2 + c = (x - 1) e^(2x) + c. Boxed (printed key p588).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(h); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: u = x, dv = sin x dx with v = -cos x; the sign is the usual trap in this classic.
questions.question: Q1(i). Calculate the integral: integral of x sin x dx. (T.U. 2053 H, HSEB 2057).
questions.solution: By parts with u = x, dv = sin x dx, du = dx, v = -cos x: integral x sin x dx = -x cos x + integral cos x dx = -x cos x + sin x + c = sin x - x cos x + c. Check: d/dx = cos x - cos x + x sin x = x sin x. Boxed (printed key p588).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(i); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: dv = sec^2 x dx integrates straight to tan x, and the leftover integral of tan x gives log cos x.
questions.question: Q1(j). Calculate the integral: integral of x sec^2 x dx. (T.U. 048 H).
questions.solution: By parts with u = x, dv = sec^2 x dx, du = dx, v = tan x: integral x sec^2 x dx = x tan x - integral tan x dx = x tan x - log|sec x| + c = x tan x + log|cos x| + c. Boxed (printed key p588 prints x tan x + log cos x + c).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(j); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: sec x tan x is the derivative of sec x, so it is the dv; the remaining integral is the standard integral of sec x.
questions.question: Q1(k). Calculate the integral: integral of x sec x tan x dx.
questions.solution: By parts with u = x, dv = sec x tan x dx, du = dx, v = sec x: integral x sec x tan x dx = x sec x - integral sec x dx = x sec x - log|sec x + tan x| + c. Boxed (printed key p588).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(k); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: Linear times cosine: u = x, dv = cos nx dx, and the chain factor 1/n appears twice.
questions.question: Q1(l). Calculate the integral: integral of x cos(nx) dx.
questions.solution: By parts with u = x, dv = cos nx dx, du = dx, v = sin nx/n: integral x cos nx dx = x sin nx/n - (1/n) integral sin nx dx = x sin nx/n + cos nx/n^2 + c = (1/n) x sin nx + (1/n^2) cos nx + c. Boxed (printed key p588).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(l); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: The general-frequency version of Q1(i); keep the two 1/a factors straight.
questions.question: Q1(m). Calculate the integral: integral of x sin(ax) dx.
questions.solution: By parts with u = x, dv = sin(ax) dx, du = dx, v = -cos(ax)/a: integral = -x cos(ax)/a + (1/a) integral cos(ax) dx = -x cos(ax)/a + sin(ax)/a^2 + c = (1/a^2) sin ax - (1/a) x cos ax + c. Boxed (printed key p588).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(m); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: Phase-shifted cosine: integrate cos(ax - b) to sin(ax - b)/a, then the leftover integrates to cos(ax - b)/a^2.
questions.question: Q1(n). Calculate the integral: integral of x cos(ax - b) dx.
questions.solution: By parts with u = x, dv = cos(ax-b) dx, du = dx, v = sin(ax-b)/a: integral = x sin(ax-b)/a - (1/a) integral sin(ax-b) dx = x sin(ax-b)/a + cos(ax-b)/a^2 + c = (1/a) x sin(ax - b) + (1/a^2) cos(ax - b) + c. Boxed (printed key p588).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(n); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: Two rounds of by parts; the first leaves integral x cos x dx, which Q1(i)-style by parts finishes.
questions.question: Q1(o). Calculate the integral: integral of x^2 sin x dx. (T.U. 2049, HSEB 2057).
questions.solution: By parts with u = x^2, dv = sin x dx, du = 2x dx, v = -cos x: integral = -x^2 cos x + 2 integral x cos x dx. For integral x cos x dx take u = x, dv = cos x dx: = x sin x - integral sin x dx = x sin x + cos x. Hence integral x^2 sin x dx = -x^2 cos x + 2x sin x + 2 cos x + c. Check: d/dx = -2x cos x + x^2 sin x + 2 sin x + 2x cos x - 2 sin x = x^2 sin x. Boxed (printed key p588).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(o); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: Same double by-parts as Q1(o) with frequency n: two factors of 1/n and one of 1/n^2 appear.
questions.question: Q1(p). Calculate the integral: integral of x^2 cos(nx) dx.
questions.solution: By parts with u = x^2, dv = cos nx dx, du = 2x dx, v = sin nx/n: integral = x^2 sin nx/n - (2/n) integral x sin nx dx. Then integral x sin nx dx = -x cos nx/n + sin nx/n^2. So the integral = x^2 sin nx/n + (2/n)(x cos nx/n - sin nx/n^2) + c = (1/n)x^2 sin nx + (2/n^2)x cos nx - (2/n^3) sin nx + c. Boxed (printed key p588).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(p); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: Phase-shifted double by-parts: v = -cos(3x-2)/3, then the linear remainder integrates twice more with factors 1/3 and 1/9.
questions.question: Q1(q). Calculate the integral: integral of x^2 sin(3x - 2) dx.
questions.solution: By parts with u = x^2, dv = sin(3x-2)dx, du = 2x dx, v = -cos(3x-2)/3: integral = -(x^2/3) cos(3x-2) + (2/3) integral x cos(3x-2) dx. Now by parts with u = x, dv = cos(3x-2)dx: integral x cos(3x-2) dx = (x/3) sin(3x-2) + (1/9) cos(3x-2). Therefore integral = -(1/3)x^2 cos(3x-2) + (2/9)x sin(3x-2) + (2/27) cos(3x-2) + c. Boxed (printed key p588).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(q); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: Linearise first: sin^2 x = (1 - cos 2x)/2 turns the integrand into x/2 minus x cos 2x/2, and only the second piece needs by parts.
questions.question: Q1(r). Calculate the integral: integral of x sin^2 x dx. (T.U. 2050 H).
questions.solution: sin^2 x = (1 - cos 2x)/2, so integral x sin^2 x dx = (1/2) integral x dx - (1/2) integral x cos 2x dx = x^2/4 - (1/2)[x sin 2x/2 + cos 2x/4] + c (by parts with u = x, dv = cos 2x dx) = (1/4)x^2 - (1/4)x sin 2x - (1/8) cos 2x + c. Boxed (printed key p588).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(r); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: Linearise cos^2 2x = (1 + cos 4x)/2 so only the cosine term needs by parts.
questions.question: Q1(s). Calculate the integral: integral of x cos^2(2x) dx.
questions.solution: cos^2(2x) = (1 + cos 4x)/2, so integral x cos^2 2x dx = (1/2) integral x dx + (1/2) integral x cos 4x dx = x^2/4 + (1/2)[x sin 4x/4 + cos 4x/16] + c = (1/4)x^2 + (1/8)x sin 4x + (1/32) cos 4x + c. Boxed (printed key p588).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(s); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: General-frequency linearisation: sin^2 nx = (1 - cos 2nx)/2, and every frequency is doubled in the by-parts piece.
questions.question: Q1(t). Calculate the integral: integral of x sin^2(nx) dx.
questions.solution: sin^2(nx) = (1 - cos 2nx)/2, so integral x sin^2 nx dx = x^2/4 - (1/2) integral x cos 2nx dx = x^2/4 - (1/2)[x sin 2nx/(2n) + cos 2nx/(4n^2)] + c = (1/4)x^2 - (1/(4n)) x sin 2nx - (1/(8n^2)) cos 2nx + c. Boxed (printed key p588).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(t); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: tan^2 = sec^2 - 1: the x sec^2 nx piece is by parts, and integral tan nx dx supplies the logarithm.
questions.question: Q1(u). Calculate the integral: integral of x tan^2(nx) dx.
questions.solution: tan^2(nx) = sec^2(nx) - 1. So integral x tan^2 nx dx = integral x sec^2(nx) dx - integral x dx. By parts with u = x, dv = sec^2(nx)dx, v = tan(nx)/n: integral x sec^2(nx) dx = x tan(nx)/n - (1/n) integral tan(nx) dx = x tan(nx)/n + log|cos nx|/n^2. Hence the answer = (1/n) x tan nx + (1/n^2) log|cos nx| - (1/2) x^2 + c. Boxed (printed key p588 prints log cos nx without modulus).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(u); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: The classic cyclic by-parts: u = sec x, dv = sec^2 x dx brings back integral sec^3 x, which is then solved algebraically.
questions.question: Q1(v). Calculate the integral: integral of sec^3 x dx. (T.U. 057) (HSEB 051).
questions.solution: Write I = integral sec^3 x dx = integral sec x sec^2 x dx. By parts with u = sec x, dv = sec^2 x dx, du = sec x tan x dx, v = tan x: I = sec x tan x - integral sec x tan^2 x dx = sec x tan x - integral sec x (sec^2 x - 1) dx = sec x tan x - I + integral sec x dx. So 2I = sec x tan x + log|sec x + tan x|, giving I = (1/2) sec x tan x + (1/2) log|sec x + tan x| + c. Boxed (printed key p588).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(v); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: Same cyclic trick with the co-function; d(cot x) = -cosec^2 x dx puts a minus sign into the recurrence.
questions.question: Q1(w). Calculate the integral: integral of cosec^3 x dx.
questions.solution: Write I = integral cosec^3 x dx = integral cosec x cosec^2 x dx. By parts with u = cosec x, dv = cosec^2 x dx, du = -cosec x cot x dx, v = -cot x: I = -cosec x cot x - integral cosec x cot^2 x dx = -cosec x cot x - integral cosec x (cosec^2 x - 1) dx = -cosec x cot x - I + integral cosec x dx. So 2I = -cosec x cot x + log|cosec x - cot x|, giving I = -(1/2) cosec x cot x + (1/2) log|cosec x - cot x| + c. Boxed (printed key p588).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(w); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: Cyclic by parts: two rounds return the original integral with a minus sign, so it is solved as an equation.
questions.question: Q1(x). Calculate the integral: integral of e^x sin x dx. (T.U. 2050).
questions.solution: Let I = integral e^x sin x dx. By parts with u = sin x, dv = e^x dx: I = e^x sin x - integral e^x cos x dx; apply by parts again to integral e^x cos x dx = e^x cos x + integral e^x sin x dx = e^x cos x + I. Therefore I = e^x sin x - e^x cos x - I, so 2I = e^x(sin x - cos x) and I = (1/2) e^x (sin x - cos x) + c. Boxed (printed key p588).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(x); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: General cyclic case: dividing by (a^2 + b^2) after two rounds is the standard result to memorise.
questions.question: Q1(y). Calculate the integral: integral of e^(ax) sin(bx) dx. (T.U. 051, 056).
questions.solution: Let I = integral e^(ax) sin(bx) dx. By parts with u = sin bx, dv = e^(ax)dx, v = e^(ax)/a: I = e^(ax) sin(bx)/a - (b/a) integral e^(ax) cos(bx) dx. By parts again on the cosine integral (u = cos bx, dv = e^(ax)dx): integral e^(ax) cos(bx) dx = e^(ax) cos(bx)/a + (b/a) I. Substituting: I = e^(ax) sin(bx)/a - (b/a)[e^(ax) cos(bx)/a + (b/a) I] = e^(ax)(a sin bx - b cos bx)/a^2 - (b^2/a^2) I. Hence I(1 + b^2/a^2) = e^(ax)(a sin bx - b cos bx)/a^2, so I = e^(ax)(a sin bx - b cos bx)/(a^2 + b^2) + c. Boxed (printed key p588).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.4 Q1(y); book p587 = PDF p614; key book p588 = PDF p615

questions.knowledgeNote: Companion of Q1(y): the sign pattern flips in the numerator (b sin bx + a cos bx).
questions.question: Q1(z). Calculate the integral: integral of e^(ax) cos(bx) dx. (T.U. 2053).
questions.solution: Let I = integral e^(ax) cos(bx) dx. By parts with u = cos bx, dv = e^(ax)dx: I = e^(ax) cos(bx)/a + (b/a) integral e^(ax) sin(bx) dx. Using integral e^(ax) sin(bx) dx = e^(ax)(a sin bx - b cos bx)/(a^2+b^2) from Q1(y): I = e^(ax) cos(bx)/a + (b/a) * e^(ax)(a sin bx - b cos bx)/(a^2+b^2) = e^(ax)[(a^2+b^2) cos bx + ab sin bx - b^2 cos bx]/[a(a^2+b^2)] = e^(ax)(a cos bx + b sin bx)/(a^2 + b^2) + c. Boxed (printed key p588 prints e^(ax)(b sin bx + a cos bx)/(a^2+b^2) + c - same expression).

questions.knowledgeNote: Definite integral of a polynomial: antiderivative first, then substitute the upper limit minus the lower limit.
questions.question: Q1. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to 1 of (x^2 + 5) dx.
questions.solution: Antiderivative: x^3/3 + 5x. Evaluate: [x^3/3 + 5x]_0^1 = (1/3 + 5) - 0 = 16/3. Numeric check: 5.333333. Final value: 16/3. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q1; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: Same rule term by term; keep the arithmetic in sixths to avoid slips.
questions.question: Q2. Evaluate the definite integral from 1 to 2 of (2x^2 + 3x + 4) dx.
questions.solution: Antiderivative: 2x^3/3 + 3x^2/2 + 4x. At x = 2: 16/3 + 6 + 8 = 16/3 + 14. At x = 1: 2/3 + 3/2 + 4 = 2/3 + 11/2. Difference: (16/3 - 2/3) + (14 - 11/2) = 14/3 + 17/2 = (28 + 51)/6 = 79/6. Numeric check: 13.166667. Final value: 79/6. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q2; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: Power rule on a linear inner function: antiderivative (x+2)^3/3, no chain factor needed since d(x+2) = dx.
questions.question: Q3. Evaluate the definite integral from -1 to 2 of (x + 2)^2 dx.
questions.solution: Antiderivative: (x+2)^3/3. Evaluate: [(x+2)^3/3]_{-1}^{2} = (4^3 - 1^3)/3 = (64 - 1)/3 = 63/3 = 21. Numeric check: 21.000000. (Same as the area under the shifted parabola over a width of 3 centred at 0.5.) Final value: 21. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q3; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: The limits run backwards here, so the answer is negative: swapping limits flips the sign of a definite integral.
questions.question: Q4. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to -1 of dx/(x + 2).
questions.solution: Antiderivative: log|x+2|. Evaluate: [log|x+2|]_0^{-1} = log 1 - log 2 = -log 2 (because 1 < 2, the value is negative, consistent with integrating backwards). Numeric check: -0.693147. Equivalently integral from -1 to 0 of dx/(x+2) = log 2. Final value: -log 2 (about -0.6931). Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q4; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: Substitution u = 1 + 2x^4 with du = 8x^3 dx, and change the limits with the variable.
questions.question: Q5. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to 1 of x^3 sqrt(1 + 2x^4) dx.
questions.solution: Let u = 1 + 2x^4, du = 8x^3 dx; when x = 0, u = 1; when x = 1, u = 3. The integral becomes (1/8) integral from 1 to 3 of u^(1/2) du = (1/8)(2/3)[u^(3/2)]_1^3 = (1/12)(3 sqrt 3 - 1). Numeric check: 0.349679. Final value: (3 sqrt 3 - 1)/12 (about 0.3497). Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q5; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: u = 2x^2 - 1 gives du = 4x dx, so the printed 2x dx is du/2; limits move to u(1) = 1 and u(2) = 7.
questions.question: Q6. Evaluate the definite integral from 1 to 2 of e^(2x^2 - 1) 2x dx.
questions.solution: Let u = 2x^2 - 1, du = 4x dx, so 2x dx = du/2. Limits: x = 1 gives u = 1; x = 2 gives u = 7. The integral = (1/2) integral from 1 to 7 of e^u du = (1/2)(e^7 - e). Numeric check: 546.957438. Final value: (e^7 - e)/2. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q6; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: u = a^2 + x^2 turns the integrand into (1/2)u^(-3/2) du; the antiderivative is -(a^2+x^2)^(-1/2).
questions.question: Q7. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to a of x dx/(a^2 + x^2)^(3/2).
questions.solution: Let u = a^2 + x^2, du = 2x dx. Antiderivative: -(a^2 + x^2)^(-1/2). Evaluate from 0 to a: -1/sqrt(a^2 + a^2) + 1/sqrt(a^2) = -1/(a sqrt 2) + 1/a = (1/a)(1 - 1/sqrt 2). Numeric check with a = 1: 0.292893. Final value: (1/a)(1 - 1/sqrt 2). Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q7; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: Logarithmic form: the numerator is exactly the derivative of the denominator.
questions.question: Q8. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to 1 of 2x dx/(x^2 + 3).
questions.solution: With u = x^2 + 3, du = 2x dx: integral = [log(x^2 + 3)]_0^1 = log 4 - log 3 = log(4/3). Numeric check: 0.287682. Final value: log(4/3). Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q8; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: Power rule after u = a^2 + x^2: the antiderivative is (a^2+x^2)^(3/2)/3.
questions.question: Q9. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to a of x sqrt(a^2 + x^2) dx.
questions.solution: With u = a^2 + x^2, du = 2x dx: antiderivative (a^2 + x^2)^(3/2)/3. Evaluate: [(a^2+x^2)^(3/2)/3]_0^a = [(2a^2)^(3/2) - (a^2)^(3/2)]/3 = [2 sqrt 2 a^3 - a^3]/3 = a^3(2 sqrt 2 - 1)/3. Numeric check with a = 1: 0.609476. Final value: a^3(2 sqrt 2 - 1)/3. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q9; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: cos t is even and the interval is symmetric, so the integral is twice the integral from 0 to pi/3.
questions.question: Q10. Evaluate the definite integral from -pi/3 to pi/3 of cos t dt. (HSEB 2057).
questions.solution: Antiderivative sin t. Evaluate: [sin t]_{-pi/3}^{pi/3} = sin(pi/3) - sin(-pi/3) = 2 sin(pi/3) = 2(sqrt 3/2) = sqrt 3. Numeric check: 1.732051. Final value: sqrt 3. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q10; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: The antiderivative of sec^2 is tan - the one direct standard form in this set.
questions.question: Q11. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to pi/4 of sec^2 theta d theta.
questions.solution: [tan theta]_0^{pi/4} = tan(pi/4) - tan 0 = 1 - 0 = 1. Numeric check: 1.000000. Final value: 1. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q11; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: Linearise the square before integrating: cos^2 u = (1 + cos 2u)/2.
questions.question: Q12. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to 1 of cos^2(pi x) dx.
questions.solution: cos^2(pi x) = (1 + cos 2 pi x)/2, so the integral = [x/2 + sin(2 pi x)/(4 pi)]_0^1 = (1/2 + 0) - 0 = 1/2. The cosine term vanishes because its period 1 fits exactly in [0,1]. Numeric check: 0.500000. Final value: 1/2. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q12; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: Linearise: sin^2 x = (1 - cos 2x)/2, then the cosine term integrates to -sin 2x/4.
questions.question: Q13. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to pi/4 of sin^2 x dx.
questions.solution: [x/2 - sin 2x/4]_0^{pi/4} = pi/8 - sin(pi/2)/4 = pi/8 - 1/4 = (pi - 2)/8. Numeric check: 0.142699. Final value: (pi - 2)/8. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q13; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: Odd power of cosine: split cos^3 = (1 - sin^2)cos and substitute u = sin x.
questions.question: Q14. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to pi/6 of cos^3 x dx.
questions.solution: cos^3 x = (1 - sin^2 x) cos x, so the antiderivative is sin x - sin^3 x/3. Evaluate from 0 to pi/6: (1/2 - (1/2)^3/3) - 0 = 1/2 - 1/24 = 12/24 - 1/24 = 11/24. Numeric check: 0.458333. Final value: 11/24. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q14; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: Same odd-power trick for sine: sin^3 = (1 - cos^2) sin, antiderivative -cos x + cos^3 x/3.
questions.question: Q15. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to pi/2 of sin^3 x dx.
questions.solution: Antiderivative: -cos x + cos^3 x/3. At pi/2 both cosine terms vanish; at 0 the value is -1 + 1/3 = -2/3. So the integral = 0 - (-2/3) = 2/3. (Consistent with Wallis' formula integral of sin^3 over a quarter period = 2/3.) Numeric check: 0.666667. Final value: 2/3. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q15; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: Multiply by the conjugate (1 - cos x): the integrand becomes cosec^2 x - cosec x cot x, whose antiderivative is tan(x/2).
questions.question: Q16. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to pi/3 of dx/(1 + cos x).
questions.solution: Multiply numerator and denominator by (1 - cos x): 1/(1+cos x) = (1 - cos x)/(1 - cos^2 x) = (1 - cos x)/sin^2 x = cosec^2 x - cosec x cot x. Antiderivative: -cot x + cosec x = (1 - cos x)/sin x = tan(x/2). Evaluate: tan(pi/6) - tan 0 = 1/sqrt 3. Numeric check: 0.577350. Final value: 1/sqrt 3. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q16; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: Use 1 - cos 2x = 2 sin^2 x, whose reciprocal integrates to -cot x/2; the descending limits make the result negative.
questions.question: Q17. Evaluate the definite integral from pi/2 to pi/6 of dx/(1 - cos 2x).
questions.solution: 1 - cos 2x = 2 sin^2 x, so the integrand is (1/2)cosec^2 x and the antiderivative is -(1/2)cot x. Evaluate from pi/2 to pi/6: -(1/2)[cot(pi/6) - cot(pi/2)] = -(1/2)[sqrt 3 - 0] = -sqrt 3/2. Numeric check: -0.866025. (The function is positive everywhere but the limits are descending, so the value is negative by definition.) Final value: -sqrt 3/2. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q17; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: Multiply by (1 + sin x): the integrand splits into sec^2 x + sec x tan x, both immediate standard forms.
questions.question: Q18. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to pi/4 of dx/(1 - sin x). (T.U. 2051).
questions.solution: Multiply numerator and denominator by (1 + sin x): 1/(1 - sin x) = (1 + sin x)/(1 - sin^2 x) = (1 + sin x)/cos^2 x = sec^2 x + sec x tan x. Antiderivative: tan x + sec x. Evaluate: [tan x + sec x]_0^{pi/4} = (1 + sqrt 2) - (0 + 1) = sqrt 2. Numeric check: 1.414214. Final value: sqrt 2. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q18; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: A line through the origin: the sum of the first n natural numbers produces the n(n+1)/2 factor.
questions.question: Q1. Find the area of the plane region bounded by y = x, from x = 0 to x = a and the x-axis, using the limit of a sum.
questions.solution: h = a/n, so nh = a and the sample points are x = ih. Divide [0, L] into n equal parts of width h = L/n; the area is A = lim(n->inf) h [f(h) + f(2h) + ... + f(nh)] (right-endpoint rectangles), then use the standard sums 1+2+...+n = n(n+1)/2 and 1^2+2^2+...+n^2 = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6. Here f(x) = x, so A = lim(n->inf) h [h + 2h + ... + nh] = lim h^2 (1 + 2 + ... + n) = lim (a^2/n^2) * n(n+1)/2 = (a^2/2) lim (1 + 1/n) = a^2/2. Boxed (printed key p598). Geometric cross-check: a right triangle with legs a and a has area a^2/2.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.6 Q1; book p597 = PDF p624; key book p598 = PDF p625

questions.knowledgeNote: Constant multiple of Q1's integrand: the 4 comes straight out of the limit.
questions.question: Q2. Find the area of the plane region bounded by y = 4x, from x = 0 to x = a and the x-axis, using the limit of a sum.
questions.solution: h = a/n. A = lim(n->inf) h [4h + 4(2h) + ... + 4(nh)] = 4h^2 (1 + 2 + ... + n) -> 4 * (a^2/2) = 2a^2. Boxed (printed key p598). Cross-check: triangle with base a and height 4a has area 2a^2.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.6 Q2; book p597 = PDF p624; key book p598 = PDF p625

questions.knowledgeNote: A decreasing line: the sum splits into h*n (the constant part) minus the arithmetic-sum part.
questions.question: Q3. Find the area of the plane region bounded by y = 1 - x, from x = 0 to x = b and the x-axis, using the limit of a sum.
questions.solution: h = b/n. A = lim(n->inf) h [(1 - h) + (1 - 2h) + ... + (1 - nh)] = lim h [n - h(1 + 2 + ... + n)] = lim [nh - h^2 n(n+1)/2] = b - (b^2/2) lim (1 + 1/n) = b - b^2/2. Boxed (printed key p598). Cross-check (for 0 < b <= 1): a trapezium with parallel sides 1 and 1-b over width b, area b(2-b)/2 = b - b^2/2.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.6 Q3; book p597 = PDF p624; key book p598 = PDF p625

questions.knowledgeNote: A parabola: the sum of squares 1^2 + ... + n^2 = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6 supplies the 2/6 = 1/3 factor.
questions.question: Q4. Find the area of the plane region bounded by y = 4x^2, from x = 0 to x = c and the x-axis, using the limit of a sum.
questions.solution: h = c/n. A = lim(n->inf) h [4h^2 + 4(2h)^2 + ... + 4(nh)^2] = 4h^3 (1^2 + 2^2 + ... + n^2) = 4h^3 * n(n+1)(2n+1)/6 = (4c^3/6)(1 + 1/n)(2 + 1/n) -> (4c^3/6)(1)(2) = 4c^3/3. Boxed (printed key p598). This is exactly integral 0 to c of 4x^2 dx = 4c^3/3, which is the point of the section.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.6 Q4; book p597 = PDF p624; key book p598 = PDF p625

questions.knowledgeNote: Q4 with the constant 4a in place of 4 and the upper limit named a as well - keep the two roles of a apart.
questions.question: Q5. Find the area of the plane region bounded by y = 4ax^2, from x = 0 to x = a and the x-axis, using the limit of a sum.
questions.solution: h = a/n. A = lim(n->inf) h [4a h^2 + 4a(2h)^2 + ... + 4a(nh)^2] = 4a h^3 * n(n+1)(2n+1)/6 = (4a * a^3/6)(1 + 1/n)(2 + 1/n) -> (4a^4/6)(2) = 4a^4/3. Boxed (printed key p598). Equivalent to integral 0 to a of 4ax^2 dx = 4a^4/3.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.6 Q5; book p597 = PDF p624; key book p598 = PDF p625

questions.knowledgeNote: Geometric series instead of power sums: the sum of e^(ih) is a finite G.P. whose limit produces (e^a - 1).
questions.question: Q6. Find the area of the plane region bounded by y = e^x, from x = 0 to x = a and the x-axis, using the limit of a sum.
questions.solution: h = a/n. A = lim(n->inf) h [e^h + e^(2h) + ... + e^(nh)]. The bracket is a G.P. with first term e^h and ratio e^h, so it equals e^h (e^(nh) - 1)/(e^h - 1). Hence A = lim h e^h (e^a - 1)/(e^h - 1) = (e^a - 1) * lim [e^h * h/(e^h - 1)] = (e^a - 1) * 1 * 1 = e^a - 1, using lim(h->0) (e^h - 1)/h = 1. Boxed (printed key p598).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.6 Q6; book p597 = PDF p624; key book p598 = PDF p625

questions.knowledgeNote: Same G.P. limit with ratio e^(3h); the h/(e^(3h)-1) factor leaves the 1/3.
questions.question: Q7. Find the area of the plane region bounded by y = e^(3x), from x = 0 to x = b and the x-axis, using the limit of a sum.

questions.knowledgeNote: Solve for y first: the only y on a parabola of this form is the positive square-root-free branch, so the area is a plain power integral.
questions.question: Find the area bounded by the x-axis, the curve x^2 = 4by and the ordinates x = a and x = b.
questions.solution: From x^2 = 4by, y = x^2/(4b). Area = integral from a to b of x^2/(4b) dx = (1/(4b))[x^3/3]_a^b = (b^3 - a^3)/(12b). Boxed (printed key p605: (b^3 - a^3)/12b). Positive when b > a > 0, otherwise the integral is negative and its modulus is the area.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q1(a); book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: Pure power rule; the whole curve is above the x-axis on [2,4] so no sign correction is needed.
questions.question: Find the area bounded by the x-axis, the curve y = 4x^3 and the ordinates x = 2 and x = 4.
questions.solution: Area = integral from 2 to 4 of 4x^3 dx = [x^4]_2^4 = 256 - 16 = 240. Boxed (printed key p605).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q1(b); book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: A parabola whose root is at x = sqrt(2/3) < 1, so the whole interval [1,4] lies above the axis and the integral is the area directly.
questions.question: Find the area bounded by the x-axis, the curve y = 3x^2 - 2 and the ordinates x = 1 and x = 4.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q1(c); book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: Take the positive branch y = sqrt(x+4); the radical integrates by the power rule with exponent 1/2.
questions.question: Find the area bounded by the x-axis, the curve y^2 - x - 4 = 0 and the ordinates x = 2 and x = 5.
questions.solution: The curve is y^2 = x + 4, so above the axis y = sqrt(x+4). Area = integral from 2 to 5 of (x+4)^(1/2) dx = (2/3)[(x+4)^(3/2)]_2^5 = (2/3)(9^(3/2) - 6^(3/2)) = (2/3)(27 - 6 sqrt 6) = 18 - 4 sqrt 6 = 2(9 - 2 sqrt 6). Boxed (printed key p605).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q1(d); book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: Exponential with a linear exponent: the antiderivative is e^(ax)/a.
questions.question: Find the area bounded by the x-axis, the curve y = e^(ax) and the ordinates x = b and x = c. (HSEB 2050, 2052)
questions.solution: Area = integral from b to c of e^(ax) dx = (1/a)[e^(ax)]_b^c = (1/a)(e^(ca) - e^(ba)). Boxed (printed key p605).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q1(e); book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: Integral of a logarithm is a by-parts standard form: integral log u du = u log u - u.
questions.question: Find the area bounded by the x-axis, the curve y = log(1 + x) and the ordinates x = 0 and x = 1.
questions.solution: Substitute u = 1 + x (du = dx, limits 1 to 2): area = integral from 1 to 2 of log u du = [u log u - u]_1^2 = (2 log 2 - 2) - (0 - 1) = 2 log 2 - 1. Boxed (printed key p605).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q1(f); book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: The 'ordinate at the point' means the x-coordinate of that point, x = 4a; take the upper branch y = sqrt(8ax).
questions.question: Find the area bounded by the x-axis, the curve y^2 = 8ax and the ordinate at the point (4a, 0).
questions.solution: Since (4a, 0) lies on the curve, the ordinate is x = 4a. Area = integral from 0 to 4a of sqrt(8ax) dx = sqrt(8a) * (2/3)[x^(3/2)]_0^{4a} = sqrt(8a) * (2/3)(4a)^(3/2) = sqrt(8a) * (2/3) * 8a^(3/2) = (2/3) * 8 * 2 sqrt 2 * a^2 = (32 sqrt 2/3) a^2. Boxed (printed key p605).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q2(i); book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: The parabola has vertex (a, 0), so the integration starts at a - the width of the region is (h - a).
questions.question: Find the area bounded by the x-axis, the curve y^2 = 4a(x - a) and the ordinate at the point (h, k).
questions.solution: The point (h, k) satisfies k^2 = 4a(h - a), so its ordinate is x = h and h >= a. Area = integral from a to h of sqrt(4a(x-a)) dx = 2 sqrt a * (2/3)[(x-a)^(3/2)]_a^h = (4/3) sqrt a (h - a)^(3/2). Boxed (printed key p605).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q2(ii); book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: Same parabola as Q1(a) with the upper limit fixed at x = b.
questions.question: Find the area bounded by the x-axis, the curve x^2 = 4by and the ordinate at the point (b, 0).
questions.solution: From x^2 = 4by, y = x^2/(4b); the ordinate through (b,0) is x = b. Area = integral from 0 to b of x^2/(4b) dx = (1/(4b))(b^3/3) = b^2/12. Boxed (printed key p605).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q2(iii); book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: Factor to find the limits: x(3 - 5x) = 0 gives 0 and 3/5, the two points where the curve meets the axis.
questions.question: Find the area enclosed by the x-axis and the curve y = 3x - 5x^2. (HSEB 2055)
questions.solution: Solving 3x - 5x^2 = 0 gives x = 0 and x = 3/5. Area = integral from 0 to 3/5 of (3x - 5x^2) dx = [3x^2/2 - 5x^3/3]_0^{3/5} = 27/50 - 27/75 = 27/50 - 18/50 = 9/50. Boxed (printed key p605).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q3(i); book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: Symmetric interval: integrate from 0 to 5 and double, since the integrand is even.
questions.question: Find the area enclosed by the x-axis and the curve y = x^2 - 25.
questions.solution: Roots at x = +-5, and the parabola lies below the axis between them. Area = integral from -5 to 5 of (25 - x^2) dx = 2[25x - x^3/3]_0^5 = 2(125 - 125/3) = 2(250/3) = 500/3 = 166 2/3. Boxed (printed key p605: 166 2/3).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q3(iv); book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: A cubic with three simple roots changes sign at each: the total enclosed area is the sum of the absolute values of the pieces.
questions.question: Find the area enclosed by the x-axis and the curve y = (x - 1)(x - 2)(x - 3).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q3(v); book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: Subtract the two y-values between the intersection abscissae; the parabola wins near 0, the line near 1, and they cross at 4.
questions.question: Find the area of the region between the curve y^2 = 16x and the line y = 2x. (HSEB 2053, 056)
questions.solution: Intersections: (2x)^2 = 16x gives 4x^2 = 16x, so x = 0 and x = 4 (y = 0 and 8). Between them the parabola's upper branch y = 4 sqrt x lies above y = 2x. Area = integral from 0 to 4 of (4 sqrt x - 2x) dx = [4(2/3)x^(3/2) - x^2]_0^4 = (8/3)(8) - 16 = 64/3 - 16 = 16/3 = 5 1/3. Boxed (printed key p605: 5 1/3).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q4(i); book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: Integrating with respect to y avoids splitting the parabola into branches: right curve minus left curve, dy.
questions.question: Find the area of the region between the curve y^2 = 4x and the line x = y.
questions.solution: x = y is the same as y = x, and y^2 = 4x gives x = y^2/4. They meet where y = y^2/4, i.e. y = 0 and y = 4. Area = integral from 0 to 4 of (y - y^2/4) dy = [y^2/2 - y^3/12]_0^4 = 8 - 64/12 = 8 - 16/3 = 8/3 = 2 2/3. Boxed (printed key p605: 2 2/3).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q4(ii); book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: The chord is vertical, so y is the natural variable; the region is symmetric about the x-axis.
questions.question: Find the area of the region between the curve y^2 = 4ax and the line x = a.
questions.solution: At x = a the parabola gives y^2 = 4a^2, so y = +-2a. For a fixed y the region runs from x = y^2/(4a) to x = a. Area = integral from -2a to 2a of (a - y^2/(4a)) dy = [ay - y^3/(12a)]_{-2a}^{2a} = (2a^2 - 8a^3/(12a)) - (-2a^2 + 8a^3/(12a)) = (2a^2 - 2a^2/3) + (2a^2 - 2a^2/3) = 8a^2/3. Boxed (printed key p605).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q4(iii); book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: x = y is the line y = x; two intersections 0 and 1, and a quick test point (x = 1/2) shows which curve is on top.
questions.question: Find the area of the region between the curve y = x^3 and the line x = y lying in the first quadrant.
questions.solution: Intersections: x^3 = x, so x = 0 and x = 1 (first quadrant). At x = 1/2 the line gives 1/2 and the cubic 1/8, so the line is above. Area = integral from 0 to 1 of (x - x^3) dx = [x^2/2 - x^4/4]_0^1 = 1/2 - 1/4 = 1/4. Boxed (printed key p605).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q4(iv); book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: y^2 = x^3 gives the two branches y = +-x^(3/2) for x >= 0; the region between them is symmetric.
questions.question: Find the area of the region between the curve y^2 = x^3 and the line x = 4.
questions.solution: For x in [0,4] the curve has y = +-x^(3/2), meeting x = 4 at y = +-8. Area = 2 integral from 0 to 4 of x^(3/2) dx = 2 * (2/5)[x^(5/2)]_0^4 = (4/5)(32) = 128/5 = 25 3/5. Boxed (printed key p605: 25 3/5).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q4(v); book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: Two parabolas, one opening sideways and one upwards; solve simultaneously to get the second intersection x = 4a.
questions.question: Find the area of the region between the curves y^2 = 4ax and x^2 = 4ay. (HSEB 2058)
questions.solution: Substituting x = y^2/(4a) into x^2 = 4ay gives y^4/(16a^2) = 4ay, so y^3 = 64a^3 and y = 4a; the points are (0,0) and (4a, 4a). On (0, 4a) the upper curve is y = 2 sqrt(ax). Area = integral from 0 to 4a of (2 sqrt(ax) - x^2/(4a)) dx = [2 sqrt a (2/3)x^(3/2) - x^3/(12a)]_0^{4a} = (4/3) sqrt a (4a)^(3/2) - (64a^3)/(12a) = (4/3)(8a^2) - 16a^2/3 = (32/3)a^2 - (16/3)a^2 = 16a^2/3. Boxed (printed key p605).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q4(vi); book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: For a circle the integral reproduces pi r^2; the substitution x = r sin theta is the clean way to see the pi appear.
questions.question: Find the area of the circle x^2 + y^2 = 16.
questions.solution: Radius r = 4, centre the origin, so the area is pi r^2 = 16 pi. Derivation: area = 2 integral from -4 to 4 of sqrt(16 - x^2) dx; with x = 4 sin theta, dx = 4 cos theta d theta and limits +-pi/2, this is 2 * 16 integral cos^2 theta d theta = 32 * (pi/2) = 16 pi. Boxed (printed key p605).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q5(i); book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: The same computation with r = a: the answer is the standard circle-area formula pi a^2.
questions.question: Find the area of the circle x^2 + y^2 = a^2.
questions.solution: Radius a. Area = 2 integral from -a to a of sqrt(a^2 - x^2) dx = 2 * (pi a^2/2) = pi a^2 (using x = a sin theta, integral of cos^2 over [-pi/2, pi/2] = pi/2). Boxed (printed key p605).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q5(ii); book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: Four quarters by symmetry, then the circle-type substitution x = a sin theta: the result is the classic pi ab.
questions.question: Find the area of the ellipse x^2/a^2 + y^2/b^2 = 1.
questions.solution: By symmetry the area is 4 times the first-quadrant part, where y = (b/a) sqrt(a^2 - x^2). So area = 4(b/a) integral from 0 to a of sqrt(a^2 - x^2) dx. With x = a sin theta, dx = a cos theta d theta and limits 0 to pi/2: integral = a^2 integral cos^2 theta d theta = a^2 (pi/4). Therefore area = 4(b/a)(a^2 pi/4) = pi ab. Boxed (printed key p605).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q6; book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: The point (h,k) on the curve fixes the vertical line x = h; the lower boundary is the x-axis, the upper boundary the shifted parabola.
questions.question: Find the area bounded by the axes of coordinates, the curve x^2 = 4a(y - 2a) and the ordinate at the point (h, k).
questions.solution: From x^2 = 4a(y - 2a), y = x^2/(4a) + 2a: a parabola with vertex (0, 2a) opening upwards. The region is bounded by the x-axis, the y-axis (x = 0) and the ordinate x = h through (h, k). Area = integral from 0 to h of (x^2/(4a) + 2a) dx = h^3/(12a) + 2ah = (h/(12a))(h^2 + 24a^2). Boxed (printed key p605).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q7; book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: The y-axis is one boundary, so integrate x as a function of y: x = 2 sqrt(by).
questions.question: Find the area bounded by the y-axis, the curve x^2 = 4by and y = b.
questions.solution: From x^2 = 4by, x = 2 sqrt(by) for x >= 0. The region lies between the y-axis (x = 0) and the curve, from y = 0 to y = b. Area = integral from 0 to b of 2 sqrt(by) dy = 2 sqrt b * (2/3)[y^(3/2)]_0^b = (4/3) sqrt b * b^(3/2) = 4b^2/3. Boxed (printed key p605).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q8; book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: The parabola's vertex is at y = 2a, so the region starts there and runs up to y = 6a; x = 2 sqrt(a(y-2a)).
questions.question: Find the area bounded by the y-axis, the curve x^2 = 4a(y - 2a) and y = 6a.
questions.solution: From x^2 = 4a(y - 2a), x = 2 sqrt(a(y - 2a)) with vertex (0, 2a). Area = integral from 2a to 6a of 2 sqrt(a(y - 2a)) dy = 2 sqrt a * (2/3)[(y - 2a)^(3/2)]_{2a}^{6a} = (4/3) sqrt a (4a)^(3/2) = (4/3) sqrt a * 8a^(3/2) = 32a^2/3. Boxed (printed key p605).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q9; book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: For a parametric curve, area = integral y (dx/dt) dt between the parameter values - here the limits are given directly as t = 0 and t = 1.
questions.question: Find the area bounded by the x-axis, the curve x = at^2, y = 2at and the ordinates corresponding to t = 0 to t = 1.
questions.solution: x = at^2 gives dx = 2at dt, and y = 2at. Area = integral from t = 0 to 1 of y dx = integral from 0 to 1 of (2at)(2at) dt = 4a^2 integral t^2 dt = 4a^2/3. Boxed (printed key p605).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.7 Q10; book p604-605 = PDF p631-632; key book p605 = PDF p632

questions.knowledgeNote: Antiderivative = any function whose derivative returns the given function; the +c family is the whole answer set of an indefinite integral.
questions.question: AQ1. What is an antiderivative? Is it true that there are a number of antiderivatives of a function which differ from one another only by a constant? Show this relation by taking an example.
questions.solution: An antiderivative (primitive) of f on an interval is a function F with F'(x) = f(x) for every x in the interval. Yes, the statement is true: if F is one antiderivative then F + c is another for every constant c, and conversely any two antiderivatives of the same f on an interval differ by a constant - because (F - G)' = f - f = 0, and a function with zero derivative on an interval is constant (mean value theorem). Example: for f(x) = 3x^2, the functions x^3, x^3 + 5, x^3 - 7 and in general x^3 + c all differentiate to 3x^2, and any two of them differ only by a constant. That is exactly why the indefinite integral is written integral 3x^2 dx = x^3 + c. Boxed (printed book p605, theory).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ1; book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Indefinite integral = a family of functions (the antiderivatives); definite integral = one number, the signed area, and the two are linked by the fundamental theorem.
questions.question: AQ2. What does an indefinite integral mean? How does it differ from a definite integral? What does integral from a to b of f(x) dx represent?
questions.solution: The indefinite integral integral f(x) dx denotes the whole family of antiderivatives of f, i.e. F(x) + c where F' = f; its value is a function (plus an arbitrary constant). The definite integral integral from a to b of f(x) dx is a single real number computed as F(b) - F(a) for any antiderivative F; the arbitrary constant cancels, so the answer does not depend on which antiderivative is chosen. Geometrically, integral from a to b of f(x) dx represents the signed area between the graph of y = f(x), the x-axis, and the vertical lines x = a and x = b: area above the axis counts positive, area below counts negative, and the two cancel where the curve changes sign. The link between the two notions is the fundamental theorem of calculus: d/dx integral from a to x of f(t) dt = f(x). Boxed (printed book p605, theory).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ2; book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Expand the cube with the binomial theorem, then integrate term by term; the x^(-2) term is the only one needing the power rule with a negative exponent.
questions.question: AQ3(i). Evaluate: integral of (x + 1/x)^3 dx.
questions.solution: Expand: (x + 1/x)^3 = x^3 + 3x + 3/x + 1/x^3. Integrate term by term: x^4/4 + 3x^2/2 + 3 log|x| + x^(-2)/(-2) + c = x^4/4 + 3x^2/2 + 3 log x - 1/(2x^2) + c. Boxed (printed key p607).

questions.knowledgeNote: Substitute u = 6x + 8 and rewrite the linear factor 2x + 3 in terms of u: it becomes (u + 1)/3.
questions.question: AQ3(ii). Evaluate: integral of (2x + 3)(6x + 8)^5 dx.
questions.solution: Let u = 6x + 8, so x = (u - 8)/6, dx = du/6 and 2x + 3 = (u - 8)/3 + 3 = (u + 1)/3. The integral becomes (1/18) integral (u + 1) u^5 du = (1/18)(u^7/7 + u^6/6) = u^6(6u + 7)/756. Back-substituting 6u + 7 = 6(6x + 8) + 7 = 36x + 55 gives (1/756)(36x + 55)(6x + 8)^6 + c. Boxed (printed key p607).

questions.knowledgeNote: Factor both differences with the sum-to-product formulas; nearly everything cancels and 2(cos x + cos alpha) is left.
questions.question: AQ3(iv). Evaluate: integral of (cos 2x - cos 2alpha)/(cos x - cos alpha) dx.
questions.solution: cos 2x - cos 2alpha = -2 sin(x + alpha) sin(x - alpha) and cos x - cos alpha = -2 sin((x+alpha)/2) sin((x-alpha)/2). The ratio is [2 sin(x+alpha) sin(x-alpha)]/[2 sin((x+alpha)/2) sin((x-alpha)/2)] = 4 cos((x+alpha)/2) cos((x-alpha)/2) = 2(cos x + cos alpha), using sin 2t = 2 sin t cos t twice and 2 cos A cos B = cos(A+B) + cos(A-B). Hence the integral = 2(sin x + x cos alpha) + c. Boxed (printed key p607).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ3(iv); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Both lines collapse by sum-to-product: the numerator is 2 sin x sin alpha and the denominator 2 sin x cos alpha.
questions.question: AQ3(v). Evaluate: integral of [cos(x - alpha) - cos(x + alpha)]/[sin(x + alpha) + sin(x - alpha)] dx.
questions.solution: cos(x - alpha) - cos(x + alpha) = 2 sin x sin alpha and sin(x + alpha) + sin(x - alpha) = 2 sin x cos alpha. The quotient is therefore tan alpha - a constant - so the integral is x tan alpha + c. Boxed (printed key p607).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ3(v); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: The numerator is a difference of squares: e^(2x) - 1 = (e^x - 1)(e^x + 1), so the fraction cancels to e^x - 1.
questions.question: AQ3(vi). Evaluate: integral of (e^(2x) - 1)/(e^x + 1) dx.
questions.solution: (e^(2x) - 1)/(e^x + 1) = (e^x - 1)(e^x + 1)/(e^x + 1) = e^x - 1. Hence the integral = e^x - x + c. Boxed (printed key p607).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ3(vi); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Multiply by (sec x - tan x) so the denominator becomes sec^2 - tan^2 = 1; the result is 1/(1 + sin x) = sec^2 x - sec x tan x.
questions.question: AQ3(vii). Evaluate: integral of sec x/(sec x + tan x) dx.
questions.solution: Multiply numerator and denominator by (sec x - tan x): sec x(sec x - tan x)/(sec^2 x - tan^2 x) = sec^2 x - sec x tan x. Both terms are immediate derivatives: integral = tan x - sec x + c. Boxed (printed key p607).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ3(vii); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Split the fraction term by term: sin^3/(sin^2 cos^2) = sin/cos^2 = sec x tan x, and cos^3/(sin^2 cos^2) = cos/sin^2 = -d(cosec x)/dx.
questions.question: AQ3(viii). Evaluate: integral of (a sin^3 x + b cos^3 x)/(sin^2 x cos^2 x) dx.
questions.solution: (a sin^3 x)/(sin^2 x cos^2 x) = a sin x/cos^2 x = a sec x tan x, whose integral is a sec x. (b cos^3 x)/(sin^2 x cos^2 x) = b cos x/sin^2 x, whose integral is -b cosec x. Hence the answer is a sec x - b cosec x + c. Boxed (printed key p607).

questions.knowledgeNote: Put u = sqrt(3x + 1) (so x = (u^2 - 1)/3) - the square root disappears and a plain polynomial in u remains.
questions.question: AQ4(i). Evaluate: integral of (2x + 3)/sqrt(3x + 1) dx. (T.U. 2048).
questions.solution: Let u = sqrt(3x + 1); then 3x + 1 = u^2, x = (u^2 - 1)/3, dx = 2u du/3 and 2x + 3 = (2u^2 + 7)/3. The integral = integral [(2u^2 + 7)/3](2u du/3)/u = (2/9) integral (2u^2 + 7) du = (2/9)(2u^3/3 + 7u) = (2/27) u (2u^2 + 21). Since 2u^2 + 21 = 2(3x + 1) + 21 = 6x + 23, the answer is (2/27)(6x + 23) sqrt(3x + 1) + c. Boxed (printed key p607).

questions.question: AQ4(v). Evaluate: integral of tan^3 x sec^4 x dx. (T.U. 2051).
questions.solution: Let u = tan x, du = sec^2 x dx and sec^4 x = (1 + u^2)^2. The integral = integral u^3 (1 + u^2) du = u^4/4 + u^6/6 + c = tan^4 x/4 + tan^6 x/6 + c. Boxed (printed key p607).

questions.knowledgeNote: Rationalise the denominator: the product of the conjugates is the constant a + b, which pulls out of the integral.
questions.question: AQ4(viii). Evaluate: integral of dx/[sqrt(3x + a) - sqrt(3x - b)]. (HSEB 2050).
questions.solution: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate (sqrt(3x+a) + sqrt(3x-b)): the denominator becomes (3x + a) - (3x - b) = a + b, a constant. So the integral = (1/(a+b)) integral [sqrt(3x + a) + sqrt(3x - b)] dx = (1/(a+b))[(2/9)(3x + a)^(3/2) + (2/9)(3x - b)^(3/2)] + c = (2/(9(a+b)))[(3x + a)^(3/2) + (3x - b)^(3/2)] + c. Boxed (printed key p608).

questions.question: AQ5(i). Evaluate: integral of (1 - sin x)/(x + cos x) dx.
questions.solution: d/dx (x + cos x) = 1 - sin x, so with u = x + cos x the integral is integral du/u = log|x + cos x| + c. Boxed (printed key p608).

questions.knowledgeNote: The numerator is the derivative of the denominator, so the answer is a single logarithm (this is the integral of tanh x).
questions.question: AQ5(ii). Evaluate: integral of (e^x - e^(-x))/(e^x + e^(-x)) dx.
questions.solution: d/dx (e^x + e^(-x)) = e^x - e^(-x), so the integral = log(e^x + e^(-x)) + c (the quantity is positive, so no modulus is needed). Boxed (printed key p608).

questions.knowledgeNote: d(x e^x) = e^x(1 + x) dx, so the integrand is sec^2 u du with u = x e^x.
questions.question: AQ5(iii). Evaluate: integral of e^x (1 + x)/cos^2(x e^x) dx.
questions.solution: Let u = x e^x; then du = (e^x + x e^x) dx = e^x(1 + x) dx. The integral = integral sec^2 u du = tan u + c = tan(x e^x) + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ5(iii); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Note (x + 1)/x = 1 + 1/x = d(x + log x)/dx: the whole integrand is u^3 du.
questions.question: AQ5(iv). Evaluate: integral of (x + 1)(x + log x)^3/x dx.
questions.solution: Let u = x + log x; then du = (1 + 1/x) dx = (x + 1)/x dx. The integral = integral u^3 du = u^4/4 + c = (x + log x)^4/4 + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ5(iv); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Multiply top and bottom by e^x: the integrand becomes e^x/(1 + e^x), whose derivative is the denominator.
questions.question: AQ5(v). Evaluate: integral of dx/(1 + e^(-x)).
questions.solution: 1/(1 + e^(-x)) = e^x/(1 + e^x). With u = 1 + e^x, du = e^x dx, the integral = log(1 + e^x) + c. Boxed (printed key p608). Equivalent form: x - log(1 + e^x) + c.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ5(v); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: The denominator's derivative is 2(b - a) sin x cos x, so the answer is a logarithm divided by that constant.
questions.question: AQ5(vi). Evaluate: integral of sin x cos x dx/(a cos^2 x + b sin^2 x).
questions.solution: Let u = a cos^2 x + b sin^2 x. Then du = (-2a cos x sin x + 2b sin x cos x) dx = 2(b - a) sin x cos x dx, so sin x cos x dx = du/(2(b - a)). The integral = (1/(2(b - a))) log|a cos^2 x + b sin^2 x| + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ5(vi); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: d(cos^2 x) = -sin 2x dx, so the minus sign of the substitution lands in front of the exponential.
questions.question: AQ5(vii). Evaluate: integral of e^(cos^2 x) sin 2x dx.
questions.solution: Let u = cos^2 x; du = -2 sin x cos x dx = -sin 2x dx. The integral = -integral e^u du = -e^u + c = -e^(cos^2 x) + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ5(vii); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: d(e^(x^2)) = 2x e^(x^2) dx: the whole coefficient is the inner derivative, leaving sec^2 u du.
questions.question: AQ5(viii). Evaluate: integral of 2x e^(x^2) sec^2(e^(x^2)) dx.
questions.solution: Let u = e^(x^2); du = 2x e^(x^2) dx. The integral = integral sec^2 u du = tan u + c = tan(e^(x^2)) + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ5(viii); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: u = e^(sqrt x) with du = e^(sqrt x) dx/(2 sqrt x); then tan^2 u = sec^2 u - 1 gives two immediate integrals.
questions.question: AQ5(ix). Evaluate: integral of e^(sqrt x) tan^2(e^(sqrt x))/(2 sqrt x) dx.
questions.solution: Let u = e^(sqrt x); du = e^(sqrt x) * (1/(2 sqrt x)) dx, exactly the factor present. The integral = integral tan^2 u du = integral (sec^2 u - 1) du = tan u - u + c = tan(e^(sqrt x)) - e^(sqrt x) + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ5(ix); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Write the denominator as tan x cos^2 x: the integrand becomes (tan x)^(-1/2) sec^2 x dx, i.e. u^(-1/2) du.
questions.question: AQ5(x). Evaluate: integral of sqrt(tan x)/(sin x cos x) dx.
questions.solution: sqrt(tan x)/(sin x cos x) = sqrt(tan x)/(tan x cos^2 x) = (tan x)^(-1/2) sec^2 x. With u = tan x, du = sec^2 x dx: the integral = integral u^(-1/2) du = 2 sqrt u + c = 2 sqrt(tan x) + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ5(x); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Half-angle form: 1 + cos x = 2cos^2(x/2) and 1 + sin x = 1 + 2 sin(x/2)cos(x/2), giving sec^2(x/2)/2 plus tan(x/2).
questions.question: AQ5(xi). Evaluate: integral of (1 + sin x)/(1 + cos x) dx.
questions.solution: 1 + cos x = 2 cos^2(x/2) and sin x = 2 sin(x/2) cos(x/2), so the integrand = 1/(2cos^2(x/2)) + sin(x/2)/cos(x/2) = (1/2) sec^2(x/2) + tan(x/2). Integrate: tan(x/2) - 2 log|cos(x/2)| + c. Since 2 cos^2(x/2) = 1 + cos x, 2 log cos(x/2) = log(1 + cos x) - log 2, so the answer is tan(x/2) - log(1 + cos x) + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ5(xi); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Split the numerator by the angle-addition formula: sin x = sin((x - alpha) + alpha) = sin(x-alpha)cos alpha + cos(x-alpha) sin alpha.
questions.question: AQ5(xii). Evaluate: integral of sin x dx/sin(x - alpha).
questions.solution: sin x = sin(x - alpha) cos alpha + cos(x - alpha) sin alpha, so sin x/sin(x - alpha) = cos alpha + sin alpha * cot(x - alpha). The integral is therefore x cos alpha + sin alpha log|sin(x - alpha)| + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ5(xii); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Multiply by e^(-x)/e^(-x): the integrand becomes e^(-x)/(1 + e^(-x)), whose denominator has derivative -e^(-x).
questions.question: AQ5(xiii). Evaluate: integral of dx/(1 + e^x).
questions.solution: 1/(1 + e^x) = e^(-x)/(e^(-x) + 1). With u = 1 + e^(-x), du = -e^(-x) dx, the integral = -log(1 + e^(-x)) + c. Boxed (printed key p608). This equals x - log(1 + e^x) + c, the same family as AQ5(v).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ5(xiii); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: 1 + cos x = 2cos^2(x/2), so the integrand is (x/2)sec^2(x/2) - one clean by-parts with v = 2tan(x/2).
questions.question: AQ6(i). Evaluate: integral of x/(1 + cos x) dx.
questions.solution: 1 + cos x = 2 cos^2(x/2), so the integral = (1/2) integral x sec^2(x/2) dx. By parts with u = x, dv = sec^2(x/2)dx, v = 2 tan(x/2): (1/2)[2x tan(x/2) - 2 integral tan(x/2) dx] = x tan(x/2) - integral tan(x/2) dx = x tan(x/2) + 2 log|cos(x/2)| + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ6(i); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Differentiate the answer to see the structure: log(1 - cos x) supplies sin x/(1 - cos x) and x cot(x/2) supplies the -x/(1 - cos x) part.
questions.question: AQ6(ii). Evaluate: integral of (sin x - x)/(1 - cos x) dx.
questions.solution: Write the integrand as sin x/(1 - cos x) - x/(1 - cos x). The first part integrates to log(1 - cos x) because d(1 - cos x) = sin x dx. For the second, 1 - cos x = 2 sin^2(x/2), so x/(1 - cos x) = (x/2) cosec^2(x/2); by parts with u = x, dv = (1/2)cosec^2(x/2)dx, v = -cot(x/2): integral = -x cot(x/2) + integral cot(x/2) dx = -x cot(x/2) + 2 log|sin(x/2)|. Subtracting gives log(1 - cos x) + x cot(x/2) - 2 log sin(x/2) + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ6(ii); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Substitute u = sqrt x (dx = 2u du) to get 2 integral u e^u du, then one by-parts.
questions.question: AQ6(iii). Evaluate: integral of e^(sqrt x) dx.
questions.solution: Let u = sqrt x, dx = 2u du. The integral = 2 integral u e^u du = 2(u e^u - e^u) + c = 2 e^(sqrt x)(sqrt x - 1) + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ6(iii); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Recognise a product-rule derivative: d(x/log x) = 1/log x - x*(1/x)/(log x)^2 = 1/log x - 1/(log x)^2.
questions.question: AQ6(iv). Evaluate: integral of {1/log x - 1/(log x)^2} dx.
questions.solution: Observe that d/dx [x/log x] = 1/log x - x(1/x)/(log x)^2 = 1/log x - 1/(log x)^2, which is exactly the integrand. Hence the integral = x/log x + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ6(iv); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: u = sqrt x gives 2 integral u sin u du, and that by-parts is the standard -u cos u + sin u.
questions.question: AQ6(v). Evaluate: integral of sin(sqrt x) dx.
questions.solution: Let u = sqrt x, dx = 2u du. The integral = 2 integral u sin u du = 2(-u cos u + sin u) + c = 2(sin sqrt x - sqrt x cos sqrt x) + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ6(v); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x, so u = sin x turns it into 2 integral u e^u du.
questions.question: AQ6(vi). Evaluate: integral of e^(sin x) sin 2x dx.
questions.solution: sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x. With u = sin x, du = cos x dx: the integral = 2 integral u e^u du = 2 e^u(u - 1) + c = 2 e^(sin x)(sin x - 1) + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ6(vi); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Two rounds of by parts: x^2 -> 2x -> 2, giving e^x(x^2 - 2x + 2).
questions.question: AQ6(vii). Evaluate: integral of x^2 e^x dx. (HSEB 2054).
questions.solution: By parts twice: integral x^2 e^x dx = x^2 e^x - 2 integral x e^x dx, and integral x e^x dx = x e^x - e^x. Hence integral x^2 e^x dx = x^2 e^x - 2x e^x + 2 e^x + c = e^x(x^2 - 2x + 2) + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ6(vii); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: First linearise sin^3 x = (3 sin x - sin 3x)/4, then do two by-parts integrals of x times a sine.
questions.question: AQ6(viii). Evaluate: integral of x sin^3 x dx.
questions.solution: sin^3 x = (3 sin x - sin 3x)/4, so the integral = (3/4) integral x sin x dx - (1/4) integral x sin 3x dx. Using integral x sin(ax) dx = sin(ax)/a^2 - x cos(ax)/a: the first is (-x cos x + sin x) and the second is (-x cos 3x/3 + sin 3x/9). Therefore the answer is -(3/4)x cos x + (3/4) sin x + (1/12)x cos 3x - (1/36) sin 3x + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ6(viii); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Both integrals over a quarter period are pi/4, so the answer is (a + b)pi/4 - no dependence on the mixture.
questions.question: AQ7(i). Evaluate: integral from 0 to pi/2 of (a cos^2 x + b sin^2 x) dx.
questions.solution: integral 0 to pi/2 of cos^2 x dx = pi/4 and integral 0 to pi/2 of sin^2 x dx = pi/4 (both are half the interval, by symmetry of the linearised integrands). Hence the value = a(pi/4) + b(pi/4) = (1/4)(a + b)pi. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ7(i); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Factor sqrt x out of the denominator and substitute u = sqrt x, which turns the integrand into 2/(1 + u).
questions.question: AQ7(ii). Evaluate: integral from 0 to 1 of dx/(sqrt x + x).
questions.solution: sqrt x + x = sqrt x(1 + sqrt x). With u = sqrt x, dx = 2u du and the limits stay 0 and 1: the integral = integral from 0 to 1 of 2u du/[u(1 + u)] = 2 integral from 0 to 1 of du/(1 + u) = 2[log(1 + u)]_0^1 = 2 log 2. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ7(ii); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: u = 1 + log x has du = dx/x and moves the limits to 1 and 3.
questions.question: AQ7(iii). Evaluate: integral from 1 to e^2 of dx/[x(1 + log x)^2].
questions.solution: Let u = 1 + log x, du = dx/x; when x = 1, u = 1; when x = e^2, u = 3. The integral = integral from 1 to 3 of u^(-2) du = [-1/u]_1^3 = -1/3 + 1 = 2/3. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ7(iii); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: sin^2 x cos^2 x = (1/4) sin^2 2x, then linearise again; the cosine term vanishes over the full quarter period.
questions.question: AQ7(iv). Evaluate: integral from 0 to pi/2 of sin^2 x cos^2 x dx.
questions.solution: sin^2 x cos^2 x = (1/4) sin^2 2x = (1/8)(1 - cos 4x). Hence the integral = (1/8)[x - sin 4x/4]_0^{pi/2} = (1/8)(pi/2 - 0) = pi/16. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ7(iv); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: u = a^2 sin^2 + b^2 cos^2 has derivative 2(a^2 - b^2) sin cos, and the limits map to b^2 and a^2; the result factors as (a^2 + ab + b^2)/(3(a+b)).
questions.question: AQ7(v). Evaluate: integral from 0 to pi/2 of sin theta cos theta sqrt(a^2 sin^2 theta + b^2 cos^2 theta) d theta.
questions.solution: Let u = a^2 sin^2 theta + b^2 cos^2 theta; du = 2(a^2 - b^2) sin theta cos theta d theta, with u = b^2 at theta = 0 and u = a^2 at theta = pi/2. The integral = (1/(2(a^2 - b^2))) integral from b^2 to a^2 of u^(1/2) du = (1/(2(a^2 - b^2))) * (2/3)[u^(3/2)]_{b^2}^{a^2} = (a^3 - b^3)/(3(a^2 - b^2)) = (a^2 + ab + b^2)/(3(a + b)), using a^3 - b^3 = (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2) and a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b). Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ7(v); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635
