questions.knowledgeNote: Divide top and bottom by cosA, then cross-multiply: both sides become cosA times (sinA - cosA + 1).
questions.question: Q1(a). Prove that (tanA - secA + 1)/(tanA + secA - 1) = cosA/(1 + sinA).
questions.solution: Divide numerator and denominator by cosA: LHS = (sinA - 1 + cosA)/(sinA + 1 - cosA). Cross-check: (sinA+cosA-1)(1+sinA) = sinA+sin^2A+cosA+sinAcosA-1-sinA = sin^2A+cosA+sinAcosA-1 = -cos^2A+cosA+sinAcosA = cosA(1-cosA+sinA) = cosA(sinA-cosA+1) = RHS numerator times denominator. Hence equal. Proved. (Statement via 200-dpi image read; OCR had merged the fraction bars.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.1 Q1(a); book p142 = PDF p169 (200-dpi image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: sec^2 - tan^2 = 1 makes the two unit fractions sum to exactly 2secA.
questions.question: Q1(b). Prove that 1/cosA - 1/(secA+tanA) = 1/(secA-tanA) - 1/cosA.
questions.solution: Rearranged: 2secA = 1/(secA-tanA) + 1/(secA+tanA). RHS = ((secA+tanA)+(secA-tanA))/((secA-tanA)(secA+tanA)) = 2secA/(sec^2A-tan^2A) = 2secA/1 = 2secA = LHS. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.1 Q1(b); book p142 = PDF p169 (200-dpi image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Read sinA straight off the hypothesis: sinA = (sqrt(2)-1)cosA - then both target sides are the same multiple of cosA.
questions.question: Q2. If cosA + sinA = sqrt(2)cosA, show that cosA - sinA = sqrt(2)sinA.
questions.solution: From the hypothesis sinA = (sqrt(2)-1)cosA (cosA != 0, else 1 = 0). Then cosA - sinA = cosA-(sqrt(2)-1)cosA = (2-sqrt(2))cosA; and sqrt(2)sinA = sqrt(2)(sqrt(2)-1)cosA = (2-sqrt(2))cosA. Equal. Shown. (No squaring, so no sign ambiguity.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.1 Q2; book p142 = PDF p169 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: sin(B-C)/(sinB sinC) = cotC - cotB: the three terms telescope to zero.
questions.question: Q3(a). Show that sin(B-C)/(sinB sinC) + sin(C-A)/(sinC sinA) + sin(A-B)/(sinA sinB) = 0.
questions.solution: sin(B-C)/(sinB sinC) = (sinBcosC-cosBsinC)/(sinBsinC) = cotC-cotB. Cyclically the others give cotA-cotC and cotB-cotA. Sum = 0. Shown.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.1 Q3(a); book p142 = PDF p169 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: cos(120+A)+cos(120-A) = 2cos120 cosA = -cosA: the pair eats the leading cosA.
questions.question: Q3(b). Show that cosA + cos(120deg+A) + cos(120deg-A) = 0.
questions.solution: cos(120+A)+cos(120-A) = 2cos120deg.cosA = 2(-1/2)cosA = -cosA. Adding cosA gives 0. Shown.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.1 Q3(b); book p142 = PDF p169 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Componendo in disguise: write k = sinxcosy/(cosxsiny) and expand both sides to (k^2-1)cosxsiny.
questions.question: Q4(a). If tanx = k.tany, show that (k-1)sin(x+y) = (k+1)sin(x-y).
questions.solution: tanx = k.tany gives sinxcosy = k.cosxsiny. LHS = (k-1)(sinxcosy+cosxsiny) = (k-1)(k+1)cosxsiny. RHS = (k+1)(sinxcosy-cosxsiny) = (k+1)(k-1)cosxsiny. Equal. Shown.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.1 Q4(a); book p142 = PDF p169 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Solve for (k-1) and (k+1) from the hypothesis: both equal twice a product over the same denominator.
questions.question: Q4(b). If sin(A+B) = k.sin(A-B), prove that (k-1)cotB = (k+1)cotA.
questions.solution: k = (sinAcosB+cosAsinB)/(sinAcosB-cosAsinB) =: N/D. Then k-1 = 2cosAsinB/D and k+1 = 2sinAcosB/D. So (k-1)cotB = 2cosAcosB/D = (k+1)cotA. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.1 Q4(b); book p142 = PDF p169 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Divide top and bottom by cos^2A: tan^2A appears and cos2A = cos^2 - sin^2 drops out.
questions.question: Q5(a). Prove that cos2A = (1-tan^2A)/(1+tan^2A).
questions.solution: (1-tan^2A)/(1+tan^2A) = ((cos^2A-sin^2A)/cos^2A)/((cos^2A+sin^2A)/cos^2A) = (cos^2A-sin^2A)/1 = cos2A. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.1 Q5(a); book p142 = PDF p169 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Double-angle both parts: 2cos^2B over 2sinBcosB.
questions.question: Q5(b). Prove that (1+cos2B)/sin2B = cotB.
questions.solution: (1+cos2B)/sin2B = 2cos^2B/(2sinBcosB) = cosB/sinB = cotB. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.1 Q5(b); book p142 = PDF p169 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Average of three 120-degree-shifted squares is 3/2: the cross terms cancel in pairs. (OCR misread '= 2'; the image confirms 3/2.)
questions.question: Q5(c). Prove that cos^2(A-120deg) + cos^2A + cos^2(A+120deg) = 3/2.
questions.solution: cos(A+-120) = -cosA/2 -/+ sqrt(3)sinA/2. Squaring: each = cos^2A/4 + 3sin^2A/4 -/+ cross term; the two cross terms (+sqrt(3)sinAcosA/2 and its negative) cancel. Sum = cos^2A + 2(cos^2A/4+3sin^2A/4) = (3/2)(cos^2A+sin^2A) = 3/2. Proved. (Book prints 3/2 - confirmed by image; OCR's '= 2' was a misread.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.1 Q5(c); book p142 = PDF p169 (200-dpi image read: '= 3/2')

questions.knowledgeNote: Write cos2phi with t = tan^2phi, simplify to (1-2t)/(1+2t), then read tan^2theta = 2t off the half-angle form.
questions.question: Q6. If theta and phi are acute angles and cos2theta = (3cos2phi-1)/(3-cos2phi), show that tantheta = sqrt(2).tanphi.
questions.solution: Put t = tan^2phi, so cos2phi = (1-t)/(1+t). RHS = (3(1-t)/(1+t)-1)/(3-(1-t)/(1+t)) = (2-4t)/(2+4t) = (1-2t)/(1+2t). Hence cos2theta = (1-2t)/(1+2t), and tan^2theta = (1-cos2theta)/(1+cos2theta) = 4t/2 = 2t. Acute angles give positive roots: tantheta = sqrt(2).tanphi. Shown.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.1 Q6; book p143 = PDF p170 (200-dpi image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: tan(A-B) with tanA = 3tanB/2 on top; on the bottom write everything with tanB via sin2B and cos2B.
questions.question: Q7. If 2tanA = 3tanB, prove that tan(A-B) = sin2B/(5-cos2B).
questions.solution: LHS = (tanA-tanB)/(1+tanAtanB) = (tanB/2)/((2+3tan^2B)/2) = tanB/(2+3tan^2B). RHS = (2tanB/(1+tan^2B))/(5-(1-tan^2B)/(1+tan^2B)) = 2tanB/(4+6tan^2B) = tanB/(2+3tan^2B). Equal. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.1 Q7; book p143 = PDF p170 (200-dpi image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Half-angle t-substitution plus k^2(1+e) = 1-e: numerator and denominator share the factor (1-e).
questions.question: Q8. If tan(theta/2) = sqrt((1-e)/(1+e)).tan(phi/2), prove that cosphi = (costheta-e)/(1-e.costheta).
questions.solution: Put t = tan(phi/2), T = tan(theta/2) = k.t with k^2 = (1-e)/(1+e). Then (costheta-e)/(1-e.costheta) with costheta = (1-k^2t^2)/(1+k^2t^2): numerator = ((1-e)-k^2t^2(1+e))/(1+k^2t^2) = (1-e)(1-t^2)/(1+k^2t^2) since k^2(1+e) = 1-e; denominator = ((1-e)+k^2t^2(1+e))/(1+k^2t^2) = (1-e)(1+t^2)/(1+k^2t^2). Ratio = (1-t^2)/(1+t^2) = cosphi. Proved. (The orbital true-anomaly relation.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.1 Q8; book p143 = PDF p170 (200-dpi image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: sin20.sin40.sin80 = sin60/4: the triple-angle product identity with theta = 20.
questions.question: Q9(a). Prove that 8.sin20deg.sin40deg.sin80deg = sqrt(3).
questions.solution: sin(theta)sin(60-theta)sin(60+theta) = sin3theta/4 with theta = 20deg gives sin20sin40sin80 = sin60/4 = sqrt(3)/8. Times 8: sqrt(3). Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.1 Q9(a); book p143 = PDF p170 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: cos20cos40cos80 = sin160/(8sin20) = 1/8; the cos60 factor halves it once more.
questions.question: Q9(b). Prove that 16.cos20deg.cos40deg.cos60deg.cos80deg = 1.
questions.solution: cos60 = 1/2. cos20cos40cos80 = sin(8x20)/(8sin20) = sin160/sin... = sin20/(8sin20) = 1/8 (using costheta.cos2theta.cos4theta = sin8theta/(8sintheta)). Product = (1/8)(1/2) = 1/16; times 16 = 1. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.1 Q9(b); book p143 = PDF p170 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Pair them as (sqrt(5)-2)(sqrt(5)+2) = 1: exact surd values at 6/66 and 42/78 degrees.
questions.question: Q9(c). Prove that tan6deg.tan42deg.tan66deg.tan78deg = 1.
questions.solution: tan6tan66 = (cos60-cos72)/(cos60+cos72) = (1/2-sin18)/(1/2+sin18) = sqrt(5)-2 (with sin18 = (sqrt(5)-1)/4). tan42tan78 = (cos36-cos120)/(cos36+cos120) = (sin54+1/2)/(sin54-1/2) = sqrt(5)+2 (with sin54 = (sqrt(5)+1)/4). Product = (sqrt(5)-2)(sqrt(5)+2) = 5-4 = 1. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.1 Q9(c); book p143 = PDF p170 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Componendo-dividendo on sin2x/sin2y = 3/1 turns the ratio into tan(x+y)/tan(x-y) = 2.
questions.question: Q10. If sin2x = 3.sin2y, prove that 2.tan(x-y) = tan(x+y).
questions.solution: (sin2x+sin2y)/(sin2x-sin2y) = (3+1)/(3-1) = 2. LHS = (2sin(x+y)cos(x-y))/(2cos(x+y)sin(x-y)) = tan(x+y)/tan(x-y). So tan(x+y)/tan(x-y) = 2, i.e. tan(x+y) = 2tan(x-y). Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.1 Q10; book p143 = PDF p170

questions.knowledgeNote: Each bracket is +-cot((A-B)/2): same sign (even n) doubles, opposite signs (odd n) cancel.
questions.question: Q11. Prove that ((cosA+cosB)/(sinA-sinB))^n + ((sinA+sinB)/(cosA-cosB))^n = 2cot^n((A-B)/2) or 0 according as n is even or odd.
questions.solution: (cosA+cosB)/(sinA-sinB) = (2cos((A+B)/2)cos((A-B)/2))/(2cos((A+B)/2)sin((A-B)/2)) = cot((A-B)/2). (sinA+sinB)/(cosA-cosB) = (2sin((A+B)/2)cos((A-B)/2))/(-2sin((A+B)/2)sin((A-B)/2)) = -cot((A-B)/2). Sum = cot^n + (-cot)^n = 2cot^n((A-B)/2) for even n, 0 for odd n. Proved. (Statement via 200-dpi image read; OCR had scrambled the denominators.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.1 Q11; book p143 = PDF p170 (200-dpi image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: (A+B)/2 and C/2 are complementary: tan((A+B)/2) = cot(C/2) rearranges straight into the result.
questions.question: Q12(a). If A+B+C = pi, prove that tan(B/2)tan(C/2) + tan(C/2)tan(A/2) + tan(A/2)tan(B/2) = 1.
questions.solution: (A+B)/2 = pi/2 - C/2, so (tan(A/2)+tan(B/2))/(1-tan(A/2)tan(B/2)) = tan((A+B)/2) = cot(C/2) = 1/tan(C/2). Cross-multiplying: tan(A/2)tan(C/2)+tan(B/2)tan(C/2) = 1-tan(A/2)tan(B/2). Rearranged: sum = 1. Proved. (Statement via 200-dpi image read; OCR had dropped the half-angles.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.1 Q12(a); book p143 = PDF p170 (200-dpi image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Pair the first two sines, then fold sin2C in: cosC = -cos(A+B) makes the last step click.
questions.question: Q12(b). If A+B+C = pi, prove that sin2A + sin2B + sin2C = 4.sinA.sinB.sinC.
questions.solution: sin2A+sin2B = 2sin(A+B)cos(A-B) = 2sinC.cos(A-B). Add sin2C = 2sinCcosC: total = 2sinC(cos(A-B)+cosC) = 2sinC(cos(A-B)-cos(A+B)) = 2sinC.2sinAsinB = 4sinAsinBsinC. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.1 Q12(b); book p143 = PDF p170 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Group cos^2A+cos^2B with the half-angle form, then let cosC = -cos(A+B) finish it - the book's own worked example uses this.
questions.question: Q13(a). If A+B+C = pi, prove that cos^2A + cos^2B + cos^2C = 1 - 2cosAcosBcosC.
questions.solution: cos^2A+cos^2B = 1+(cos2A+cos2B)/2 = 1+cos(A+B)cos(A-B) = 1-cosC.cos(A-B). Add cos^2C: 1-cosC.cos(A-B)+cos^2C = 1-cosC(cos(A-B)-cosC) = 1-cosC(cos(A-B)+cos(A+B)) = 1-2cosAcosBcosC. Proved. (Same proof as the book's worked example above Ex 4.1.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.1 Q13(a); book p143 = PDF p170 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Apply the Q13(a) pattern to the half-angles X = A/2 etc. (X+Y+Z = pi/2): the cofunction flips cos into sin exactly where needed.
questions.question: Q13(b). If A+B+C = pi, prove that sin^2(A/2) + sin^2(B/2) + sin^2(C/2) = 1 - 2sin(A/2)sin(B/2)sin(C/2).
questions.solution: Put X = A/2, Y = B/2, Z = C/2 with X+Y+Z = pi/2. sin^2X+sin^2Y = 1-(cos2X+cos2Y)/2 = 1-cos(X+Y)cos(X-Y) = 1-sinZ.cos(X-Y). Add sin^2Z: 1-sinZ.cos(X-Y)+sin^2Z = 1-sinZ(cos(X-Y)-sinZ) = 1-sinZ(cos(X-Y)-cos(X+Y)) = 1-2sinXsinYsinZ. Proved. (Statement via 200-dpi image read; OCR had dropped the half-angles.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.1 Q13(b); book p143 = PDF p170 (200-dpi image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: cosx = +-1/2: read both branches off the unit circle - pi/3 in QI/QIV.
questions.question: Q1(a). Solve 4cos^2x = 1.
questions.solution: cos^2x = 1/4, so cosx = 1/2 or cosx = -1/2. Both give x = n.pi +- pi/3. Matches the printed Answers key (p154): 'n.pi +- pi/3'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q1(a); book p152 = PDF p179 (OCR conf 0.93); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: cos2x = 1 - 2sin^2x turns it into a quadratic in sinx: (2sinx-1)(sinx+1) = 0.
questions.question: Q1(b). Solve cos2x - sinx = 0.
questions.solution: 1-2sin^2x-sinx = 0, i.e. 2sin^2x+sinx-1 = (2sinx-1)(sinx+1) = 0. sinx = 1/2: x = n.pi+(-1)^n.pi/6. sinx = -1: x = 2n.pi-pi/2 (=(4n-1).pi/2). Both verified by substitution.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q1(b); book p152 = PDF p179; key form differs, answers verified

questions.knowledgeNote: sin2x = 2sinxcosx: factor sinx out and solve each factor.
questions.question: Q1(c). Solve 2sin2x = sinx.
questions.solution: 4sinxcosx-sinx = sinx(4cosx-1) = 0. sinx = 0: x = n.pi. cosx = 1/4: x = 2n.pi +- cos^(-1)(1/4). Matches the key: 'n.pi, 2n.pi +- cos^(-1)(1/4)'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q1(c); book p152 = PDF p179; matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Same factor trick: sinx(2cosx+1) = 0.
questions.question: Q1(d). Solve sin2x + sinx = 0.
questions.solution: sinx(2cosx+1) = 0. sinx = 0: x = n.pi. cosx = -1/2: x = 2n.pi +- 2pi/3 (=(6n+-2).pi/3). Matches the key: 'n.pi, (6n+-2).pi/3'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q1(d); book p152 = PDF p179; matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: sin^2 = 1 - cos^2: the equation becomes cosx(cosx+1) = 0 - handle BOTH branches.
questions.question: Q2(a). Solve sin^2x - cosx = 1.
questions.solution: (1-cos^2x)-cosx = 1 gives cosx(cosx+1) = 0. cosx = 0: x = (4n+-1).pi/2. cosx = -1: x = (2n+1).pi. (Note: x = (2n+1).pi/2 alone would wrongly admit x = pi; both families are needed.) Matches the key.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q2(a); book p152 = PDF p179; matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Quadratic in sinx with roots -3 and 2: both outside [-1,1], so no solution exists.
questions.question: Q2(b). Solve cos^2x - sinx + 5 = 0.
questions.solution: (1-sin^2x)-sinx+5 = 0 gives sin^2x+sinx-6 = (sinx+3)(sinx-2) = 0. sinx = -3 or 2 are both impossible. No solution. Matches the key: 'No solution'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q2(b); book p152 = PDF p179; matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Multiply by cosx: a perfect square (2cosx-1)^2 = 0 - a double root.
questions.question: Q2(c). Solve 4cosx + secx - 4 = 0.
questions.solution: 4cos^2x-4cosx+1 = (2cosx-1)^2 = 0, so cosx = 1/2: x = 2n.pi +- pi/3 (=(6n+-1).pi/3). Matches the key.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q2(c); book p152 = PDF p179; matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Multiply by sinx, then REJECT cosx = 1: it makes cot/cosec undefined in the original.
questions.question: Q2(d). Solve 2sinx + cotx - cosecx = 0.
questions.solution: 2sin^2x+cosx-1 = 0 gives 2cos^2x-cosx-1 = (2cosx+1)(cosx-1) = 0. cosx = 1 would make sinx = 0 (cot, cosec undefined) - rejected. cosx = -1/2: x = 2n.pi +- 2pi/3. Matches the key: '(6n+-2).pi/3' (rejection noted).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q2(d); book p152 = PDF p179; matches key; extraneous root rejected

questions.knowledgeNote: 2+2sin^2x = 3 at once: sin^2x = 1/2.
questions.question: Q3(a). Solve 2cos^2x + 4sin^2x = 3.
questions.solution: 2(1-sin^2x)+4sin^2x = 3 gives 2sin^2x = 1, sinx = +-1/sqrt(2): x = n.pi +- pi/4. Matches the key. (Statement order confirmed by 200-dpi image read.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q3(a); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); matches key

questions.question: Q3(b). Solve 7sin^2x + 3cos^2x = 4.
questions.solution: 4sin^2x+3(cos^2x+sin^2x)... = 4sin^2x+3 = 4, so sin^2x = 1/4, sinx = +-1/2: x = n.pi +- pi/6. Verified: x = pi/6 gives 7/4+3(3/4) = 7/4+9/4 = 4. (Statement via image read.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q3(b); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); verified by substitution

questions.knowledgeNote: tan+cot = 1/(sinxcosx): the sinx cancels leaving cosx = 1/2 (sinx = 0 was never allowed).
questions.question: Q3(c). Solve tanx + cotx = 2cosecx.
questions.solution: (sin^2x+cos^2x)/(sinxcosx) = 2/sinx gives 1/cosx = 2 (sinx != 0), so cosx = 1/2: x = 2n.pi +- pi/3. Verified: tan(pi/3)+cot(pi/3) = sqrt(3)+1/sqrt(3) = 4/sqrt(3) = 2cosec(pi/3).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q3(c); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); verified by substitution

questions.knowledgeNote: tan^2 = sec^2-1: (secx-2)(secx+1) = 0 - and secx = -1 (x = odd pi) IS valid here since tan is 0, not undefined.
questions.question: Q3(d). Solve tan^2x = secx + 1 [HSEB 2058].
questions.solution: sec^2x-1 = secx+1 gives (secx-2)(secx+1) = 0. secx = 2: x = 2n.pi +- pi/3. secx = -1: x = (2n+1).pi (tan = 0, sec = -1: 0 = -1+1 checks). Matches the key: '(2n+1).pi, 2n.pi +- ...'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q3(d) [HSEB 2058]; book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: R-form: sinx+sqrt(3)cosx = 2sin(x+pi/3) = sqrt(2).
questions.question: Q4(a). Solve sinx + sqrt(3)cosx = sqrt(2) [T.U. 2049 H] [HSEB 2055].
questions.solution: 2sin(x+pi/3) = sqrt(2), so sin(x+pi/3) = 1/sqrt(2): x+pi/3 = n.pi+(-1)^n.pi/4, i.e. x = 2n.pi-pi/12 or 2n.pi+5pi/12. Verified: x = -pi/12 gives sin(-pi/12)+sqrt(3)cos(-pi/12) = sqrt(2). (Statement via image read.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q4(a); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); verified by substitution

questions.knowledgeNote: 2sin(x-pi/6) = sqrt(2) with x-pi/6 in [-pi/6, 5pi/6]: only pi/4 and 3pi/4 qualify.
questions.question: Q4(b). Solve sqrt(3)sinx - cosx = sqrt(2) (0 <= x <= pi).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q4(b); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); both values verified

questions.knowledgeNote: Same equation as Q4(a) (addition commutes) - same solution set; the book asks it twice (once as T.U. 2053).
questions.question: Q4(c). Solve cosx + sqrt(3)sinx = sqrt(2) [T.U. 2053].
questions.solution: Identical to Q4(a) (terms commute): x = 2n.pi-pi/12 or 2n.pi+5pi/12. (Duplication is in the print, kept faithfully.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q4(c) [T.U. 2053]; book p153 = PDF p180 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: sqrt(2)sin(x+pi/4) = sqrt(2) forces sin = 1: x = 2n.pi+pi/4, then keep only those inside [-2pi, 2pi].
questions.question: Q4(d). Solve sinx + cosx = sqrt(2) (-2pi <= x <= 2pi).
questions.solution: sin(x+pi/4) = 1 gives x = 2n.pi+pi/4. Inside [-2pi, 2pi]: n = -1 gives -7pi/4; n = 0 gives pi/4 (n = 1 gives 9pi/4 > 2pi, excluded). Solutions: x = -7pi/4, pi/4. Both verified.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q4(d); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); interval filter applied

questions.knowledgeNote: sin3x+sinx = 2sin2xcosx: the cosx factor is absorbed - everything is already covered by sin2x = 0.
questions.question: Q5(a). Solve sin3x + sinx = 0.
questions.solution: 2sin2xcosx = 0. sin2x = 0: x = n.pi/2 (this already includes cosx = 0's (2n+1).pi/2). So x = n.pi/2. Verified: x = pi/2 gives sin(3pi/2)+sin(pi/2) = -1+1 = 0.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q5(a); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Move sin2x over: sin2x(2cosx-1) = 0.
questions.question: Q5(b). Solve sin3x + sinx = sin2x.
questions.solution: 2sin2xcosx-sin2x = sin2x(2cosx-1) = 0. sin2x = 0: x = n.pi/2. cosx = 1/2: x = 2n.pi +- pi/3. Verified: x = pi/3 gives sin(pi)+sin(pi/3) = sqrt(3)/2 = sin(2pi/3).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q5(b); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); verified by substitution

questions.knowledgeNote: cos3x-cosx = -2sin2xsinx: the extra sinx factor adds nothing beyond sin2x = 0.
questions.question: Q5(c). Solve cos3x - cosx = 0.
questions.solution: -2sin2xsinx = 0. sin2x = 0: x = n.pi/2 (includes sinx = 0's n.pi). So x = n.pi/2. Verified: x = pi/2 gives cos(3pi/2)-cos(pi/2) = 0.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q5(c); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: 3x = n.pi with the window (-pi/2, pi/2): only -pi/3, 0, pi/3 survive (endpoints and +-pi/4 were never in the set).
questions.question: Q5(d). Solve tan2x + tanx = 0 (-pi/2 <= x <= pi/2).
questions.solution: tan2x = tan(-x) gives 2x = n.pi-x, i.e. x = n.pi/3. In [-pi/2, pi/2] with tan defined: x = -pi/3, 0, pi/3 (each verified: tan(-2pi/3)+tan(-pi/3) = -sqrt(3)+... = 0). Endpoints +-pi/2 excluded (tan undefined).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q5(d); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); interval filter applied

questions.knowledgeNote: Divide by cos^2x: tan^2x-tanx-2 = (tanx-2)(tanx+1) = 0.
questions.question: Q6(a). Solve 2cos^2x + sinxcosx - sin^2x = 0.
questions.solution: 2+tanx-tan^2x = 0, i.e. (tanx-2)(tanx+1) = 0. tanx = 2: x = n.pi+alpha (alpha = tan^(-1)2). tanx = -1: x = n.pi-pi/4. Matches the key: 'n.pi-pi/4, n.pi+alpha'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q6(a); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Group as 2sinx(cosx-2)-(cosx-2): cosx = 2 is impossible, leaving sinx = 1/2.
questions.question: Q6(b). Solve sin2x - 4sinx - cosx + 2 = 0.
questions.solution: (2sinx-1)(cosx-2) = 0. cosx = 2 impossible. sinx = 1/2: x = n.pi+(-1)^n.pi/6. Verified: x = pi/6 gives sin(pi/3)-4(1/2)-cos(pi/6)+2 = 0.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q6(b); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); verified by substitution

questions.knowledgeNote: 9theta = n.pi+(-1)^n.theta: even n gives theta = mpi/4, odd n gives (2m+1).pi/10 - check each branch, don't just write n.pi/8.
questions.question: Q7(a). Solve sin9theta = sintheta.
questions.solution: 9theta = n.pi+(-1)^n.theta. n even (n = 2m): 8theta = 2m.pi, theta = m.pi/4. n odd: 10theta = (2m+1).pi, theta = (2m+1).pi/10. Verified: theta = pi/4 gives sin(9pi/4) = sin(pi/4); theta = pi/10 gives sin(9pi/10) = sin(pi/10).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q7(a); book p153 = PDF p180; branches derived exactly

questions.knowledgeNote: cot2theta = tan(pi/2-2theta): linear equation 7theta = n.pi+pi/2.
questions.question: Q7(b). Solve tan5theta = cot2theta.
questions.solution: 5theta = n.pi+(pi/2-2theta), so 7theta = n.pi+pi/2: theta = (2n+1).pi/14. Verified: theta = pi/14 gives tan(5pi/14) = cot(pi/7).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q7(b); book p153 = PDF p180; verified by substitution

questions.knowledgeNote: tan2x = tan(pi/2-x): 3x = n.pi+pi/2 - and every one of these keeps both tans defined.
questions.question: Q7(c). Solve tan2x - cotx = 0.
questions.solution: 2x = n.pi+(pi/2-x), so x = (2n+1).pi/6. Definedness: (2n+1).pi/6 = pi/2+k.pi would need 2n+1 = 3+6k (odd = odd: n = 1+3k gives x = pi/2 mod pi - but tan(pi) = 0 and cot(pi/2) = 0 are both DEFINED, value 0-0 = 0, valid!). All x = (2n+1).pi/6 valid; never hits tan2x's pi/4+k.pi/2 (would need even = odd) or cot's k.pi. Verified at pi/6, pi/2, 5pi/6.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q7(c); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); definedness checked

questions.knowledgeNote: tan(m.theta) = tan(n.theta-pi/2): (m-n).theta = k.pi-pi/2. If m = n the equation is 1/(sin.cos) = 0 - impossible.
questions.question: Q7(d). Solve tan(m.theta) + cot(n.theta) = 0.
questions.solution: tan(m.theta) = -cot(n.theta) = tan(n.theta-pi/2), so (m-n).theta = k.pi-pi/2: theta = (2k-1).pi/(2(m-n)) for m != n (wherever all tans/cots are defined). If m = n: tan+cot = 1/(sin.cos) = 0 has no solution. (Standard form; validity caveat as stated.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q7(d); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); m = n case noted

questions.knowledgeNote: Pair outer terms: cos+cos3 = 2cos2cos - then cos2theta factors the whole row.
questions.question: Q8(a). Solve costheta + cos2theta + cos3theta = 0 [T.U. 2056 S].
questions.solution: (cos+cos3)+cos2 = 2cos2.cos+cos2 = cos2(2cos+1) = 0. cos2 = 0: theta = n.pi +- pi/4 (=(4n+-1).pi/4). cos = -1/2: theta = 2n.pi +- 2pi/3 (=(6n+-2).pi/3). Matches the key's three-family form.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q8(a) [T.U. 2056 S]; book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: cos-cos2 = -2sin(3t/2)sin(-t/2): three families - 2n.pi/3, n.pi+pi/4, 2n.pi-pi/2.
questions.question: Q8(b). Solve costheta - sin3theta = cos2theta.
questions.solution: cos-cos2 = sin3 gives 2sin(3t/2)sin(t/2) = 2sin(3t/2)cos(3t/2), i.e. 2sin(3t/2)(sin(t/2)-cos(3t/2)) = 0. sin(3t/2) = 0: t = 2n.pi/3. Else sin(t/2) = cos(3t/2) = sin(pi/2-3t/2): t = n.pi+pi/4 or t = 2n.pi-pi/2 (even/odd-n branches). All three verified (e.g. t = -pi/2: 0-1 = -1 = cos(-pi)).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q8(b); book p153 = PDF p180; all branches verified

questions.knowledgeNote: tan3 = (tan+tan2)/(1-tan.tan2): the equation becomes tan3.tan.tan2 = 0 - then throw out every point where a tan is undefined (none of n.pi/3 is one).
questions.question: Q8(c). Solve tantheta + tan2theta = tan3theta [T.U. 2057 S].
questions.solution: With T = tan+tan2: T = T/(1-tan.tan2), so T.tan.tan2 = 0. tan = 0: t = k.pi. tan2 = 0: t = k.pi/2 (odd k undefined for tan, even k already counted). T = 0: sin3/(cos.cos2) = 0 gives 3t = n.pi, t = n.pi/3 (all keep every tan defined: n.pi/3 = pi/2+k.pi and = pi/4+k.pi/2 have no integer solutions). Union: t = n.pi/3. Verified at 0, pi/3, 2pi/3. (Key line illegible; answer substitution-verified.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q8(c) [T.U. 2057 S]; book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); definedness checked, verified

questions.knowledgeNote: 2sinxsin3x = cos2x-cos4x: then cos2x(1-2cos2x) = 0.
questions.question: Q8(d). Solve 2sinx.sin3x = 1 [T.U. 2052 H].
questions.solution: cos2x-cos4x = 1 gives cos2x(1-2cos2x) = 0 (using cos4x = 2cos^2 2x-1). cos2x = 0: x = n.pi +- pi/4. cos2x = 1/2: x = n.pi +- pi/6. Verified: x = pi/4 gives 2(.707)(.707) = 1; x = pi/6 gives 2(.5)(1) = 1. Matches the key: '(4n+-1).pi/4, (6n+-1).pi/6'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q8(d) [T.U. 2052 H]; book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: cosec^2-1 = cot^2: (cosec-2)(cosec+1) = 0.
questions.question: Q9(a). Solve cot^2x - cosecx - 1 = 0.
questions.solution: cosec^2x-cosecx-2 = (cosecx-2)(cosecx+1) = 0. cosecx = 2: x = n.pi+(-1)^n.pi/6. cosecx = -1: x = (4n-1).pi/2. Verified: x = -pi/2 gives 0+1-1 = 0. Matches the key.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q9(a); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Square it: cosx(cosx+4/5)... then KEEP only branches satisfying 2cosx+1 = sinx - here both survive.
questions.question: Q9(b). Solve 2cosx + 1 = sinx.
questions.solution: (2cosx+1)^2 = sin^2x gives 5cos^2x+4cosx = cosx(5cosx+4) = 0. cosx = 0: x = 2n.pi+pi/2 (check: 1 = 1 valid; 2n.pi-pi/2 gives 1 = -1 rejected). cosx = -4/5: then sinx = -3/5, i.e. x = 2n.pi+pi+alpha with sin(alpha) = 3/5 (check: -8/5+1 = -3/5 valid). Solutions: x = 2n.pi+pi/2 or 2n.pi+pi+alpha. (Key partially legible; every kept branch substitution-verified, rejects verified.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q9(b); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); extraneous branch rejected

questions.knowledgeNote: sinx/cos^2x = sqrt(2): quadratic in sinx with roots 1/sqrt(2) and -sqrt(2) - keep only |.| <= 1.
questions.question: Q9(c). Solve secx.tanx = sqrt(2).
questions.solution: sinx = sqrt(2)cos^2x = sqrt(2)(1-sin^2x) gives sqrt(2)sin^2x+sinx-sqrt(2) = 0: sinx = 1/sqrt(2) (other root -sqrt(2) rejected). x = n.pi+(-1)^n.pi/4. Verified: x = pi/4 gives sqrt(2).1 = sqrt(2). (Statement via image read: product, not sum.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q9(c); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); |sin|<=1 enforced

questions.knowledgeNote: sin^4 = (1-cos2x)^2/4: the cos^2 2x terms cancel leaving 1-2cos2x = 0.
questions.question: Q9(d). Solve 4sin^4x - cos^2 2x = 0.
questions.solution: (1-cos2x)^2-cos^2 2x = 1-2cos2x = 0, so cos2x = 1/2: x = n.pi +- pi/6 (=(6n+-1).pi/6). Verified: x = pi/6 gives 4/16-1/4 = 0. Matches the key. (Statement via image read: 4sin^4x.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q9(d); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: sin8theta = 8sinthetacostheta...: 4cos.cos2.cos4 = sin8/(2sin) - zeros at n.pi/8 except multiples of pi.
questions.question: Q10(a). Solve costheta + cos3theta + cos5theta + cos7theta = 0.
questions.solution: Pair outer/inner: 2cos4.cos3+2cos4.cos = 2cos4(cos3+cos) = 4cos.cos2.cos4 = sin8/(2sin) = 0 (sin != 0). So sin8 = 0, sin != 0: theta = n.pi/8 with n not a multiple of 8; i.e. (4n+-1).pi/8, (4n+-1).pi/4, (4n+-1).pi/2 families. Matches the key's three-family form.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q10(a); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: T(1-tan.tan2) = T with T = tan+tan2: T.tan.tan2 = 0 - union of tan = 0 and tan+tan2 = 0 is just n.pi/3.
questions.question: Q10(b). Solve tantheta + tan2theta + tan3theta = 0.
questions.solution: tan3 = (tan+tan2)/(1-tan.tan2) gives (tan+tan2).tan.tan2 = 0. tan = 0: t = k.pi. tan2 = 0: t = k.pi/2 (odd k undefined for tan, even k already counted). tan+tan2 = sin3/(cos.cos2) = 0: 3t = n.pi, t = n.pi/3 (all keep every tan defined: no integer n hits pi/2+k.pi or pi/4+k.pi/2). Union: t = n.pi/3. Verified at 0, pi/3 (sqrt(3)-sqrt(3)+0 = 0), 2pi/3. (Key line illegible; substitution-verified.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q10(b); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); definedness checked, verified

questions.knowledgeNote: (t^2-3)/t = 2tan3theta with t = tantheta: clears to (t^2-1)(t^2-3) = 0 - then check all 8 against tan3theta's undefined points (none hit).
questions.question: Q11. Find all solutions of tantheta - 3cottheta = 2tan3theta between 0deg and 360deg.
questions.solution: (t^2-3)/t = 2(3t-t^3)/(1-3t^2) clears to t^4-4t^2+3 = (t^2-1)(t^2-3) = 0: tantheta = +-1, +-sqrt(3). In [0, 360): 45, 135, 225, 315 (from +-1) and 60, 120, 240, 300 (from +-sqrt(3)). Domain check: none equals 30+60k (tan3 undefined) or 90k (tan/cot undefined). All 8 valid. (Key garbled; every value substitution-verified.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q11; book p153-154 = PDF p180 (image read); domain-checked

questions.knowledgeNote: Two equations, two unknowns: tanx+tany = sin(x+y)/(cosxcosy) = 2 with cosxcosy = 1/2 forces sin(x+y) = 1.
questions.question: Q12. Find the (principal) solution of tanx + tany = 2, 2cosxcosy = 1 (general solution not required).
questions.solution: cosxcosy = 1/2 and (tanx+tany) = sin(x+y)/(cosxcosy) = 2 gives sin(x+y) = 1, so x+y = pi/2 (principal). Then tany = cotx and tanx+cotx = 2 gives (tanx-1)^2 = 0: tanx = 1, x = pi/4, y = pi/4. Check: 1+1 = 2; 2(1/2) = 1. Solution: (pi/4, pi/4).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q12; book p154 = PDF p180 (image read); verified pair

questions.knowledgeNote: tanA+tanB+tanC = tanAtanBtanC iff A+B+C = k.pi: here 6theta = k.pi, minus odd k (tan3theta undefined there).
questions.question: Q13(i). Solve tantheta + tan2theta + tan3theta = tantheta.tan2theta.tan3theta.
questions.solution: Holds iff theta+2theta+3theta = k.pi (all tans defined), i.e. 6theta = k.pi: theta = k.pi/6. Exclude odd k (tan3theta = tan(k.pi/2) undefined) and k = 3 mod 6 (tantheta undefined; already odd). Even k: theta = m.pi/3. Verified: pi/3 gives 0 = 0; 0 gives 0 = 0. (Key row misaligned in scan; substitution-verified.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q13(i); book p154 = PDF p180 (image read); exclusions handled, verified

questions.knowledgeNote: Clear denominators: -(t^3)+3t^2+3t... factors as (t+1)(t^2-4t+1) = 0 - three tan values: -1, 2+-sqrt(3) = tan(-45, 15, 75 deg).
questions.question: Q13(ii). Solve tantheta + tan2theta + tantheta.tan2theta = 1.
questions.solution: With t = tantheta: t+2t/(1-t^2)+2t^2/(1-t^2) = 1 clears to t^3-3t^2-3t+1 = (t+1)(t^2-4t+1) = 0. t = -1: theta = n.pi-pi/4. t = 2+sqrt(3) = tan75: theta = n.pi+5pi/12. t = 2-sqrt(3) = tan15: theta = n.pi+pi/12. All verified (e.g. pi/12: (2-sqrt(3))+1/sqrt(3)+(2-sqrt(3))/sqrt(3) = 1).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q13(ii); book p154 = PDF p180 (image read); verified by substitution

questions.question: Q13(iii). Solve tan(pi/4+theta) + tan(pi/4-theta) = 4.
questions.solution: 2(1+t^2)/(1-t^2) = 4 where t = tantheta, so t^2 = 1/3: tantheta = +-1/sqrt(3), theta = n.pi +- pi/6 (t = +-1 never hits the excluded 1). Verified: pi/6 gives tan(5pi/12)+tan(pi/12) = (2+sqrt(3))+(2-sqrt(3)) = 4. (Statement via image read.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q13(iii); book p154 = PDF p180 (image read); verified by substitution

questions.knowledgeNote: (sin2x-1)(tanx-1) = 0: BOTH branches give x = n.pi+pi/4 - a double lock.
questions.question: Q14(i). Solve sin2x.tanx + 1 = sin2x + tanx [T.U. 2051 H, 058 S].
questions.solution: (sin2x-1)(tanx-1) = 0. sin2x = 1: x = n.pi+pi/4. tanx = 1: x = n.pi+pi/4. So x = n.pi+pi/4 (cos != 0 throughout). Verified: sin(pi/2).1+1 = 2 = 1+1. Matches the key: 'n.pi+pi/4'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q14(i) [T.U. 2051 H, 058 S]; book p154 = PDF p180 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: (tanx-1)(2sinx-1) = 0: two independent families.
questions.question: Q14(ii). Solve 2sinx.tanx + 1 = tanx + 2sinx [T.U. 2053 H].
questions.solution: (tanx-1)(2sinx-1) = 0. tanx = 1: x = n.pi+pi/4. sinx = 1/2: x = n.pi+(-1)^n.pi/6. Both verified (e.g. pi/6: 2(.5)(1/sqrt(3))+1 = 1/sqrt(3)+1 = tan+2sin). Matches the key.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q14(ii) [T.U. 2053 H]; book p154 = PDF p180 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: cosx-cos2x = sin2x-sinx: -2sin(3x/2)sin(-x/2) = 2cos(3x/2)sin(x/2).
questions.question: Q15(i). Solve cosx + sinx = cos2x + sin2x.
questions.solution: 2sin(x/2)(sin(3x/2)-cos(3x/2)) = 0. sin(x/2) = 0: x = 2n.pi. tan(3x/2) = 1: x = (4n+1).pi/6. Verified: pi/6 gives (sqrt(3)+1)/2 on both sides. Matches the key: '2n.pi, (4n+1).pi/6'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q15(i); book p154 = PDF p180 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: cosx-cosx... = sinx+sinx...: pair as -2sin((x+a)/2)sin((x-a)/2) = 2sin((x+a)/2)cos((x-a)/2). (The key's second family drops '-pi/2' in print/OCR - exact form filed.)
questions.question: Q15(ii). Solve cosx - sinx = cos(alpha) + sin(alpha).
questions.solution: -2sin((x+alpha)/2)sin((x-alpha)/2) = 2sin((x+alpha)/2)cos((x-alpha)/2), i.e. 2sin((x+alpha)/2)(-sin((x-alpha)/2)-cos((x-alpha)/2)) = 0. sin((x+alpha)/2) = 0: x = 2n.pi-alpha. tan((x-alpha)/2) = -1: x = 2n.pi+alpha-pi/2. Verified at alpha = 0: {2n.pi} and {2n.pi-pi/2} both satisfy cosx-sinx = 1. (Statement via image read; key fragment '2n.pi+-alpha' appears to drop the -pi/2.)

questions.knowledgeNote: An equation true for ALL values is an identity; one true for SOME values is a (conditional) equation.
questions.question: AQ1(a). What does the trigonometrical equation mean?
questions.solution: An equation involving trigonometric functions of an unknown angle (variable) is a trigonometrical equation. It is 'conditional': unlike an identity (true for every admissible value), it holds only for specific values - e.g. sin x = 1/2 is satisfied by x = 30deg but not by x = 45deg (book Section 4.2).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q1; book p155 = PDF p182; answer from Section 4.2 text

questions.knowledgeNote: Roots are the specific angles that satisfy the equation.
questions.question: AQ1(b). What is the solution (root) of a trigonometrical equation?
questions.solution: Any particular value of the unknown angle that satisfies the equation is a solution (root) - e.g. x = 30deg and x = 150deg are roots of sin x = 1/2, since both satisfy it (book Section 4.2).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q1; book p155 = PDF p182; answer from Section 4.2 text

questions.knowledgeNote: Periodicity makes roots infinite: the general solution packages them all with an integer n.
questions.question: AQ1(c). What is the general value (general solution) of a trigonometrical equation?
questions.solution: Because trig functions repeat every 360deg, an equation has infinitely many roots (e.g. sin x = 1/2 holds at 30deg, 150deg and every coterminal angle). The set of ALL solutions, written with an arbitrary integer n, is the general solution - e.g. x = n.360deg+30deg or n.360deg+150deg (book Section 4.2).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q1; book p155 = PDF p182; answer from Section 4.2 text

questions.knowledgeNote: sin2x+sin6x = 2sin4xcos2x: the whole row collapses on sin4x.
questions.question: AQ2(i). Solve sin2x + sin4x + sin6x = 0.
questions.solution: (sin2x+sin6x)+sin4x = 2sin4xcos2x+sin4x = sin4x(2cos2x+1) = 0. sin4x = 0: x = n.pi/4. cos2x = -1/2: x = n.pi +- pi/3. Verified: x = pi/4 gives 1+0-1 = 0; x = pi/3 gives 0. (Key's 'n.pi/4' fraction partially legible; both families verified.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q2(i); book p155 = PDF p182 (200-dpi image read); verified by substitution

questions.knowledgeNote: Half the equation, then everything in cos2x: -cos2x(cos2x+1) = 0.
questions.question: AQ2(ii). Solve 2sin^2x + sin^2 2x = 2.
questions.solution: sin^2x(1+2cos^2x) = 1; with sin^2x = (1-cos2x)/2 and 2sin^2xcos^2x = sin^2 2x/2: 1-cos2x+sin^2 2x = 2 gives -cos2x(cos2x+1) = 0. cos2x = 0: x = n.pi+pi/2... i.e. odd multiples: x = (2n+1).pi/4? No: cos2x = 0 gives 2x = (2n+1).pi/2, x = (2n+1).pi/4 (odd pi/4s). cos2x = -1: x = (2n+1).pi/2. Union: x = (2n+1).pi/4 or (2n+1).pi/2 - equivalently n.pi+pi/2 or n.pi+-pi/4. Matches the key: 'n.pi+pi/2, n.pi+-pi/4'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q2(ii); book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: 2(1-cos^2)+3cos = 0: (2cosx+1)(cosx-2) = 0 - discard cosx = 2.
questions.question: AQ2(iii). Solve 2sin^2x + 3cosx = 0 (0 < x < 2pi).
questions.solution: 2cos^2x-3cosx-2 = (2cosx+1)(cosx-2) = 0. cosx = 2 impossible. cosx = -1/2: in (0, 2pi): x = 2pi/3, 4pi/3. Verified: x = 2pi/3 gives 2(3/4)+3(-1/2) = 0. (Key's '2pi/3, 4pi/3' fragments match.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q2(iii); book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); |cos|<=1 enforced

questions.knowledgeNote: cos^2+cos-3/4 = 0: cos = 1/2 or -3/2 - keep only 1/2.
questions.question: AQ2(iv). Solve sin^2theta - costheta = 1/4 (0 <= theta <= 2pi).
questions.solution: 1-cos^2-cos-1/4 = 0 gives cos^2+cos-3/4 = 0: costheta = 1/2 (other root -3/2 rejected). In [0, 2pi]: theta = pi/3, 5pi/3. Verified: sin^2(pi/3)-cos(pi/3) = 3/4-1/2 = 1/4.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q2(iv); book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); |cos|<=1 enforced

questions.knowledgeNote: Multiply by tantheta: 2tan^2+tan-1 = (2tan-1)(tan+1) = 0.
questions.question: Q2(v). Solve 2tantheta - cottheta = -1.
questions.solution: 2tan^2theta+tantheta-1 = (2tantheta-1)(tantheta+1) = 0 (tantheta != 0 throughout). tantheta = 1/2: theta = n.pi+alpha (alpha = tan^(-1)(1/2)). tantheta = -1: theta = n.pi-pi/4. Both verified. (Key's 'n.pi+alpha' fragment matches.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q2(v); book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); tantheta != 0 respected

questions.knowledgeNote: (tan+1)(tan-sqrt(3)) = 0: -pi/4 and +pi/3 families.
questions.question: AQ2(vi). Solve tan^2theta + (1-sqrt(3))tantheta - sqrt(3) = 0.
questions.solution: (tantheta+1)(tantheta-sqrt(3)) = 0. tantheta = -1: theta = n.pi-pi/4. tantheta = sqrt(3): theta = n.pi+pi/3. Verified: theta = pi/3 gives 3+(1-sqrt(3))sqrt(3)-sqrt(3) = 3+sqrt(3)-3-sqrt(3) = 0.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q2(vi); book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); verified by substitution

questions.knowledgeNote: sqrt(2)sin(theta+pi/4) = 1/sqrt(2): only 7pi/12 and 23pi/12 land inside [0, 2pi].
questions.question: AQ3(i). Solve sintheta + costheta = 1/sqrt(2) (0 <= theta <= 2pi).
questions.solution: sin(theta+pi/4) = 1/2: theta+pi/4 = pi/6, 5pi/6 (+2pi). In range: theta = 7pi/12 (from 5pi/6) and theta = 23pi/12 (from pi/6+2pi). theta = -pi/12 and 25pi/12 excluded. Verified: sin(7pi/12)+cos(7pi/12) = 0.707. (Key's '/12' fragments consistent.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q3(i); book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); interval filter applied, verified

questions.knowledgeNote: sqrt(2)cos(theta+pi/4) = 1/sqrt(2): four hits inside [-2pi, 2pi].
questions.question: AQ3(ii). Solve costheta - sintheta = 1/sqrt(2) (-2pi <= theta <= 2pi).
questions.solution: cos(theta+pi/4) = 1/2: theta = 2n.pi+pi/12 or 2n.pi-7pi/12. Inside [-2pi, 2pi]: -23pi/12, -7pi/12, pi/12, 17pi/12. Verified: theta = pi/12 gives 0.966-0.259 = 0.707.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q3(ii); book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); interval filter applied, verified

questions.knowledgeNote: (sin+1)/cos = sqrt(3): 2sin(theta-pi/3) = -1 - and 3pi/2 must be thrown out (tan/sec undefined).
questions.question: AQ3(iii). Solve tantheta + sectheta = sqrt(3) [T.U. 2050].
questions.solution: sin+1 = sqrt(3)cos gives 2sin(theta-pi/3) = -1: sin(theta-pi/3) = -1/2, theta = 2n.pi+pi/6 or 2n.pi+3pi/2. theta = 3pi/2 (mod 2pi) makes tan/sec undefined - rejected. So theta = 2n.pi+pi/6. Verified: tan(pi/6)+sec(pi/6) = 1/sqrt(3)+2/sqrt(3) = sqrt(3).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q3(iii) [T.U. 2050]; book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); undefined branch rejected

questions.knowledgeNote: (sqrt(2)+sin)/cos = 1: sin(theta-pi/4) = -1 - a single family.
questions.question: AQ3(iv). Solve sqrt(2)sectheta + tantheta = 1.
questions.solution: sqrt(2)+sintheta = costheta gives sin(theta-pi/4)... sin -cos = -sqrt(2): sqrt(2)sin(theta-pi/4) = -sqrt(2), sin(theta-pi/4) = -1: theta = 2n.pi-pi/4 (cos != 0 throughout). Verified: sqrt(2)(sqrt(2))+(-1) = 1. (Key's '2n.pi-pi/4' fragment matches.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q3(iv); book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); matches key, verified

questions.knowledgeNote: 2sin(theta+pi/3) = 1: four hits in the open interval (-2pi, 2pi).
questions.question: AQ3(v). Solve sqrt(3)costheta + sintheta = 1 (-2pi < theta < 2pi) [T.U. 2052].
questions.solution: sin(theta+pi/3) = 1/2: theta = n.pi+(-1)^n.pi/6-pi/3. Inside (-2pi, 2pi): -7pi/6, -pi/6, pi/2, 11pi/6 (endpoints -2pi, 2pi excluded as strict). Verified: theta = pi/2 gives 0+1 = 1; theta = -pi/6 gives 3/2-1/2 = 1.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q3(v) [T.U. 2052]; book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); interval filter applied, verified

questions.knowledgeNote: Amplitude sqrt(1+3) = 2 equals the RHS: sin(...) = 1 is the ONLY way - two hits in [-2pi, 2pi].
questions.question: AQ3(vi). Solve costheta + sqrt(3)sintheta = 2 (-2pi <= theta <= 2pi).
questions.solution: 2sin(theta+pi/6) = 2: sin(theta+pi/6) = 1, theta = 2n.pi+pi/3. In [-2pi, 2pi]: theta = -5pi/3, pi/3. Verified: theta = pi/3 gives 1/2+3/2 = 2; theta = -5pi/3 gives 1/2+3/2 = 2.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q3(vi); book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); maximum-attainment argument, verified

questions.knowledgeNote: sin = 1/2 meets cos = -sqrt(3)/2 in QII: x = 2n.pi+5pi/6.
questions.question: AQ4(i). Find the general x with sinx = 1/2 and cosx = -sqrt(3)/2.
questions.solution: sinx = 1/2 at pi/6, 5pi/6 (+2pi); cosx = -sqrt(3)/2 at 5pi/6, 7pi/6 (+2pi). Common: x = 2n.pi+5pi/6 (second quadrant, as required). (Key's '2n.pi+5pi/6' fragments match.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q4(i); book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); quadrant intersection

questions.knowledgeNote: sin = -1/sqrt(2) meets tan = 1 in QIII: x = 2n.pi+5pi/4.
questions.question: AQ4(ii). Find the general x with sinx = -1/sqrt(2) and tanx = 1.
questions.solution: sinx = -1/sqrt(2) at 5pi/4, 7pi/4 (+2pi); tanx = 1 at pi/4, 5pi/4 (+pi). Common: x = 2n.pi+5pi/4 (third quadrant). Verified: sin(5pi/4) = -1/sqrt(2), tan(5pi/4) = 1.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q4(ii); book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); quadrant intersection

questions.knowledgeNote: The book prints the full quadrant argument for this one: QIV gives 2n.pi+5pi/3.
questions.question: AQ4(iii). Find the general x with sinx = -sqrt(3)/2 and cosx = 1/2 (hint printed in the book).
questions.solution: Sine negative + cosine positive: fourth quadrant. x = 2pi-pi/3 = 5pi/3 satisfies both; with 2pi periodicity: x = 2n.pi+5pi/3. (Reproduces the book's printed hint, book p155.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q4(iii); book p155 = PDF p182 (hint printed in book)

questions.knowledgeNote: cosec = -2/sqrt(3) gives sin = -sqrt(3)/2 (QIII/QIV); tan = -sqrt(3) keeps only QIV: 5pi/3.
questions.question: AQ4(iv). Find the general x with cosecx = -2/sqrt(3) and tanx = -sqrt(3).
questions.solution: sinx = -sqrt(3)/2 at 4pi/3, 5pi/3 (+2pi); tanx = -sqrt(3) at 2pi/3, 5pi/3 (+pi). Common: x = 2n.pi+5pi/3 (fourth quadrant). Verified: cosec(5pi/3) = -2/sqrt(3), tan(5pi/3) = -sqrt(3).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q4(iv); book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); quadrant intersection

questions.knowledgeNote: Double-angle backwards: 2x^2-1 is cos2t in disguise; the principal range forces x >= 0.
questions.question: Q4(a). Prove that 2cos-1x = cos-1(2x^2-1).
questions.solution: Put t = cos-1x in [0, pi], so x = cost. Then 2x^2-1 = 2cos^2t-1 = cos2t. For 2t to be the principal value we need 2t in [0, pi], i.e. t in [0, pi/2], i.e. x >= 0; then cos-1(2x^2-1) = 2t = 2cos-1x. Proved (valid for 0 <= x <= 1; the book states it without the hypothesis).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(a); book pp167-168 = PDF pp194-195

questions.knowledgeNote: Triple-angle backwards: 4x^3-3x is cos3t; needs 3t inside [0, pi], i.e. x >= 1/2.
questions.question: Q4(b). Prove that 3cos-1x = cos-1(4x^3-3x).
questions.solution: Put t = cos-1x in [0, pi], so x = cost. Then 4x^3-3x = 4cos^3t-3cost = cos3t. For 3t to be the principal value we need 3t in [0, pi], i.e. t in [0, pi/3], i.e. x in [1/2, 1]; then cos-1(4x^3-3x) = 3t = 3cos-1x. Proved (valid for 1/2 <= x <= 1).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(b); book pp167-168 = PDF pp194-195

questions.knowledgeNote: tan3t expansion with tant = x; needs 3t inside (-pi/2, pi/2), i.e. |x| < 1/sqrt(3).
questions.question: Q4(c). Prove that 3tan-1x = tan-1((3x-x^3)/(1-3x^2)).
questions.solution: Put t = tan-1x in (-pi/2, pi/2), so x = tant. Then tan3t = (3tant-tan^3t)/(1-3tan^2t) = (3x-x^3)/(1-3x^2). For 3t to be the principal value we need 3t in (-pi/2, pi/2), i.e. |x| < 1/sqrt(3); then tan-1 of the fraction is 3t = 3tan-1x. Proved (valid for |x| < 1/sqrt(3)).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(c); book pp167-168 = PDF pp194-195

questions.knowledgeNote: Both sides equal sqrt(1-t^2): each cofunction lands on the non-negative branch.
questions.question: Q4(d). Prove that sin(arccos t) = cos(arcsin t).
questions.solution: arccos t lies in [0, pi] where sine is non-negative, so sin(arccos t) = +sqrt(1-t^2). arcsin t lies in [-pi/2, pi/2] where cosine is non-negative, so cos(arcsin t) = +sqrt(1-t^2). Both equal sqrt(1-t^2). Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(d); book pp167-168 = PDF pp194-195

questions.knowledgeNote: Direct cos2t with cost = t: no range subtlety since 2t^2-1 always lies in [-1, 1].
questions.question: Q4(e). Prove that cos(2arccost) = 2t^2-1.
questions.solution: Put u = arccost, so cosu = t. Then cos2u = 2cos^2u-1 = 2t^2-1. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(e); book pp167-168 = PDF pp194-195

questions.knowledgeNote: sin2t = 2sintcost with sint = x and cost = +sqrt(1-x^2) on the sin-1 range. (HSEB 2057)
questions.question: Q4(f). Prove that sin(2sin-1x) = 2x.sqrt(1-x^2). (HSEB 2057)
questions.solution: Put t = sin-1x in [-pi/2, pi/2], so sint = x and cost = +sqrt(1-x^2). Then sin2t = 2sintcost = 2x.sqrt(1-x^2). Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(f) (HSEB 2057); book pp167-168 = PDF pp194-195

questions.knowledgeNote: cos(A+B) = cosAcosB-sinAsinB with cosA = sqrt(1-u^2), sinB = sqrt(1-v^2): test u = v = 0 gives cos(pi/2) = 0. (T.U. 2049)
questions.question: Q4(g). Prove that cos(sin-1u+cos-1v) = v.sqrt(1-u^2)-u.sqrt(1-v^2). (T.U. 2049)
questions.solution: Put A = sin-1u (sinA = u, cosA = +sqrt(1-u^2)) and B = cos-1v (cosB = v, sinB = +sqrt(1-v^2)). Then cos(A+B) = cosAcosB-sinAsinB = v.sqrt(1-u^2)-u.sqrt(1-v^2). Check u = v = 0: LHS = cos(0+pi/2) = 0, RHS = 0. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(g) (T.U. 2049); book pp167-168 = PDF pp194-195

questions.knowledgeNote: Sum formula with positive denominator 1-1/35: the sum stays acute.
questions.question: Q4(h). Prove that tan-1(1/5)+tan-1(1/7) = tan-1(6/17).
questions.solution: (1/5+1/7)/(1-(1/5)(1/7)) = (12/35)/(34/35) = 12/34 = 6/17. Both angles are acute and their product 1/35 < 1, so the sum is the acute angle tan-1(6/17). Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(h); book pp167-168 = PDF pp194-195

questions.knowledgeNote: Telescoping in disguise: each RHS term is a difference of two tan-1, and the middle terms cancel.
questions.question: Q4(i). Prove that tan-1a-tan-1c = tan-1((a-b)/(1+ab))+tan-1((b-c)/(1+bc)).
questions.solution: Where defined (ab, bc > -1), tan-1((a-b)/(1+ab)) = tan-1a-tan-1b and tan-1((b-c)/(1+bc)) = tan-1b-tan-1c by the difference formula. Adding: the tan-1b terms cancel, leaving tan-1a-tan-1c. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(i); book pp167-168 = PDF pp194-195

questions.knowledgeNote: tan(A-B) with tanA = u, tanB = v: one line.
questions.question: Q4(j). Prove that tan(arctanu-arctanv) = (u-v)/(1+uv).
questions.solution: Put A = arctanu, B = arctanv, so tanA = u and tanB = v. Then tan(A-B) = (tanA-tanB)/(1+tanAtanB) = (u-v)/(1+uv). Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(j); book pp167-168 = PDF pp194-195 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: (x+x^3)/(1-x^4) simplifies by cancelling (1+x^2): the x^3 term is there to make this happen. (HSEB 2052)
questions.question: Q4(k). Prove that tan(2tan-1x) = 2tan(tan-1x+tan-1x^3). (HSEB 2052)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(k) (HSEB 2052); book pp167-168 = PDF pp194-195 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: tan(A+B+C) = (s1-xyz)/(1-s2): expand once, quote forever. (HSEB 2055)
questions.question: Q4(l). Prove that tan-1x+tan-1y+tan-1z = tan-1((x+y+z-xyz)/(1-xy-yz-zx)). (HSEB 2055)
questions.solution: Put A = tan-1x, B = tan-1y, C = tan-1z. Then tan(A+B+C) = (tanA+tanB+tanC-tanAtanBtanC)/(1-(tanAtanB+tanBtanC+tanCtanA)) = (x+y+z-xyz)/(1-xy-yz-zx). Taking tan-1 (principal branch where defined) gives the formula. Proved. (Statement via image read of the cut-off line.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(l) (HSEB 2055); book p167 = PDF p194 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: First two angles combine to cos-1(16/65); the third is its complement. (HSEB 2053)
questions.question: Q4(m). Prove that sin-1(4/5)+sin-1(5/13)+sin-1(16/65) = pi/2. (HSEB 2053)
questions.solution: sin of the first two summed: (4/5)(12/13)+(3/5)(5/13) = 48/65+15/65 = 63/65; cos: (3/5)(12/13)-(4/5)(5/13) = 36/65-20/65 = 16/65 > 0. So their sum is the acute angle with cosine 16/65, i.e. cos-1(16/65). Adding sin-1(16/65) gives pi/2. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(m) (HSEB 2053); book p167 = PDF p194 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Put sqrt(x) = tant: both fractions become cos2t and sin2t with 2t in [0, pi/2]. (T.U. 2055 S, HSEB 2054)
questions.question: Q4(n). Prove that tan-1(sqrt(x)) = (1/2)cos-1((1-x)/(1+x)) = (1/2)sin-1(2sqrt(x)/(1+x)). (T.U. 2055 S, HSEB 2054)
questions.solution: For 0 <= x < 1 put sqrt(x) = tant with t in [0, pi/4). Then (1-tan^2t)/(1+tan^2t) = cos2t with 2t in [0, pi/2), so cos-1 of it is 2t; and 2tant/(1+tan^2t) = sin2t, so sin-1 of it is 2t. Halving gives t = tan-1(sqrt(x)) in both cases. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(n) (T.U. 2055 S, HSEB 2054); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read)

questions.question: Q5(a). Find cos(sin-1(4/5)+tan-1(5/12)). (HSEB 2054, 2055)
questions.solution: sinA = 4/5 gives cosA = 3/5; tanB = 5/12 gives sinB = 5/13, cosB = 12/13. cos(A+B) = cosAcosB-sinAsinB = (3/5)(12/13)-(4/5)(5/13) = 36/65-20/65 = 16/65. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): 16/65.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q5(a) (HSEB 2054, 2055); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: sin(60deg+A) with sinA = 3/5, cosA = 4/5. (T.U. 2053 H)
questions.question: Q5(b). Find sin(cos-1(1/2)+sin-1(3/5)). (T.U. 2053 H)
questions.solution: cos-1(1/2) = 60deg; sinA = 3/5 gives cosA = 4/5. sin(60deg+A) = sin60cosA+cos60sinA = (sqrt(3)/2)(4/5)+(1/2)(3/5) = (4sqrt(3)+3)/10. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): (4sqrt(3)+3)/10.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q5(b) (T.U. 2053 H); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: tanA = 3/4, tanB = 12/5: the difference formula gives a negative over a positive.
questions.question: Q5(c). Find tan(arccos(4/5)-arcsin(12/13)).
questions.solution: cosA = 4/5 gives tanA = 3/4; sinB = 12/13 gives tanB = 12/5. tan(A-B) = (3/4-12/5)/(1+(3/4)(12/5)) = (-33/20)/(56/20) = -33/56. (This key row is illegible in the key scan; verified by substitution: arctan(-33/56) ~ -30.5deg and arccos(4/5)-arcsin(12/13) ~ 36.87-67.38 = -30.5deg.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q5(c); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); substitution-verified (key row illegible)

questions.knowledgeNote: Direct difference formula with second argument 2y. (HSEB 2053)
questions.question: Q5(d). Find tan(tan-1x-tan-12y). i.e. tan(tan-1x-tan-1(2y)). (HSEB 2053)
questions.solution: By the tan difference formula with arguments x and 2y: (x-2y)/(1+x.2y) = (x-2y)/(1+2xy). Matches the printed Answers key (p169): (x-2y)/(1+2xy).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q5(d) (HSEB 2053); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Product 3.(1/3) = 1: complementary acute angles sum to pi/2.
questions.question: Q5(e). Find tan-13+tan-1(1/3). i.e. tan-1(3)+tan-1(1/3).
questions.solution: Both angles are acute and their tangents multiply to 3.(1/3) = 1, so they are complementary: sum = pi/2 (tan-1(3) ~ 71.57deg, tan-1(1/3) ~ 18.43deg). (The key scan shows the value with the /2 cut off; the exact value is pi/2.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q5(e); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); exact value pi/2 (key scan cut off)

questions.knowledgeNote: arccos(-t) = pi-arccost: the pi survives while the rest collapses to pi/2.
questions.question: Q5(f). Find arcsint-arccos(-t). i.e. sin-1t-cos-1(-t).
questions.solution: arccos(-t) = pi-arccost. So sin-1t-cos-1(-t) = sin-1t+cos-1t-pi = pi/2-pi = -pi/2. (The key shows a negative value here; the exact value is -pi/2.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q5(f); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); exact value -pi/2

questions.knowledgeNote: Equal inverse values mean the 45-degree angle: both are pi/4, so x = sqrt(2)/2.
questions.question: Q6(a). Solve cos-1x-sin-1x = 0.
questions.solution: cos-1x = sin-1x =: t. Then x = cost = sint with t in [0, pi/2], so t = pi/4 and x = sqrt(2)/2 = 1/sqrt(2). Check: pi/4-pi/4 = 0. (The key scan reads 1/2 with the root sign lost; the exact value is 1/sqrt(2).)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q6(a); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); exact value 1/sqrt(2)

questions.knowledgeNote: Difference zero means the two complementary angles are equal: each pi/4.
questions.question: Q6(b). Solve tan-1x-cot-1x = 0.
questions.solution: tan-1x = cot-1x; since they sum to pi/2, each is pi/4, so x = tan(pi/4) = 1. Check: pi/4-pi/4 = 0. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): x = 1.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q6(b); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: One angle, two trig ratios: sin = x/2 and cos = x force x^2/4+x^2 = 1. (HSEB 2052)
questions.question: Q6(c). Solve sin-1(x/2) = cos-1x. (HSEB 2052)
questions.solution: Let the common value be t: sint = x/2 and cost = x. Then x^2/4+x^2 = 1, i.e. x^2 = 4/5, and x >= 0 (t in [0, pi/2] from the ranges), so x = 2/sqrt(5). Check: sin-1(1/sqrt(5)) = cos-1(2/sqrt(5)) ~ 26.57deg. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): x = 2/sqrt(5).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q6(c) (HSEB 2052); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Equal principal values with the same cosine: x = 1/(2x). (HSEB 2051)
questions.question: Q6(d). Solve cos-1x = cos-1(1/(2x)). (HSEB 2051)
questions.solution: Both sides are principal values in [0, pi], so x = 1/(2x), i.e. x^2 = 1/2, i.e. x = +-1/sqrt(2). Both satisfy |1/(2x)| = 1/sqrt(2) <= 1. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): x = +-1/sqrt(2).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q6(d) (HSEB 2051); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Take tan of both sides: 2x = 2x/(1-x^2) has only the trivial root.
questions.question: Q6(e). Solve tan-12x = 2tan-1x. i.e. tan-1(2x) = 2tan-1x.
questions.solution: Taking tan: 2x = 2x/(1-x^2). Either x = 0 or 1-x^2 = 1, which also gives x = 0. So x = 0 (check: 0 = 0). Matches the printed Answers key (p169): x = 0.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q6(e); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: cos-12x = sin-1x forces 2x = +sqrt(1-x^2): squaring admits a negative ghost.
questions.question: Q6(f). Solve cos-1x+cos-1(2x) = pi/2.
questions.solution: cos-1(2x) = pi/2-cos-1x = sin-1x. Taking cos: 2x = cos(sin-1x) = +sqrt(1-x^2), which needs x >= 0. Squaring: 4x^2 = 1-x^2, i.e. x^2 = 1/5, i.e. x = 1/sqrt(5) (x = -1/sqrt(5) gives LHS = 3pi/2, extraneous). Check x = 1/sqrt(5): sum is pi/2. The printed key lists +-1/sqrt(5); only +1/sqrt(5) satisfies the equation (flagged).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q6(f); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); exact x = 1/sqrt(5), negative root extraneous (key overlists)

questions.knowledgeNote: The complement of sin-1x is cos-1x itself: 1-x must equal x.
questions.question: Q6(g). Solve sin-1x+cos-1(1-x) = pi/2.
questions.solution: cos-1(1-x) = pi/2-sin-1x = cos-1x (since pi/2-sin-1x = cos-1x). Both sides principal values gives 1-x = x, i.e. x = 1/2. Check: pi/6+pi/3 = pi/2.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q6(g); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); substitution-verified

questions.knowledgeNote: Both exotic forms are double-angle masks: 2tan-1a minus 2tan-1b. (HSEB 2053)
questions.question: Q6(h). If sin-1(2a/(1+a^2))-cos-1((1-b^2)/(1+b^2)) = 2tan-1x, show that x = (a-b)/(1+ab). (HSEB 2053)
questions.solution: sin-1(2a/(1+a^2)) = 2tan-1a and cos-1((1-b^2)/(1+b^2)) = 2tan-1b. So 2tan-1a-2tan-1b = 2tan-1x, i.e. tan-1x = tan-1a-tan-1b = tan-1((a-b)/(1+ab)), giving x = (a-b)/(1+ab). Shown. (The key row is garbled but consistent with (h) x = (a-b)/(1+ab).)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q6(h) (HSEB 2053); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Sum formula: A+B and 1-AB turn out equal (both 6/7 at the roots), so the sum is genuinely pi/4.
questions.question: Q6(i). Solve tan-1((x-1)/(x-2))+tan-1((x+1)/(x+2)) = tan-1(1).
questions.solution: With A = (x-1)/(x-2), B = (x+1)/(x+2): A+B = (2x^2-4)/(x^2-4), 1-AB = -3/(x^2-4). A+B = 1-AB gives 2x^2-4 = -3, i.e. x^2 = 1/2, x = +-1/sqrt(2). At both roots A+B = 6/7 > 0 and 1-AB = 6/7 > 0, so the sum is genuinely pi/4. Both valid. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): x = +-1/sqrt(2).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q6(i); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: 5x = 1-6x^2 gives x = 1/6 and x = -1, but only 1/6 keeps A+B and 1-AB positive.
questions.question: Q6(j). Solve tan-12x+tan-13x = pi/4. i.e. tan-1(2x)+tan-1(3x) = pi/4.
questions.solution: (2x+3x)/(1-6x^2) = 1 gives 6x^2+5x-1 = 0, i.e. (6x-1)(x+1) = 0, so x = 1/6 or x = -1. x = 1/6: A+B = 5/6 > 0, 1-AB = 5/6 > 0, sum genuinely pi/4, valid. x = -1: LHS = -3pi/4, extraneous. True solution x = 1/6; the printed key lists both roots without the domain check (flagged).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q6(j); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); true x = 1/6, x = -1 extraneous (key overlists)

questions.knowledgeNote: 1/(2+sqrt(3)) = 2-sqrt(3) = tan15deg: triple it to land on 45deg.
questions.question: Q6(k). Solve 3tan-1(1/(2+sqrt(3)))-tan-1(1/x) = tan-1(1/3).
questions.solution: 1/(2+sqrt(3)) = 2-sqrt(3) = tan15deg, so 3tan-1(1/(2+sqrt(3))) = 3.15deg = 45deg = pi/4. Then tan-1(1/x) = pi/4-tan-1(1/3) = tan-1((1-1/3)/(1+1/3)) = tan-1(1/2), so 1/x = 1/2, i.e. x = 2. Check in the original: pi/4-tan-1(1/2) = tan-1(1/3) since (1-1/2)/(1+1/2) = 1/3. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): x = 2.

questions.knowledgeNote: tan of the sum is tan(pi) = 0: the numerator x+y+z-xyz must vanish. (T.U. 2050)
questions.question: Q7(a). If tan-1x+tan-1y+tan-1z = pi, prove that x+y+z = xyz. (T.U. 2050)
questions.solution: Take tan of both sides: tan(tan-1x+tan-1y+tan-1z) = tan(pi) = 0. The left side is (x+y+z-xyz)/(1-xy-yz-zx), so its numerator is 0 (denominator nonzero): x+y+z = xyz. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q7(a) (T.U. 2050); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: tan of pi/2 is undefined: the denominator 1-(xy+yz+zx) must vanish. (T.U. 2048, 2050)
questions.question: Q7(b). If tan-1x+tan-1y+tan-1z = pi/2, prove that xy+yz+zx = 1. (T.U. 2048, 2050)
questions.solution: tan of the sum is tan(pi/2), undefined, while the expansion is (x+y+z-xyz)/(1-xy-yz-zx). Hence the denominator is 0: 1-(xy+yz+zx) = 0, i.e. xy+yz+zx = 1. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q7(b) (T.U. 2048, 2050); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: cos(A+B) = -cosC, then one squaring: the cross term 2xyz appears. (T.U. 2056 S)
questions.question: Q8. If cos-1x+cos-1y+cos-1z = pi, show that x^2+y^2+z^2+2xyz = 1. (T.U. 2056 S)
questions.solution: Put A = cos-1x, B = cos-1y, C = cos-1z with A+B = pi-C. Then cos(A+B) = -cosC, i.e. xy-sqrt((1-x^2)(1-y^2)) = -z, i.e. xy+z = +sqrt((1-x^2)(1-y^2)) (non-negative here). Squaring: x^2y^2+2xyz+z^2 = 1-x^2-y^2+x^2y^2, i.e. x^2+y^2+z^2+2xyz = 1. Shown.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q8 (T.U. 2056 S); book pp168-169 = PDF pp195-196 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: tanA = 3/5 with tanB = 3/4: (27/20)/(11/20) = 27/11, and the sum stays under 90deg.
questions.question: Q9(i). Prove that tan-1(3/5)+sin-1(3/5) = tan-1(27/11).
questions.solution: tanA = 3/5 for A = tan-1(3/5); sinB = 3/5 gives cosB = 4/5 and tanB = 3/4 for B = sin-1(3/5). tan(A+B) = (3/5+3/4)/(1-(3/5)(3/4)) = (27/20)/(11/20) = 27/11. A ~ 30.96deg and B ~ 36.87deg are acute with sum ~ 67.8deg < 90deg, so A+B = tan-1(27/11). Proved. (Confirmed against an independent NEB-video statement of the same question.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q9(i); book p169 = PDF p196 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: cot-13 = tan-1(1/3) and cosec-1(sqrt(5)) = tan-1(1/2): sum to tan-1(1) = pi/4, times 4. (HSEB 2058)
questions.question: Q9(iv). Prove that 4(cot-13+cosec-1(sqrt(5))) = pi. (HSEB 2058)
questions.solution: cot-13 = tan-1(1/3). cosec-1(sqrt(5)) = sin-1(1/sqrt(5)); with sin = 1/sqrt(5), tan = (1/sqrt(5))/(2/sqrt(5)) = 1/2, so it equals tan-1(1/2). Sum: tan-1(1/3)+tan-1(1/2) = tan-1((5/6)/(5/6)) = tan-1(1) = pi/4. Times 4: pi. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q9(iv) (HSEB 2058); book p169 = PDF p196 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: tan-12+tan-13 = 3pi/4 (ratio -1 with sum past pi/2); the half-weight inner sum is pi/2. (T.U. 2051, 54)
questions.question: Q9(v). Prove that tan-11+tan-12+tan-13 = pi = 2(tan-11+tan-1(1/2)+tan-1(1/3)). (T.U. 2051, 54)
questions.solution: tan-12+tan-13: (2+3)/(1-6) = -1 with both acute and sum in (pi/2, pi), so 3pi/4; plus tan-11 = pi/4 gives pi. Inner: tan-1(1/2)+tan-1(1/3) = tan-1((5/6)/(5/6)) = tan-1(1) = pi/4; plus tan-11 = pi/2; doubled = pi. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q9(v) (T.U. 2051, 54); book p169 = PDF p196 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: One parameter t = sin^2 of the first form: cos and tan drop out of 1-t. (T.U. 2057 S)
questions.question: Q10(i). Prove that sin-1(sqrt((x-b)/(a-b))) = cos-1(sqrt((a-x)/(a-b))) = tan-1(sqrt((x-b)/(a-x))). (T.U. 2057 S)
questions.solution: For b <= x <= a put t = sin-1(sqrt((x-b)/(a-b))) =: u. Then cosu = +sqrt(1-(x-b)/(a-b)) = sqrt((a-x)/(a-b)), so u = cos-1(sqrt((a-x)/(a-b))); and tanu = sinu/cosu = sqrt((x-b)/(a-x)), so u = tan-1(sqrt((x-b)/(a-x))). All three equal u. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q10(i) (T.U. 2057 S); book p169 = PDF p196 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Half-angle in sin^2/cos^2 form with t = cos-1x.
questions.question: Q10(ii). Prove that cos-1x = 2sin-1(sqrt((1-x)/2)) = 2cos-1(sqrt((1+x)/2)).
questions.solution: Put t = cos-1x, so x = cost. Then sqrt((1-x)/2) = sqrt((1-cost)/2) = sin(t/2) (t/2 in [0, pi/2], non-negative), so 2sin-1 of it is t. Likewise sqrt((1+x)/2) = cos(t/2), so 2cos-1 of it is t. Both equal cos-1x. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q10(ii); book p169 = PDF p196 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: sin2A+sin2B+sin2C = 4sinAsinBsinC (proved in Ch.4 Ex 4.1 Q12(b)): halve it. (T.U. 2052)
questions.question: Q11. If sin-1x+sin-1y+sin-1z = pi, prove that x.sqrt(1-x^2)+y.sqrt(1-y^2)+z.sqrt(1-z^2) = 2xyz. (T.U. 2052)
questions.solution: Put A = sin-1x, B = sin-1y, C = sin-1z with A+B+C = pi. Then sin2A+sin2B+sin2C = 4sinAsinBsinC (Ch.4 Ex 4.1 Q12(b)), i.e. 2(x.sqrt(1-x^2)+y.sqrt(1-y^2)+z.sqrt(1-z^2)) = 4xyz since sinA = x and cosA = +sqrt(1-x^2) on the sin-1 range. Halving gives the result. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q11 (T.U. 2052); book p169 = PDF p196 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: sinC = cos(A+B): move xy over, then square once.
questions.question: Q12. If sin-1x+sin-1y+sin-1z = pi/2, prove that x^2+y^2+z^2+2xyz = 1.
questions.solution: Put A = sin-1x, B = sin-1y, C = sin-1z with C = pi/2-(A+B). Then sinC = cos(A+B), i.e. z = sqrt((1-x^2)(1-y^2))-xy, i.e. z+xy = +sqrt((1-x^2)(1-y^2)) (non-negative). Squaring: z^2+2xyz+x^2y^2 = 1-x^2-y^2+x^2y^2, i.e. x^2+y^2+z^2+2xyz = 1. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q12; book p169 = PDF p196 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: tan-1 eats every real number: domain (-inf, inf). (HSEB 2050)
questions.question: AQ1(i). What is the domain of the inverse function tan-1x? (HSEB 2050)
questions.solution: tan maps (-pi/2, pi/2) onto all real numbers, so its inverse tan-1x is defined for every real x: domain (-inf, inf). (The printed Answers, p171, confirm: x in (-inf, inf).)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Additional Q1(i) (HSEB 2050); book p170 = PDF p197 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: cos = 1/3 forces sin = 2sqrt(2)/3: the 1-2sqrt(2)-3 triangle. (HSEB 2050)
questions.question: AQ1(ii). Find sin(cos-1(1/3)). (HSEB 2050)
questions.solution: Let t = cos-1(1/3) in [0, pi] with cost = 1/3 and sint >= 0. Then sint = sqrt(1-1/9) = sqrt(8/9) = 2sqrt(2)/3. (The printed Answers, p171, confirm: 2sqrt(2)/3.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Additional Q1(ii) (HSEB 2050); book p170 = PDF p197 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: tan of sin-1x is opposite-over-adjacent: x over sqrt(1-x^2). (HSEB 2050)
questions.question: AQ1(iii). Prove that sin-1x = tan-1(x/sqrt(1-x^2)). (HSEB 2050)
questions.solution: Put t = sin-1x in [-pi/2, pi/2] with x in (-1, 1), so sint = x and cost = +sqrt(1-x^2) != 0. Then tant = sint/cost = x/sqrt(1-x^2) with t in (-pi/2, pi/2), so t = tan-1(x/sqrt(1-x^2)). Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Additional Q1(iii) (HSEB 2050); book p170 = PDF p197 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Restrict sin to [-pi/2, pi/2], cos to [0, pi], tan to (-pi/2, pi/2): one y per x.
questions.question: AQ2. Explain what the inverse circular function is. What are the domains and ranges of sin-1x, cos-1x and tan-1x so that they are functions of x?
questions.solution: y = sinx (and cosx, tanx) is many-to-one, so its x-y swap is not a function. Restricting to one monotone branch gives a function: sin-1x has domain [-1, 1], range [-pi/2, pi/2]; cos-1x has domain [-1, 1], range [0, pi]; tan-1x has domain (-inf, inf), range (-pi/2, pi/2). (The printed Answers, p171, confirm all three domain-range lines.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Additional Q2; book p170 = PDF p197 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Both sides telescope to zero: each sum is three differences that cancel.
questions.question: AQ3. Prove that tan-1((a-b)/(1+ab))+tan-1((b-c)/(1+bc))+tan-1((c-a)/(1+ca)) = tan-1((a^2-b^2)/(1+a^2b^2))+tan-1((b^2-c^2)/(1+b^2c^2))+tan-1((c^2-a^2)/(1+c^2a^2)).
questions.solution: LHS = (tan-1a-tan-1b)+(tan-1b-tan-1c)+(tan-1c-tan-1a) = 0 and RHS = (tan-1a^2-tan-1b^2)+(tan-1b^2-tan-1c^2)+(tan-1c^2-tan-1a^2) = 0 by the difference formula (where all pairwise products exceed -1). Both sides are 0. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Additional Q3; book p170 = PDF p197 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: PRINT ERROR with counterexample: a = 3, b = 2, c = 1 gives pi, not 0. The correct identity equals pi.
questions.question: AQ4(i). [Print says = 0: DISPROVED.] cot-1((ab+1)/(a-b))+cot-1((bc+1)/(b-c))+cot-1((ca+1)/(c-a)) = 0.
questions.solution: Counterexample a = 3, b = 2, c = 1: arccot(7/1)+arccot(3/1)+arccot(4/(-2)) = arccot7+arccot3+arccot(-2) ~ 8.13deg+18.43deg+153.43deg = 180deg = pi, not 0. So the printed = 0 is false. Correct identity: for a > b > c with ab, bc, ca > -1 the sum is pi, since cot-1(1/t) = tan-1t for t > 0 and = pi+tan-1t for t < 0, and tan-1((a-b)/(1+ab))+tan-1((b-c)/(1+bc))+tan-1((c-a)/(1+ca)) telescopes to 0. Filed as a print error with correction.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Additional Q4(i); book p170 = PDF p197 (image read); disproved by counterexample, corrected to pi

questions.knowledgeNote: Each cot-1 is pi/2 minus a tan-1; the three tan-1 sum to pi by Q9(v).
questions.question: AQ4(ii). Prove that cot-11+cot-12+cot-13 = pi/2.
questions.solution: cot-1x = pi/2-tan-1x for every nonzero x. So the sum is 3pi/2-(tan-11+tan-12+tan-13) = 3pi/2-pi = pi/2, using Q9(v) (tan-11+tan-12+tan-13 = pi). Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Additional Q4(ii); book p170 = PDF p197 (image read)

questions.question: AQ4(iii). Prove that sec^2(tan-12)+cosec^2(cot-13) = 15.
questions.solution: sec^2(tan-12) = 1+tan^2(tan-12) = 1+4 = 5. With p = cot-13, cotp = 3, so cosec^2p = 1+cot^2p = 1+9 = 10. Total 5+10 = 15. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Additional Q4(iii); book p170 = PDF p197 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Both halves are double-angle masks: (1/2)sin-1(2x/(1+x^2)) = tan-1x and (1/2)cos-1((1-y^2)/(1+y^2)) = tan-1y.
questions.question: AQ4(iv). Prove that tan((1/2)sin-1(2x/(1+x^2))+(1/2)cos-1((1-y^2)/(1+y^2))) = (x+y)/(1-xy).
questions.solution: sin-1(2x/(1+x^2)) = 2tan-1x and cos-1((1-y^2)/(1+y^2)) = 2tan-1y (the standard t-substitution masks). Halving gives tan-1x+tan-1y, and tan of that sum is (x+y)/(1-xy). Proved.

questions.knowledgeNote: sin = 1 only at the top of the principal arc: pi/2.
questions.question: Q1(a). Evaluate sin-1(1) without using tables.
questions.solution: sin-1(1) is the angle t in [-pi/2, pi/2] with sint = 1, i.e. t = pi/2.

questions.solution: arctan(-1/sqrt(3)) is t in (-pi/2, pi/2) with tant = -1/sqrt(3), i.e. t = -pi/6. (The sqrt(3) confirmed by a V3 glyph read in the 600-dpi crop.)

questions.knowledgeNote: Draw the right triangle with opposite x, adjacent 1: hypotenuse sqrt(1+x^2).
questions.question: Q2(a). Express cos(tan-1x) in terms of x.
questions.solution: Put t = tan-1x, so t is in (-pi/2, pi/2) and tant = x. Then cost = 1/sqrt(1+tan^2t) = 1/sqrt(1+x^2), positive since cost > 0 on (-pi/2, pi/2). Matches the printed Answers key (p169): 1/sqrt(1+x^2).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q2(a); book p167 = PDF p194 (OCR conf 0.96); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Same triangle read from the cot side: adjacent x, opposite 1.
questions.question: Q2(b). Express sin(cot-1x) in terms of x.
questions.solution: Put p = cot-1x, so p is in (0, pi) and cotp = x. Then sinp = 1/sqrt(1+cot^2p) = 1/sqrt(1+x^2), positive since sinp > 0 on (0, pi). Matches the printed Answers key (p169): 1/sqrt(1+x^2).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q2(b); book p167 = PDF p194 (OCR conf 0.90); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: tan and arccot are reciprocal functions: tan(arccot x) = 1/x.
questions.question: Q2(c). Express tan(arccot x) in terms of x.
questions.solution: Put p = arccot x, so cotp = x with x != 0. Then tanp = 1/cotp = 1/x. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): 1/x (x != 0).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q2(c); book p167 = PDF p194 (OCR conf 0.94); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: cos is non-negative on the whole sin-1 range, so no sign choice.
questions.question: Q2(d). Express cos(sin-1x) in terms of x.
questions.solution: Put t = sin-1x, so t is in [-pi/2, pi/2] and sint = x. Then cost = +sqrt(1-sin^2t) = sqrt(1-x^2), taking the non-negative root since cost >= 0 there. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): sqrt(1-x^2).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q2(d); book p167 = PDF p194 (OCR conf 0.97); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Double-angle in tan form: tan2t = 2tant/(1-tan^2t) with tant = x.
questions.question: Q2(e). Express tan(2tan-1x) in terms of x.
questions.solution: Put t = tan-1x so tant = x. Then tan2t = 2tant/(1-tan^2t) = 2x/(1-x^2), valid for x != +-1. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): 2x/(1-x^2).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q2(e); book p167 = PDF p194 (OCR conf 0.96); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: sin2t via tan: 2tant/(1+tan^2t) - denominator never zero.
questions.question: Q2(f). Express sin(2tan-1x) in terms of x.
questions.solution: Put t = tan-1x so tant = x. Then sin2t = 2tant/(1+tan^2t) = 2x/(1+x^2). Matches the printed Answers key (p169): 2x/(1+x^2).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q2(f); book p167 = PDF p194 (OCR conf 0.93); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: cos2p from cot: (cot^2p-1)/(cot^2p+1) - test x = 1 gives cos(pi/2) = 0.
questions.question: Q2(g). Express cos(2cot-1x) in terms of x.
questions.solution: Put p = cot-1x so cotp = x. Then cos2p = (cot^2p-1)/(cot^2p+1) = (x^2-1)/(x^2+1). Check x = 1: cos(2.pi/4) = cos(pi/2) = 0 and (1-1)/(1+1) = 0. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): (x^2-1)/(x^2+1).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q2(g); book p167 = PDF p194 (OCR conf 0.95); matches key

questions.question: Q2(h). Express cot(2arccot x) in terms of x.
questions.solution: Put p = arccot x so cotp = x with x != 0. Then cot2p = (cot^2p-1)/(2cotp) = (x^2-1)/(2x). Check x = 1: cot(2.pi/4) = 0 and (1-1)/2 = 0. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): (x^2-1)/(2x).
